drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using If only: We regret that we did not study harder.
drills.target: If only we had studied harder.

acceptedAnswers: If only he were here now.
drills.explanation: This is a present unreal wish. If only is followed by a past form to show a situation that is not true now.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using If only: He is not here now, and we want that to be different.
drills.target: If only he were here now.

acceptedAnswers: I wish I had not said that.
drills.explanation: Use past perfect after wish to show regret about something that already happened.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: I wish I did not say that.
drills.target: I wish I had not said that.

acceptedAnswers: She wishes she could speak English more fluently.
drills.explanation: Could is used after wish for an unreal present ability. Can is not correct here.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: She wishes she can speak English more fluently.
drills.target: She wishes she could speak English more fluently.

acceptedAnswers: I wish it would stop raining.
drills.explanation: Wish + would is used for a present situation you want to change, often for things you cannot control.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence about your frustration that the rain is continuing. Use wish and would.
drills.target: I wish it would stop raining.

acceptedAnswers: If only I knew the answer.
choices: If only I know the answer.
If only I knew the answer.
If only I had knew the answer.
drills.explanation: For a present unreal wish, if only takes a past form. The other options are ungrammatical.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: If only I knew the answer.

acceptedAnswers: I wish I had taken the earlier train.
choices: I wish I took the earlier train.
I wish I had taken the earlier train.
I wish I have taken the earlier train.
drills.explanation: This is regret about a past choice, so wish + past perfect is correct.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I wish I had taken the earlier train.

acceptedAnswers: If only she had listened to me.
choices: If only she listened to me.
If only she had listened to me.
If only she has listened to me.
drills.explanation: The wish refers to a past event, so the past perfect form is needed after if only.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: If only she had listened to me.

acceptedAnswers: were
drills.explanation: In formal English, were is common after wish or if only for unreal present situations, even with I, he, she, and it.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I wish it ___ easier to learn grammar.
drills.target: were

explanation: Wish and if only are used for regrets and unreal desires. The tense after them usually shifts back: use past simple for an unreal present situation, past perfect for regret about the past, and would/could for wishes about change or ability. In formal English, were is often used after wish/if only for all subjects in unreal present situations.
explanationVi: ‘Wish’ và ‘if only’ dùng để diễn tả sự tiếc nuối hoặc mong muốn trái với thực tế. Điểm khó là thì sau chúng thường “lùi về quá khứ”: nếu muốn nói một tình huống hiện tại không đúng, ta thường dùng quá khứ đơn (I wish I had more time); nếu muốn tiếc một việc đã xảy ra trong quá khứ, ta dùng quá khứ hoàn thành (I wish I had not missed the bus). Khi muốn thay đổi một tình huống hiện tại ngoài tầm kiểm soát, tiếng Anh thường dùng would (I wish it would stop raining). Với khả năng hoặc năng lực, dùng could (She wishes she could speak English more fluently). Trong văn phạm chuẩn, sau wish/if only, ‘were’ thường được dùng trong tình huống không có thật ở hiện tại, kể cả với I/he/she/it.
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường bị ảnh hưởng bởi cách nghĩ trực tiếp sang tiếng Anh nên dễ dùng thì hiện tại sau wish/if only. Trong tiếng Việt, ý tiếc nuối có thể nói rất tự nhiên bằng ‘giá mà’, ‘ước gì’ mà không đổi thì rõ ràng như tiếng Anh, nên dễ quên bước “lùi thì”.

title: Conditional Inversion
summary: Formal conditionals without if, as in Had I known.

commonMistakes.right: Had I known about the meeting, I would have gone earlier.
commonMistakes.why: In formal conditional inversion, the past perfect comes before the subject: Had + subject + past participle. Using if is also correct, but the inverted form is common in formal writing.
commonMistakes.wrong: Had I knew about the meeting, I would have gone earlier.

commonMistakes.right: Were she my manager, I would tell her the truth.
commonMistakes.why: After were in an inverted unreal present conditional, use the base form of be, not was. This pattern is formal and means the same as If she were my manager.
commonMistakes.wrong: Were she my manager, I would tell her the truth.

commonMistakes.right: Should you need any help, please call me.
commonMistakes.why: Should can start a formal conditional meaning 'If you should need'. The structure is should + subject + base verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: Should you needed any help, please call me.

commonMistakes.right: Had I known the answer, I would have raised my hand.
commonMistakes.why: In an inverted conditional, the auxiliary comes before the subject, and the verb form must match the time meaning. Had I known means a past unreal condition.
commonMistakes.wrong: I had known the answer, I would have raised my hand.

acceptedAnswers: Had I known the answer, I would have raised my hand.
choices: Had I knew the answer, I would have raised my hand.
Had I known the answer, I would have raised my hand.
If had I known the answer, I would have raised my hand.
drills.explanation: In past unreal conditionals, inversion uses Had + subject + past participle. The full form is equivalent to If I had known.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Had I known the answer, I would have raised my hand.

acceptedAnswers: Were she here, she would help us.
drills.explanation: Were + subject is used for formal unreal present conditionals. It means If she were here.
drills.prompt: Write a formal inverted conditional sentence meaning: If she were here, she would help us.
drills.target: Were she here, she would help us.

acceptedAnswers: Should you need any assistance, call this number.
drills.explanation: Should + subject + base verb is a formal way to express a possible future condition. It means If you should need any assistance.
drills.prompt: Rewrite formally without if: If you should need any assistance, call this number.
drills.target: Should you need any assistance, call this number.

acceptedAnswers: Had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
drills.explanation: This is the past unreal inverted pattern: Had I known. It is used for a condition that did not happen in the past.
drills.prompt: Rewrite without if: If I had known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
drills.target: Had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.

acceptedAnswers: Were they to offer me the job, I would accept it.
choices: If they were to offer me the job, I would accept it.
Were they to offer me the job, I would accept it.
Were they to offered me the job, I would accept it.
drills.explanation: Were they to offer is a formal conditional for a hypothetical future situation. It is the inverted equivalent of If they were to offer.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct formal conditional sentence.
drills.target: Were they to offer me the job, I would accept it.

acceptedAnswers: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
drills.explanation: This is the non-inverted version of the same meaning. It shows the normal if-clause that the inverted form can replace.
drills.prompt: Rewrite with if: Had she studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
drills.target: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.

acceptedAnswers: Should the weather improve, we will go hiking.
drills.explanation: Should the weather improve means If the weather should improve. This structure is formal and often used in written English.
drills.prompt: Write a formal inverted conditional sentence meaning: If the weather improves, we will go hiking.
drills.target: Should the weather improve, we will go hiking.

acceptedAnswers: Were he to apologize, I would forgive him.
choices: If he were to apologize, I would forgive him.
Were he to apologize, I would forgive him.
Were he to apologizes, I would forgive him.
drills.explanation: Were he to apologize is the inverted form of a hypothetical future condition. The verb after to must be the base form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Were he to apologize, I would forgive him.

acceptedAnswers: Had the train been on time, we would not have missed the interview.
drills.explanation: Had the train been on time is an inverted past unreal condition. It is equivalent to If the train had been on time.
drills.prompt: Write a formal inverted conditional sentence meaning: If the train had been on time, we would not have missed the interview.
drills.target: Had the train been on time, we would not have missed the interview.

explanation: Conditional inversion is a formal way to express unreal or hypothetical conditions without using if. Common patterns are Had I known..., Were she here..., and Should you need..., and they are usually used in written English, speeches, or formal speech. In these structures, the auxiliary or modal comes before the subject, and the verb form must match the time meaning: Had + subject + past participle for past unreal conditions; Were + subject for unreal present conditions; and Should + subject + base verb for a possible future condition. These forms are not used in ordinary statements, only in conditional meaning.
explanationVi: Đảo ngữ trong câu điều kiện là cách nói trang trọng để diễn tả điều kiện giả định mà không dùng if. Ba mẫu rất quan trọng là: Had I known... = Nếu tôi đã biết...; Were she here... = Nếu cô ấy ở đây...; Should you need... = Nếu bạn cần... Cấu trúc này thường gặp trong văn viết, bài thi học thuật, bài phát biểu trang trọng, và nghe tự nhiên hơn trong ngữ cảnh formal. Lưu ý trật tự từ: trợ động từ hoặc động từ khuyết thiếu đứng trước chủ ngữ. Sau Had phải là quá khứ phân từ; sau Were thường dùng động từ nguyên mẫu của be trong nghĩa giả định; sau Should phải dùng động từ nguyên mẫu. Người học Việt Nam hay quên đảo trợ động từ lên trước chủ ngữ hoặc dùng sai dạng động từ sau Had/Were/Should.
formPatterns: Had + subject + past participle, ... would have + past participle
Were + subject + adjective/noun/prepositional phrase, ... would + base verb
Should + subject + base verb, ... will/would + base verb
Were + subject + to + base verb, ... would + base verb
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt không có đảo ngữ điều kiện tương đương với Had I known / Were she here / Should you need, nên người học thường giữ trật tự S-V bình thường và dịch từng từ. Cần chú ý rằng trong tiếng Anh trang trọng, trợ động từ đứng trước chủ ngữ, không có if, và không dùng was sau Were trong mẫu giả định.

title: Present Simple Passive
summary: Shifting focus to the object, where Vietnamese uses bi or duoc differently.

commonMistakes.right: The letters are posted every morning.
commonMistakes.why: Present Simple Passive uses am/is/are + past participle to show a regular action done to the object.
commonMistakes.wrong: The letters posted every morning.

commonMistakes.right: Rice is eaten with chopsticks in some countries.
commonMistakes.why: The verb needs the passive form is + past participle; the bare past participle alone is incorrect.
commonMistakes.wrong: Rice eaten with chopsticks in some countries.

commonMistakes.right: The report is written by a team.
commonMistakes.why: In the passive, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject, and the verb changes to am/is/are + past participle.
commonMistakes.wrong: The report writes by a team.

commonMistakes.right: English is spoken in many countries.
commonMistakes.why: Use is/are + past participle for a general fact in the present. The base verb after the subject is wrong here.
commonMistakes.wrong: English speaks in many countries.

acceptedAnswers: The windows are cleaned every week.
choices: The windows clean every week.
The windows are cleaned every week.
The windows is cleaned every week.
drills.explanation: The present simple passive for a plural subject uses are + past participle.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The windows are cleaned every week.

acceptedAnswers: The room is cleaned every day.
drills.explanation: This sentence needs the present simple passive: is cleaned.
drills.prompt: Build a sentence: the room / clean / every day
drills.target: The room is cleaned every day.

acceptedAnswers: is made
drills.explanation: With he/she/it, the present simple passive uses is + past participle.
drills.prompt: The soup ___ in the kitchen every morning.

acceptedAnswers: English is spoken in many countries.
drills.explanation: This is a general present fact, so the passive form is used to focus on the language, not the speaker.

acceptedAnswers: The books are returned on Fridays.
choices: The books are return on Fridays.

The books is returned on Fridays.
drills.explanation: Plural subject needs are, and the main verb must be in past participle form: returned.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The books are returned on Fridays.

acceptedAnswers: are sold
drills.explanation: With a plural subject, the passive verb is are sold.
drills.prompt: The tickets ___ at the station.
drills.target: are sold

acceptedAnswers: The house is painted every summer.
drills.explanation: Use is + past participle when the subject is singular.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The house paint every summer.
drills.target: The house is painted every summer.

acceptedAnswers: The letters are sent by courier.
choices: The letters is sent by courier.
The letters are sent by courier.
The letters sent by courier.
drills.explanation: The subject is plural, so the correct auxiliary is are.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The letters are sent by courier.

acceptedAnswers: is produced
drills.explanation: The passive pattern is is + past participle.
drills.prompt: Tea ___ in this factory.
drills.target: is produced

acceptedAnswers: The meal is served at 7 p.m.
drills.explanation: The sentence needs a passive verb to show what happens to the meal, not who does it.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in the present simple passive: They serve the meal at 7 p.m.
drills.target: The meal is served at 7 p.m.

acceptedAnswers: The emails are checked by the manager.
drills.explanation: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject in the passive.
drills.prompt: Build a sentence: the emails / check / by the manager
drills.target: The emails are checked by the manager.

acceptedAnswers: is kept
drills.explanation: For a singular subject, the passive form is is kept.
drills.prompt: The key ___ in a drawer.
drills.target: is kept

acceptedAnswers: The classrooms are cleaned after school.
choices: The classrooms cleans after school.
The classrooms are cleaned after school.
The classrooms is cleaned after school.
drills.explanation: The passive verb must be are cleaned, because classrooms is plural.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The classrooms are cleaned after school.

acceptedAnswers: Rice is grown in this region.
drills.explanation: This is a general fact, so the present simple passive is appropriate.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in the present simple passive: People grow rice in this region.
drills.target: Rice is grown in this region.

explanation: The present simple passive is used when we want to focus on the action receiver, not the doer. The form is am/is/are + past participle. Use is with singular subjects and are with plural subjects. It often describes routines, general facts, and regular processes: The windows are cleaned every day; English is spoken in many countries. If you want to mention the agent, use by: The letters are sent by courier. In Vietnamese, learners often translate directly from active sentences or overuse bi/được without changing the English verb form, so remember that English still needs be + past participle.
explanationVi: Thì hiện tại đơn bị động dùng khi ta muốn nhấn mạnh đối tượng chịu tác động của hành động, không nhấn mạnh người làm. Công thức là am/is/are + past participle (quá khứ phân từ). Với chủ ngữ số ít dùng is, với chủ ngữ số nhiều dùng are. Thì này thường dùng cho thói quen, sự thật chung, quy trình hoặc lịch trình thường xuyên: The windows are cleaned every day; English is spoken in many countries. Nếu muốn nói người thực hiện hành động thì dùng by: The letters are sent by courier. Người Việt hay bị ảnh hưởng bởi cách dùng bị/được trong tiếng Việt nên dễ quên đổi động từ sang dạng bị động trong tiếng Anh. Dù tiếng Việt có thể chỉ cần thêm “bị/được”, tiếng Anh vẫn phải có be + V3/ed.
formPatterns: subject + am/is/are + past participle (+ by + agent)
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường diễn đạt bị động bằng “bị” hoặc “được”, nên người học dễ giữ nguyên động từ chủ động trong tiếng Anh. Cần nhớ đổi sang be + V3/ed và chia be đúng với số ít/số nhiều.

title: Past Simple Passive
summary: Past events described from the object's viewpoint.

commonMistakes.right: The house was built in 1998.
commonMistakes.why: Use was/were + past participle to describe a finished action in the past from the object's point of view.
commonMistakes.wrong: The house built in 1998.

commonMistakes.right: My phone was stolen last night.
commonMistakes.why: The passive needs the auxiliary was or were in the past simple. The past participle alone is not enough.
commonMistakes.wrong: My phone stolen last night.

commonMistakes.right: The letters were sent yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: With a plural subject, use were, not was.
commonMistakes.wrong: The letters was sent yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: The room was cleaned by the students.
commonMistakes.why: In the passive, the action happens to the subject. Use by to name the agent if you want to mention who did it.
commonMistakes.wrong: The room cleaned the students.

acceptedAnswers: was repaired
drills.explanation: Use was + past participle for a singular subject in the past passive.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The car ___ yesterday.
drills.target: was repaired

acceptedAnswers: were taken
drills.explanation: Use were + past participle for a plural subject in the past passive.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The photos ___ last week.
drills.target: were taken

acceptedAnswers: The cake was eaten.
choices: The cake ate.
The cake was eaten.
The cake is eaten.
drills.explanation: The correct past passive form is was + past participle.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The cake was eaten.

acceptedAnswers: The windows were broken.
choices: The windows was broken.
The windows were broke.
The windows were broken.
drills.explanation: A plural subject needs were, and the verb needs the past participle broken.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The windows were broken.

drills.target: The letter was posted by Anna.

drills.explanation: Start with the object, then use were + past participle to describe the past action.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the past passive: We bought the shoes yesterday.

acceptedAnswers: The shop was closed at 9 p.m.

acceptedAnswers: The message was sent this morning.

drills.explanation: The passive form is were + past participle. By the manager shows who did the action.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The documents was signed by the manager.

acceptedAnswers: The bridge was built in 1980.
choices: The bridge was build in 1980.
The bridge was built in 1980.

drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The bridge was built in 1980.

acceptedAnswers: The emails were checked before the meeting.
drills.explanation: This is the passive of a past action. The subject is the thing affected, not the person doing it.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the past passive: They checked the emails before the meeting.
drills.target: The emails were checked before the meeting.

explanation:
Past Simple Passive is used when we want to talk about a finished action in the past and focus on the thing that received the action, not the person who did it. The form is was/were + past participle: was for singular subjects, were for plural subjects. If you want to say who did the action, add by + person. For example: The house was built in 1998. The letters were sent yesterday. The room was cleaned by the students.

Remember that the past participle is not the same as the past simple form of the verb. For regular verbs, the participle often ends in -ed, but many verbs are irregular: built, sent, broken, taken, written. In the passive, the subject does not do the action. It receives the action.

Use past simple passive for completed past events, especially when the doer is unknown, unimportant, or obvious. Do not use a passive form without was/were. Do not use the wrong auxiliary for singular and plural subjects.
explanationVi:
Thì quá khứ đơn bị động dùng khi bạn muốn nói về một hành động đã hoàn thành trong quá khứ, nhưng nhấn mạnh vào đối tượng nhận hành động chứ không phải người thực hiện hành động. Công thức là was/were + quá khứ phân từ. Dùng was với chủ ngữ số ít, dùng were với chủ ngữ số nhiều. Nếu muốn nói ai làm, thêm by + người. Ví dụ: The house was built in 1998. The letters were sent yesterday. The room was cleaned by the students.

Cần nhớ quá khứ phân từ không phải là dạng quá khứ đơn. Với động từ có quy tắc, quá khứ phân từ thường có đuôi -ed, nhưng nhiều động từ bất quy tắc có dạng riêng như built, sent, broken, taken, written. Trong câu bị động, chủ ngữ không làm hành động mà là người/vật bị tác động bởi hành động đó.

Dùng quá khứ đơn bị động khi hành động đã xảy ra và kết thúc trong quá khứ, nhất là khi người làm không biết, không quan trọng, hoặc đã rõ. Không được bỏ was/were. Không được dùng sai was/were với số ít hay số nhiều.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không đổi hình thức động từ để tạo bị động như tiếng Anh, nên người học hay bỏ quên was/were hoặc dùng sai was/were với danh từ số ít/số nhiều. Tiếng Việt cũng dễ làm người học đặt người làm hành động lên trước, trong khi tiếng Anh bị động thường đưa đối tượng lên đầu câu.

commonMistakes.wrong: My email has sent.

commonMistakes.why: The present perfect passive is has/have been + past participle, not has/have + past participle.
commonMistakes.wrong: All the tickets have sold.

commonMistakes.right: The rooms have already been cleaned.
commonMistakes.why: Already comes after has/have and before been or before the past participle in some structures; in the passive, keep been.
commonMistakes.wrong: The rooms have already cleaned.

drills.target: The documents have been signed.

acceptedAnswers: has been opened
drills.explanation: For a singular subject, use has been + past participle.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The shop ____ opened.
drills.target: has been opened

acceptedAnswers: The bridge has been repaired.
drills.explanation: This is a full passive sentence showing that the work is now complete.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in the present perfect passive: They have repaired the bridge.

acceptedAnswers: The message has been read.

explanation:
The present perfect passive is formed with has/have been + past participle. We use it when the action is finished, but the result is important now, for example: The bridge has been repaired, so people can use it again.

In this structure, the person or thing affected by the action becomes the subject: They have painted the house becomes The house has been painted. Use has with singular subjects and have with plural subjects and I/you/we/they. After has/have, do not forget been. A very common error is to leave out been and say The house has painted, which is not correct.

For Vietnamese learners, the main difficulty is that English shows the passive with an extra helper verb, been, while Vietnamese often uses đã + bị/được or just context without changing the verb form much. So remember the pattern: has/have + been + past participle.
explanationVi:
Thì hiện tại hoàn thành bị động được tạo bằng has/have been + quá khứ phân từ. Ta dùng nó khi hành động đã hoàn tất, nhưng kết quả của hành động vẫn quan trọng ở hiện tại, ví dụ: The bridge has been repaired nghĩa là cây cầu đã được sửa xong và bây giờ có thể sử dụng.

Trong cấu trúc này, đối tượng chịu tác động của hành động trở thành chủ ngữ: They have painted the house đổi thành The house has been painted. Dùng has với chủ ngữ số ít, và have với chủ ngữ số nhiều cũng như I/you/we/they. Sau has/have, không được quên been. Lỗi rất phổ biến là bỏ been và viết The house has painted, nhưng câu đó sai.

Với người học tiếng Việt, khó nhất là tiếng Anh phải dùng thêm động từ phụ been để tạo bị động, trong khi tiếng Việt thường dùng đã + bị/được hoặc chỉ cần ngữ cảnh mà không đổi hình thức động từ nhiều. Vì vậy cần nhớ thật chắc mẫu: has/have + been + past participle.
formPatterns: Singular subject + has been + past participle
Plural subject + have been + past participle
Passive focus on the result of a completed action
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường diễn đạt bị động bằng đã + bị/được hoặc chỉ đổi trật tự câu, nên người học dễ quên been trong tiếng Anh và viết kiểu *has repaired* thay vì *has been repaired*. Cũng dễ nhầm giữa thì hiện tại hoàn thành và quá khứ đơn khi nói về kết quả hiện tại.

explanation:
Modal passive is the pattern modal verb + be + past participle. The modal shows obligation, possibility, or permission, while be + past participle shows that the subject receives the action rather than does it.

Common modals in this pattern are must be done, should be checked, can be repaired, may be used, and could be improved. The passive is often used when the person doing the action is unknown, unimportant, or obvious from context.

Remember that the be cannot be dropped: must finished, should cleaned, and can signed are all incorrect. In a passive sentence with a modal, the form after the modal is always be + past participle.

Trong IELTS, cấu trúc này rất hữu ích vì nó trang trọng và chính xác, thường đi với need, want, hope, ready, likely, important và các động từ/tính từ tương tự.
formPatterns: verb/adjective + to have been + past participle
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không có dạng nguyên mẫu bị động tương ứng, nên người học dễ bỏ to be hoặc dùng sai dạng chủ động: cần nhớ 'được/bị' trong tiếng Việt thường tương ứng với passive infinitive trong tiếng Anh, đặc biệt sau need, want, hope, ready, important, likely. Với ý hoàn thành trước đó, tiếng Việt hay nói 'đã được...', còn tiếng Anh cần 'to have been + V3'.

title: Causative Have and Get
summary: Arranging for someone else to do something, as in have the car repaired.

commonMistakes.right: I had my car repaired yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: This means I arranged for someone else to repair the car. The structure is have + object + past participle.
commonMistakes.wrong: I had repaired my car yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: She got her hair cut before the wedding.
commonMistakes.why: Get + object + past participle also means arranging for someone else to do the action, often in informal English.
commonMistakes.wrong: She got cut her hair before the wedding.

commonMistakes.right: We had the house painted last month.
commonMistakes.why: In the causative, the object comes before the past participle. The past participle shows the service done by another person.
commonMistakes.wrong: We had painted the house last month.

commonMistakes.right: He is having his phone fixed now.
commonMistakes.why: Have can be used in the continuous form for a service arranged in progress. The structure is be having + object + past participle.
commonMistakes.wrong: He is having fixed his phone now.

acceptedAnswers: had my laptop repaired
drills.explanation: In the causative, have is followed by an object and a past participle. This means someone else repaired the laptop for me.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I ______ yesterday.
drills.target: had my laptop repaired

acceptedAnswers: got her watch fixed
drills.explanation: Get + object + past participle is a common causative pattern. It means she arranged for someone to fix the watch.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She ______ last week.
drills.target: got her watch fixed

acceptedAnswers: had the windows cleaned
drills.explanation: This is the causative have structure. The windows are not doing the cleaning; someone else is.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: They ______ this morning.
drills.target: had the windows cleaned

acceptedAnswers: got my bike repaired
drills.explanation: This sentence uses get in the causative form. It means I arranged for another person to repair the bike.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I ______ after the accident.
drills.target: got my bike repaired

acceptedAnswers: He had his suit tailored for the interview.
choices: He had his suit tailored for the interview.
He had tailored his suit for the interview.
He had his suit tailors for the interview.
drills.explanation: The correct causative pattern is have + object + past participle. The suit was tailored by someone else.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He had his suit tailored for the interview.

acceptedAnswers: She got her documents translated into English.
choices: She got translated her documents into English.
She got her documents translated into English.
She got her documents translate into English.
drills.explanation: Get + object + past participle is correct here. The documents were translated by another person.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She got her documents translated into English.

acceptedAnswers: We had the carpet cleaned yesterday.
choices: We had cleaned the carpet yesterday.
We had the carpet cleaned yesterday.
We had the carpet clean yesterday.
drills.explanation: In causative have, the object comes before the past participle. This means we arranged the cleaning.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: We had the carpet cleaned yesterday.

acceptedAnswers: They got their roof repaired after the storm.
choices: They got repaired their roof after the storm.
They got their roof repaired after the storm.
They got their roof repair after the storm.
drills.explanation: This is the correct get causative pattern. It means they arranged for someone to repair the roof.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: They got their roof repaired after the storm.

acceptedAnswers: I had my phone fixed because it stopped working.
drills.explanation: This is a full causative sentence. Have + object + past participle shows that another person fixed the phone.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence. Use have and this meaning: someone else fixed my phone.
drills.target: I had my phone fixed because it stopped working.

acceptedAnswers: She got her hair cut before the ceremony.
drills.explanation: Get + object + past participle means she arranged the haircut. This is common in everyday English.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence. Use get and this meaning: another person cut her hair.
drills.target: She got her hair cut before the ceremony.

acceptedAnswers: Have you had your passport renewed yet?
drills.explanation: This question uses the causative have in the present perfect. It asks whether someone else has renewed the passport.
drills.prompt: Write a question. Use have and this meaning: someone else renewed your passport.
drills.target: Have you had your passport renewed yet?

acceptedAnswers: He is having his car washed at the moment.
drills.explanation: The continuous form can show an arranged service in progress. The car is being washed by someone else now.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence. Use have in the continuous form: someone else is washing his car now.
drills.target: He is having his car washed at the moment.

acceptedAnswers: I have my suit cleaned every month.
drills.explanation: This sentence shows a repeated arranged service. It means another person cleans the suit every month.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the causative form: A cleaner cleans my suit every month.
drills.target: I have my suit cleaned every month.

acceptedAnswers: They got their house painted last summer.
drills.explanation: This is the same meaning in causative get form. It shows that they arranged for someone else to paint the house.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the causative form: They arranged for someone to paint their house last summer.
drills.target: They got their house painted last summer.

explanation: The causative have/get is used when you arrange for another person or a service company to do something for you. The form is have/get + object + past participle: I had my car repaired, She got her hair cut, We had the house painted. In negative and question forms, the auxiliary changes in the normal way: Did you have your passport renewed? He didn’t get his phone fixed. Be careful not to use an active verb after the object: I had my car repaired is correct, but I had repaired my car means something different and does not express the causative meaning.
explanationVi: Cấu trúc causative have/get được dùng khi bạn nhờ hoặc thuê người khác làm gì cho mình. Mẫu câu là have/get + tân ngữ + quá khứ phân từ: I had my car repaired = tôi đã mang xe đi sửa / nhờ người khác sửa xe cho tôi; She got her hair cut = cô ấy đi cắt tóc. Trong cấu trúc này, hành động do người khác thực hiện nên động từ phải ở dạng quá khứ phân từ, không dùng dạng chủ động thường như repaired hay cut phía sau tân ngữ trực tiếp. Ví dụ đúng là I had my car repaired, còn I had repaired my car lại là thì hoàn thành của động từ have/repair và không mang nghĩa nhờ ai đó làm giúp. Với câu hỏi và phủ định, trợ động từ vẫn đổi như bình thường: Did you have your passport renewed?; He didn’t get his phone fixed. Người Việt hay bị ảnh hưởng bởi cách nói “đi sửa”, “nhờ sửa”, nên dễ đặt sai thứ tự từ hoặc quên quá khứ phân từ.
formPatterns: have/get + object + past participle + time expression
did + subject + have/get + object + past participle?
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng “đi + động từ” hoặc “nhờ + người + làm gì”, nên người học dễ dịch từng chữ và đặt sai trật tự: I had repaired my car, I got fixed my phone. Cần nhớ tiếng Anh phải có tân ngữ đứng trước quá khứ phân từ: had my car repaired, got my phone fixed.

title: Impersonal Passive
summary: It is said that, and He is said to, for reporting without a source.

commonMistakes.right: It is said that the company will expand next year.
commonMistakes.why: Use impersonal passive with it is said that + clause when the speaker does not name the source.
commonMistakes.wrong: Is said that the company will expand next year.

commonMistakes.right: He is believed to be the best candidate.
commonMistakes.why: Use the passive reporting pattern subject + be + past participle + to-infinitive.
commonMistakes.wrong: He believed to be the best candidate.

commonMistakes.right: People say that the meeting starts at nine.
commonMistakes.why: If you keep the active reporting verb, you need a real subject such as people or they.
commonMistakes.wrong: Is said that the meeting starts at nine.

commonMistakes.right: It is believed that the road is closed.
commonMistakes.why: Use it + be + past participle + that-clause, not a bare passive verb at the start.
commonMistakes.wrong: Believed that the road is closed.

acceptedAnswers: It is said that the price will rise.
choices: It said that the price will rise.
It is said that the price will rise.
It is saying that the price will rise.
drills.explanation: This is the impersonal passive with it is said that + clause. It reports information without naming who said it.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: It is said that the price will rise.

acceptedAnswers: He is expected to arrive soon.
drills.explanation: This pattern is subject + be + past participle + to-infinitive. It is used when we report what others think or predict.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using: He / expect / arrive soon.
drills.target: He is expected to arrive soon.

acceptedAnswers: It is believed that the museum is closed on Mondays.
drills.explanation: Use it is believed that + clause when the belief is general and the source is not named.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the impersonal passive: People believe that the museum is closed on Mondays.
drills.target: It is believed that the museum is closed on Mondays.

acceptedAnswers: The museum is believed to be closed on Mondays.
choices: The museum believes to be closed on Mondays.
The museum is believed to be closed on Mondays.
The museum is believing to be closed on Mondays.
drills.explanation: This is the passive reporting structure with a person or thing as the subject. The to-infinitive follows the past participle.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The museum is believed to be closed on Mondays.

acceptedAnswers: It is rumored that the singer has left the country.
drills.explanation: Rumored is a reporting passive verb here. The it + be + past participle + that-clause pattern is common in news style.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence: rumor / singer / leave the country.
drills.target: It is rumored that the singer has left the country.

acceptedAnswers: The singer is rumored to have left the country.
drills.explanation: When the reporting verb is followed by a subject, use subject + be + past participle + to have + past participle for an earlier action.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using passive reporting with the subject first: It is rumored that the singer has left the country.
drills.target: The singer is rumored to have left the country.

acceptedAnswers: It is reported that the bridge will open next month.
choices: It reports that the bridge will open next month.
It is reported that the bridge will open next month.
It is report that the bridge will open next month.
drills.explanation: The impersonal passive uses it + be + past participle + that-clause. The reporting source is left unspecified.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: It is reported that the bridge will open next month.

acceptedAnswers: The bridge is reported to open next month.
drills.explanation: This sentence is grammatical, though it often sounds less natural than the version with a that-clause when the event is still in the future.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the passive reporting structure with the bridge as the subject: People report that the bridge will open next month.
drills.target: The bridge is reported to open next month.

acceptedAnswers: It is widely accepted that online learning is effective.
drills.explanation: An adverb like widely can modify the passive reporting verb. The structure still hides the source.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence: widely accept / online learning / effective.
drills.target: It is widely accepted that online learning is effective.

acceptedAnswers: He is said to be working in Singapore.
choices: He is said to works in Singapore.
He is said to be working in Singapore.
He said to be working in Singapore.
drills.explanation: After said, use be + verb-ing for an action in progress. Do not use a bare infinitive or omit be.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He is said to be working in Singapore.

acceptedAnswers: It is thought that the policy will fail.
drills.explanation: It is thought that + clause is another impersonal passive reporting form. It is common in formal writing.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence: think / the policy / fail.
drills.target: It is thought that the policy will fail.

acceptedAnswers: The policy is thought to fail.
choices: The policy is thought fail.
The policy thought to fail.
The policy is thought to fail.
drills.explanation: This is the subject form of the passive reporting pattern. The to-infinitive is required after thought.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The policy is thought to fail.

explanation:
The impersonal passive is used to report a belief, rumour, opinion, or statement without naming the source. Two very common patterns are it is said that + clause and subject + be + past participle + to-infinitive, for example It is said that the company will expand and The company is said to expand. In many cases, the subject form sounds more natural with present perfect or progressive meaning, for example He is said to be working in Singapore or The singer is rumored to have left the country. Choose the pattern that best fits the tense and meaning you want to report.

In formal English, this structure is common in news reports, academic writing, and neutral summaries. It lets the writer distance themselves from the information and avoid naming a source. The meaning is similar to People say that... or They believe that..., but the passive form is more compact and more formal.
explanationVi:
Thể bị động vô nhân xưng dùng để báo cáo ý kiến, tin đồn, nhận định hoặc thông tin mà không nêu rõ ai là người nói ra. Hai mẫu rất thường gặp là it is said that + mệnh đề và chủ ngữ + be + past participle + to-infinitive, ví dụ It is said that the company will expand và The company is said to expand. Trong nhiều trường hợp, dạng có chủ ngữ phía trước tự nhiên hơn khi muốn diễn tả ý đang diễn ra hoặc đã xảy ra trước đó, ví dụ He is said to be working in Singapore hoặc The singer is rumored to have left the country. Hãy chọn mẫu phù hợp với thì và ý nghĩa bạn muốn diễn đạt.

Trong tiếng Anh trang trọng, cấu trúc này rất phổ biến trong báo chí, văn viết học thuật và các bản tường thuật trung tính. Nó giúp người viết giữ khoảng cách với thông tin và không phải nêu nguồn cụ thể. Ý nghĩa gần giống People say that... hoặc They believe that..., nhưng dạng bị động thường gọn hơn và trang trọng hơn.
formPatterns: Subject + be + past participle + to be + -ing
Subject + be + past participle + to have + past participle
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng câu chủ động vô chủ ngữ rõ ràng như người ta nói rằng..., ai cũng cho rằng..., dư luận cho rằng...; khi chuyển sang tiếng Anh, người học dễ bỏ it hoặc bỏ be trong mẫu bị động vô nhân xưng. Cũng hay sai ở chỗ dùng trực tiếp He said to... thay vì He is said to..., hoặc giữ nguyên mệnh đề tiếng Việt mà không đổi sang cấu trúc bị động báo cáo.

title: Indefinite Article A/An
summary: First mention and non-specific reference. Vietnamese has no article system at all.

commonMistakes.right: I bought an umbrella because it was raining.
commonMistakes.why: Umbrella begins with a vowel sound, so we use an. Many Vietnamese learners choose a because the spelling starts with u, but article choice depends on sound, not spelling.
commonMistakes.wrong: I bought a umbrella because it was raining.

commonMistakes.right: She wants a job in Hanoi.
commonMistakes.why: We use a before a singular countable noun when we mention it for the first time or when it is not specific. Vietnamese has no article, so learners often leave it out.
commonMistakes.wrong: She wants job in Hanoi.

commonMistakes.right: He is an engineer.
commonMistakes.why: Engineer starts with a vowel sound, so we use an. The spelling starts with e and the pronunciation also starts with a vowel sound.
commonMistakes.wrong: He is a engineer.

commonMistakes.right: Please give me a pen.
commonMistakes.why: We use a with one singular countable noun when it is not a specific pen. A bare singular noun is not correct in standard English.
commonMistakes.wrong: Please give me pen.

acceptedAnswers: a
drills.explanation: We use a before a singular countable noun that starts with a consonant sound.
drills.prompt: I need ___ book for class.
drills.target: a

acceptedAnswers: an
drills.explanation: We use an before a singular countable noun that starts with a vowel sound.
drills.prompt: She is reading ___ interesting article.
drills.target: an

acceptedAnswers: a
drills.explanation: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so the correct article is an.
drills.prompt: He bought ___ umbrella yesterday.
drills.target: a

acceptedAnswers: an
drills.explanation: Engineer starts with a vowel sound, so we use an.
drills.prompt: My brother is ___ engineer.
drills.target: an

acceptedAnswers: I saw a cat in the garden.
drills.explanation: We use a for a singular countable noun when we mention it for the first time and it is not specific.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: I / see / cat / in the garden
drills.target: I saw a cat in the garden.

acceptedAnswers: She wants a new job.
drills.explanation: Job is a singular countable noun, so we need a before it.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: She / want / new job
drills.target: She wants a new job.

acceptedAnswers: He is an old teacher.
drills.explanation: Old begins with a vowel sound, so we use an.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: He / be / old teacher
drills.target: He is an old teacher.

acceptedAnswers: There is a hospital near my house.
drills.explanation: We use a before a singular countable noun when talking about one example, not a specific one.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: There / be / hospital / near my house
drills.target: There is a hospital near my house.

acceptedAnswers: an
choices: a
an
drills.explanation: Ice cream begins with a vowel sound, so an is correct.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct article: She wants ___ ice cream.
drills.target: an

acceptedAnswers: a
choices: an
a
drills.explanation: University begins with a consonant sound /j/, so we use a, not an.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct article: He goes to ___ university in the city.
drills.target: a

acceptedAnswers: an
drills.explanation: Use an before hour because hour starts with a vowel sound, even though h is written first.
drills.prompt: It will take ___ hour.
drills.target: an

acceptedAnswers: a
drills.explanation: House starts with a consonant sound, so we use a.
drills.prompt: They live in ___ house near the park.
drills.target: a

acceptedAnswers: He is an honest man.
drills.explanation: Honest begins with a silent h, so the first sound is a vowel sound and we use an.
drills.prompt: Rewrite with the correct article: He is a honest man.
drills.target: He is an honest man.

acceptedAnswers: It is a useful book.
drills.explanation: Useful begins with a consonant sound /j/, so the correct article is a, not an.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: It is an useful book.
drills.target: It is a useful book.

explanation: A and an are indefinite articles. They are used before a singular countable noun when the noun is not specific, when we mention it for the first time, or when we mean one example of a thing or job: a car, an apple, a doctor. Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound. The sound is important, not the spelling, so we say an hour but a university. With most singular countable nouns in English, you need an article; Vietnamese often leaves this out because Vietnamese does not have an article system. The article is not used with plural nouns or uncountable nouns in the same way, so this lesson focuses only on singular countable nouns.
explanationVi: Mạo từ bất định a/an dùng trước danh từ đếm được số ít khi danh từ chưa xác định, khi ta nhắc đến nó lần đầu, hoặc khi ta nói về một người/vật thuộc loại đó. Ví dụ: a car, an apple, a doctor. Dùng a trước âm phụ âm và dùng an trước âm nguyên âm. Điều quan trọng là âm đầu, không phải chữ cái đầu, nên ta nói an hour nhưng a university. Đây là điểm rất dễ sai với người Việt vì tiếng Việt không có hệ thống mạo từ, nên người học thường bỏ luôn a/an. Với đa số danh từ đếm được số ít trong tiếng Anh, bạn cần có mạo từ.
formPatterns: a + singular countable noun beginning with a consonant sound
an + singular countable noun beginning with a vowel sound
a/an + noun for first mention or non-specific reference
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt không có mạo từ, nên người học thường bỏ a/an trước danh từ đếm được số ít. Ngoài ra, cần nhớ chọn theo âm đầu chứ không theo chữ cái đầu.

title: Definite Article The
summary: Shared or previously mentioned reference. A1 by level, near the hardest thing in English by difficulty.

commonMistakes.right: The sun is very bright today.
commonMistakes.why: Use the when there is only one of something in the world, such as the sun, the moon, or the earth.
commonMistakes.wrong: Sun is very bright today.

commonMistakes.right: I bought a book and the book was expensive.
commonMistakes.why: Use the when you mention the same noun again after it has already been introduced.
commonMistakes.wrong: I bought a book and book was expensive.

commonMistakes.right: The teacher gave us homework.
commonMistakes.why: Use the when both speaker and listener know which person or thing is meant from the situation.
commonMistakes.wrong: Teacher gave us homework.

commonMistakes.right: I need the key to my room.
commonMistakes.why: Use the when a specific noun is identified, not when you mean any one item in general.
commonMistakes.wrong: I need key to my room.

acceptedAnswers: the
drills.explanation: Use the before a specific noun that both speaker and listener can identify.
drills.prompt: I bought a coat yesterday. ___ coat is warm.
drills.target: the

acceptedAnswers: the
drills.explanation: The is used when we refer back to a noun that was mentioned before.
drills.prompt: She saw a cat in the garden. Later, she fed ___ cat.
drills.target: the

acceptedAnswers: The book is on the table.
choices: A book is on the table.
The book is on the table.
Book is on the table.
drills.explanation: The is correct because the speaker refers to one specific book and one specific table in the situation.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The book is on the table.

acceptedAnswers: The boy in the blue shirt is my son.
drills.explanation: Use the when a noun is made specific by extra information after it, such as a phrase starting with in, on, or with.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using these words: boy / in the blue shirt / is / my son
drills.target: The boy in the blue shirt is my son.

acceptedAnswers: The
drills.explanation: The is used before a noun when the speaker and listener know exactly which one is meant.
drills.prompt: Please open ___ window.
drills.target: the

acceptedAnswers: I went to the hospital yesterday.
choices: I went to a hospital yesterday.
I went to the hospital yesterday.
I went to hospital yesterday.
drills.explanation: The hospital is correct when you mean a specific hospital or, in some varieties of English, when the place is used for its normal function. A is wrong here because it means one hospital among many, not a known one.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I went to the hospital yesterday.

acceptedAnswers: the
drills.explanation: Use the with a noun that has already been identified in the conversation or text.
drills.prompt: There is a car outside. ___ car is red.
drills.target: the

acceptedAnswers: The people in my class are friendly.
drills.explanation: Use the before people when you mean a specific group, not people in general.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using these words: people / in my class / are / friendly
drills.target: The people in my class are friendly.

acceptedAnswers: The
drills.explanation: The marks a noun as specific, not general.
drills.prompt: I like ___ music on the radio.
drills.target: the

acceptedAnswers: I met the manager of the hotel.
choices: I met a manager of the hotel.
I met the manager of the hotel.
I met manager of the hotel.
drills.explanation: The is needed because the manager is a particular person identified by the phrase of the hotel.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I met the manager of the hotel.

acceptedAnswers: The girl sitting next to me is my cousin.
drills.explanation: The is used when a noun is defined by a participle phrase or other description, so the listener knows which one you mean.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using these words: girl / sitting next to me / is / my cousin
drills.target: The girl sitting next to me is my cousin.

acceptedAnswers: the
drills.explanation: Use the when the noun is one specific thing in the situation, not any thing of that type.
drills.prompt: Can you turn on ___ light, please?
drills.target: the

acceptedAnswers: The plane leaves at 9 a.m.

explanation: The definite article the is used when a noun is specific, known, or already mentioned. It tells the listener which person or thing you mean. This is different from a/an, which introduces one non-specific singular countable noun for the first time: a book means any book, while the book means one particular book that is already known from context or discussion. Vietnamese learners often leave out the because Vietnamese usually does not need an article, so in English you must check whether the noun is general or specific. Use the when the noun has already been mentioned, when the speaker and listener both know it, when there is only one of it, or when a phrase after the noun makes it specific.
explanationVi: Mạo từ xác định the dùng khi danh từ đã xác định rõ: người nghe biết bạn đang nói về ai/cái gì, hoặc danh từ đó đã được nhắc trước, hoặc được xác định bởi ngữ cảnh. the làm cho danh từ trở nên “cụ thể”, không còn là một đối tượng bất kỳ nữa. Ví dụ: a book = một quyển sách bất kỳ, còn the book = quyển sách cụ thể đó. Nhiều người Việt hay bỏ the vì trong tiếng Việt thường không có mạo từ, nhưng trong tiếng Anh bạn phải kiểm tra xem danh từ là chung hay riêng, đã biết hay chưa, rồi mới chọn đúng. Dùng the khi danh từ đã xuất hiện trước đó, khi cả người nói và người nghe đều biết, khi chỉ có một thứ duy nhất, hoặc khi cụm phía sau danh từ làm nó trở nên xác định.

explanation: Zero article means no article is used before a noun. In English, this is common with generic plurals, uncountable nouns, and many abstract nouns when we talk about them in a general sense: apples, water, honesty, music, English, advice. In these cases, the noun does not point to one specific thing, so the is usually wrong. Use the only when the noun becomes specific: the apples on the table, the water in this bottle, the honesty of his answer, the children in the garden. For Vietnamese learners, this point is difficult because Vietnamese often does not have articles, so it can be tempting to add the everywhere. In English, however, zero article and the have different meanings: zero article = general; the = specific and known.
explanationVi: Zero article là khi tiếng Anh dùng danh từ mà không có mạo từ a/an hay the. Điểm này rất quan trọng vì tiếng Việt thường không có hệ mạo từ như tiếng Anh, nên người học dễ bỏ sót hoặc thêm the một cách không cần thiết. Với danh từ số nhiều mang nghĩa chung, danh từ không đếm được, và nhiều danh từ trừu tượng dùng theo nghĩa khái quát, tiếng Anh thường không dùng mạo từ: apples, water, honesty, music, advice, English. Ví dụ I like apples nghĩa là thích táo nói chung, Water is essential for life nghĩa là nước nói chung, Honesty is important nghĩa là sự trung thực nói chung. Trong các trường hợp này, the không dùng vì the chỉ một thứ cụ thể, đã xác định: the apples on the table, the water in this bottle, the children in the garden. Vì vậy, hãy nhớ: không có mạo từ = nghĩa chung/khái quát; the = nghĩa cụ thể, người nói và người nghe cùng biết đang nói về cái nào.

specific noun with context: the + apples on the table

Say some advice, some information, some furniture, or a piece of advice / a piece of information when you need one item of meaning or information.
