The earlier you start, easier it is to finish on time.
drills.explanation: The structure uses a comparative in each clause: earlier... the easier.

drills.target: The earlier you start, the easier it is to finish on time.

acceptedAnswers: The more carefully she prepares, the fewer mistakes she makes.

acceptedAnswers: The longer we talk, the clearer the problem becomes.
choices: The longer we talk, the clearer the problem becomes.
The longer we talk, clearer the problem becomes.
Longer we talk, the clearer the problem becomes.
drills.explanation: Both halves need the comparative pattern: longer... the clearer.

acceptedAnswers: The more we practise speaking, the more confident we become.

title: Prepositions of Time
summary: In, on, and at across clock time, dates, and periods.

commonMistakes.right: The meeting starts at 3 p.m.
commonMistakes.why: Use at with a specific clock time. In Vietnamese, the same preposition is often used for both time and date expressions, so learners may confuse at, on, and in.
commonMistakes.wrong: The meeting starts in 3 p.m.

commonMistakes.right: We have a test on Monday.
commonMistakes.why: Use on with days and dates. Vietnamese does not mark this distinction the same way, so on is often omitted or replaced with in.
commonMistakes.wrong: We have a test in Monday.

commonMistakes.right: She was born in 2001.
commonMistakes.why: Use in with years, months, and longer periods such as seasons. Vietnamese learners may use on or at before a year.
commonMistakes.wrong: She was born on 2001.

commonMistakes.right: I usually study in the evening.
commonMistakes.why: Use in with parts of the day like morning, afternoon, and evening, but not with exact clock times. Vietnamese speakers may say at the evening by transferring the general pattern of at + time.
commonMistakes.wrong: I usually study at the evening.

acceptedAnswers: at
drills.explanation: Use at for a specific clock time.

explanationVi:
Giới từ chỉ thời gian trong tiếng Anh rất nhỏ nhưng rất quan trọng vì chúng cho biết một sự việc xảy ra khi nào. Dùng at cho thời điểm chính xác và những mốc cố định như 7:30, midnight, noon. Dùng on cho ngày trong tuần và ngày tháng cụ thể như Monday, Friday, 12 June. Dùng in cho tháng, năm, mùa, và các khoảng thời gian dài hơn như in the morning hoặc in the evening. Một số cụm là cố định, vì vậy nên học theo từng cụm từ chứ không chỉ học quy tắc riêng lẻ.

Người học tiếng Việt thường dễ nhầm vì tiếng Việt không dùng hệ thống giới từ thời gian giống tiếng Anh. Trong tiếng Việt, một từ như “vào” hoặc ngữ cảnh câu có thể dùng cho nhiều loại thời gian khác nhau, nên khi chuyển sang tiếng Anh dễ bị dùng nhầm at, on, in hoặc bỏ giới từ hoàn toàn. Cần nhớ: at = giờ cụ thể; on = ngày/ngày tháng; in = tháng, năm, mùa, buổi trong ngày.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không phân biệt rõ ba mốc thời gian này bằng giới từ riêng, nên người học hay nói sai kiểu dùng in cho giờ, on cho năm, hoặc bỏ giới từ trước ngày giờ.

explanation: In, on, and at are all prepositions of place, but they do not mean the same thing. In usually means inside an enclosed space or area: in a box, in a room, in Hanoi. On usually means on a surface: on the table, on the wall, on the floor. At usually means a specific point, place, or location used as a reference: at the door, at the station, at school, at home, at work. These are not always completely logical, so some phrases must be learned as fixed patterns. English often cares about whether something is inside, touching a surface, or located at a point. Vietnamese learners often use one place word for all of these meanings, so the English choice must be memorized and practised.
explanationVi: Trong tiếng Anh, in, on, và at đều là giới từ chỉ nơi chốn, nhưng mỗi từ dùng trong một kiểu vị trí khác nhau. In thường có nghĩa là “ở trong”, dùng với không gian kín hoặc khu vực: in a box, in a room, in Hanoi. On thường có nghĩa là “ở trên bề mặt”: on the table, on the wall, on the floor. At thường dùng cho một điểm hoặc địa điểm cụ thể: at the door, at the station, at school, at home, at work. Nhiều cách dùng không hoàn toàn theo logic, nên có những cụm phải học thuộc như mẫu cố định. Điểm khó với người học tiếng Việt là tiếng Việt thường dùng một từ/kiểu diễn đạt chung cho nhiều quan hệ không gian, còn tiếng Anh phân biệt khá rõ giữa “ở trong”, “ở trên”, và “ở tại/ở điểm nào đó”.
formPatterns: fixed expressions: at home, at work, at school
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng một cách nói chung cho vị trí (ở, trong, trên, tại), nên người học dễ đổi in/on/at sai theo thói quen dịch từng từ.

explanationVi: Trong tiếng Anh, các giới từ chỉ chuyển động diễn tả hướng đi của hành động, không chỉ vị trí. Dùng to khi đi về phía một nơi hoặc một người; dùng into khi đi từ bên ngoài vào bên trong; dùng onto khi di chuyển lên trên một bề mặt hoặc lên phương tiện; dùng through khi đi xuyên qua một nơi, thường là từ đầu này sang đầu kia; và dùng across khi đi từ bên này sang bên kia của một khu vực, mặt phẳng, con đường hoặc cây cầu. Người học tiếng Việt hay nhầm vì trong tiếng Việt thường chỉ dùng các từ như “đến”, “vào”, “lên”, “qua”, nên cần chú ý rằng trong tiếng Anh phải chọn đúng giới từ theo kiểu chuyển động. Ví dụ: walk to the park, run into the house, jump onto the bed, drive through the tunnel, swim across the river.

title: During, For, and While
summary: Duration expressed with a noun versus with a clause.

commonMistakes.right: We stayed in Hanoi for three days.
commonMistakes.why: Use for with a length of time. Three days tells us how long the action lasted.
commonMistakes.wrong: We stayed in Hanoi during three days.

commonMistakes.right: I met my teacher during the meeting.
commonMistakes.why: Use during with a noun for a period or event. Meeting is a noun, so during is correct here.
commonMistakes.wrong: I met my teacher for the meeting.

commonMistakes.right: The power went out while I was cooking dinner.
commonMistakes.why: Use while with a clause about an action in progress. It connects two actions happening at the same time.
commonMistakes.wrong: The power went out during I was cooking dinner.

commonMistakes.right: I studied English for two hours every day.
commonMistakes.why: For is used with a duration. It does not mean 'throughout the whole period' in this structure.
commonMistakes.wrong: I studied English during two hours every day.

explanation: For, during, and while are all used to talk about time, but they are not interchangeable. Use for + a length of time, such as for two hours or for a week; use during + a noun, such as during the lesson or during the holiday; use while + a clause, such as while I was studying or while the baby slept. A simple test is this: if the time expression answers how long, use for; if it names an event or period, use during; if it includes a subject and verb, use while. In IELTS writing and speaking, Vietnamese learners often mix during and for because both can be translated as trong, but English makes a stronger form distinction.
explanationVi:
For, during, và while đều nói về thời gian, nhưng không dùng thay thế cho nhau. Dùng for + một khoảng thời gian, ví dụ for two hours, for a week, for three days. Dùng during + một danh từ chỉ sự kiện hoặc một giai đoạn, ví dụ during the lesson, during the holiday, during the meeting. Dùng while + một mệnh đề, tức là có chủ ngữ và động từ, ví dụ while I was studying, while the baby slept.

Cách nhớ nhanh: nếu ý là “trong bao lâu” thì dùng for; nếu ý là “trong lúc nào / trong sự kiện nào” thì dùng during; nếu sau đó có cả chủ ngữ và động từ thì dùng while. Người Việt hay nhầm vì từ “trong” trong tiếng Việt có thể tương ứng với cả during, for, và while tùy ngữ cảnh. Vì vậy, không nên dịch từng từ một. Hãy nhìn cấu trúc của câu tiếng Anh trước.

L1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng “trong” cho cả khoảng thời gian, sự kiện, và thời điểm diễn ra đồng thời, nên người học hay viết during three days, for the meeting, hoặc during I was working thay vì phân biệt for + duration, during + noun, while + clause.

drills.target: He repaired the bike with a wrench.

acceptedAnswers: The window was broken by a child.
choices: The window was broken with a child.
The window was broken by a child.
The window was broken in a child.
drills.explanation: By is correct because a child is the agent who broke the window.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The window was broken by a child.

acceptedAnswers: with
drills.explanation: With is used for the thing that opens the bottle.
drills.prompt: They opened the bottle ___ a corkscrew.
drills.target: with

acceptedAnswers: The song was sung by the singer.
drills.explanation: By is correct because the singer is the person who performed the action.
drills.prompt: The song was sung with the singer.
drills.target: The song was sung by the singer.

acceptedAnswers: The room was cleaned with a vacuum cleaner.
drills.explanation: With is correct because the vacuum cleaner is the cleaning tool.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the correct preposition: They cleaned the room using a vacuum cleaner.
drills.target: The room was cleaned with a vacuum cleaner.

acceptedAnswers: by
drills.explanation: By is correct because the action was done by the teacher.
drills.prompt: The homework was checked ___ the teacher.
drills.target: by

acceptedAnswers: with
drills.explanation: With is correct because a hammer is the instrument used.
drills.prompt: He hit the nail ___ a hammer.
drills.target: with

explanation: By and with often look similar, but they do different jobs. Use by to show the agent, the person or thing that does the action, especially in passive sentences: The letter was written by Sarah. Use with to show the instrument, tool, or object used to do the action: He cut the rope with a knife. In Vietnamese, learners often overuse bằng for both meanings, but English separates these ideas. A useful test is: if you mean “ai làm?”, use by; if you mean “dùng cái gì?”, use with. Sometimes context can allow either word with a different meaning, so always check whether you mean the doer or the tool.
explanationVi: By và with rất dễ nhầm vì tiếng Việt thường dùng “bằng” hoặc “do” cho nhiều trường hợp khác nhau. Trong tiếng Anh, by dùng để chỉ tác nhân, tức là người hoặc vật thực hiện hành động, nhất là trong câu bị động: The report was written by my manager. With dùng để chỉ công cụ, dụng cụ, phương tiện hoặc thứ được dùng để làm việc gì: I cut the paper with scissors. Cách tự kiểm tra rất đơn giản: nếu muốn hỏi “ai làm?” thì thường dùng by; nếu muốn hỏi “dùng cái gì?” thì dùng with. Ví dụ: The cake was made by my mother (mẹ tôi là người làm bánh), nhưng I made the cake with an oven and a mixer (tôi dùng lò nướng và máy trộn). Lưu ý là by không thay cho with, và with không thay cho by trong các câu này.
l1Notes: Người Việt dễ chuyển thẳng cách dùng “bằng”, “do”, “bởi” sang tiếng Anh, nên hay viết sai cả khi nói về người làm và khi nói về công cụ. Cần nhớ: by = người/vật thực hiện hành động; with = vật/dụng cụ dùng để thực hiện hành động.

title: Verb + Preposition
summary: Depend on, listen to, and the other fixed pairings with no logic to derive.

commonMistakes.right: She depends on her parents for support.
commonMistakes.why: Depend is followed by on, not by to or of.
commonMistakes.wrong: She depends to her parents for support.

commonMistakes.right: I listened to the teacher carefully.
commonMistakes.why: Listen is followed by to, not by at or in.
commonMistakes.wrong: I listened at the teacher carefully.

commonMistakes.right: They arrived in Hanoi late at night.
commonMistakes.why: Arrive is followed by in when we mean a city or country, and at for a specific point in time or place; the wrong preposition changes the meaning or makes the sentence ungrammatical.
commonMistakes.wrong: They arrived at Hanoi late in night.

commonMistakes.right: We are interested in this topic.
commonMistakes.why: Interested is followed by in, not by about.
commonMistakes.wrong: We are interested about this topic.

acceptedAnswers: on
drills.explanation: Depend is followed by on. In English, this fixed pairing must be memorized.
drills.prompt: She depends ___ her family.
drills.target: on

acceptedAnswers: to
drills.explanation: Listen is followed by to when you hear someone or something.
drills.prompt: Please listen ___ the instructions.
drills.target: to

acceptedAnswers: in
drills.explanation: Interested is followed by in.
drills.prompt: I am interested ___ science.
drills.target: in

acceptedAnswers: at
drills.explanation: Arrive is often followed by at for a specific place, or in for a city or country. Here the correct preposition is at.
drills.prompt: We arrived ___ the airport early.
drills.target: at

acceptedAnswers: of
drills.explanation: Consist is followed by of.
drills.prompt: This cake consists ___ flour, sugar, and eggs.
drills.target: of

acceptedAnswers: about
drills.explanation: Worry is followed by about when we say what causes concern.
drills.prompt: Do not worry ___ the small mistakes.
drills.target: about

acceptedAnswers: Choose the correct sentence. She depends on her teacher for advice.
choices: Choose the correct sentence. She depends to her teacher for advice.
Choose the correct sentence. She depends on her teacher for advice.
Choose the correct sentence. She depends at her teacher for advice.
drills.explanation: Depend is followed by on, so the sentence with depends on is correct.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Choose the correct sentence. She depends on her teacher for advice.

acceptedAnswers: Choose the correct sentence. I listened to the song on the radio.
choices: Choose the correct sentence. I listened at the song on the radio.
Choose the correct sentence. I listened to the song on the radio.
Choose the correct sentence. I listened in the song on the radio.
drills.explanation: Listen is followed by to.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Choose the correct sentence. I listened to the song on the radio.

acceptedAnswers: Choose the correct sentence. We are interested in your idea.
choices: Choose the correct sentence. We are interested about your idea.
Choose the correct sentence. We are interested in your idea.
Choose the correct sentence. We are interested at your idea.
drills.explanation: Interested is followed by in.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Choose the correct sentence. We are interested in your idea.

acceptedAnswers: I apologized to my colleague for the mistake.
drills.explanation: Apologize is followed by to when we say who we speak to.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with the correct preposition: I apologized my colleague for the mistake.
drills.target: I apologized to my colleague for the mistake.

acceptedAnswers: They are talking about the exam results.
drills.explanation: Talk about is the correct fixed pairing when the subject is the topic of the conversation.
drills.prompt: They are talking of the exam results.
drills.target: They are talking about the exam results.

acceptedAnswers: She is good at drawing.
drills.explanation: Good is followed by at before an activity or skill.
drills.prompt: Build a correct sentence using: she / good / drawing
drills.target: She is good at drawing.

acceptedAnswers: He is afraid of dogs.
drills.explanation: Afraid is followed by of.
drills.prompt: Build a correct sentence using: he / afraid / dogs
drills.target: He is afraid of dogs.

explanation:
Many English verbs need a fixed preposition. You cannot always translate from Vietnamese word by word. For example, depend on, listen to, talk about, interested in, good at, afraid of, and apologize to are fixed pairs that must be memorized. The preposition is part of the verb pattern, so changing it usually makes the sentence wrong or changes the meaning. A useful method is to learn the whole verb phrase together, not the verb alone.

Some verbs can take different prepositions in different meanings or structures. For example, arrive at is used for a specific place, while arrive in is used for a city or country. Because of this, it is safer to study each verb with a typical example sentence.

Với người Việt học tiếng Anh, lỗi rất hay gặp là dịch từng từ từ tiếng Việt sang tiếng Anh rồi chọn giới từ theo cảm giác hoặc theo nghĩa chung. Trong tiếng Việt, nhiều động từ không cần giới từ cố định như tiếng Anh, nên người học dễ bỏ giới từ hoặc dùng sai giới từ: depend to, listen at, interested about, apologize my friend, good in, afraid with. Nhưng trong tiếng Anh, các cụm này phải học như một khối cố định. Cách học tốt là ghi nhớ cả cụm: depend on, listen to, talk about, interested in, good at, afraid of, apologize to. Khi làm bài IELTS, nếu dùng đúng giới từ cố định, câu sẽ tự nhiên hơn và điểm ngữ pháp cũng tốt hơn.
explanationVi:
Nhiều động từ tiếng Anh đi kèm một giới từ cố định. Không thể dịch từng từ từ tiếng Việt sang tiếng Anh rồi tự chọn giới từ theo cảm giác. Ví dụ: depend on, listen to, talk about, interested in, good at, afraid of, apologize to. Giới từ ở đây là một phần của mẫu động từ, nên đổi giới từ thường làm câu sai hoặc đổi nghĩa.

Một số động từ có thể đi với giới từ khác nhau trong các nghĩa hoặc cấu trúc khác nhau. Ví dụ, arrive at dùng cho một địa điểm cụ thể, còn arrive in dùng cho một thành phố hoặc một quốc gia. Vì vậy, cách học an toàn nhất là học cả cụm cùng một câu ví dụ.

Với người Việt học tiếng Anh, lỗi phổ biến là bỏ giới từ hoặc dùng sai do ảnh hưởng của tiếng Việt, vì tiếng Việt không có nhiều mẫu động từ + giới từ cố định như tiếng Anh. Người học dễ viết depend to, listen at, interested about, apologize my friend, good in, afraid with. Trong tiếng Anh tự nhiên, các cụm này phải được học như một đơn vị cố định. Khi làm IELTS, dùng đúng giới từ giúp câu nghe tự nhiên hơn và tăng độ chính xác ngữ pháp.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không dùng giới từ cố định sau động từ như tiếng Anh, nên người học dễ dịch từng từ và chọn sai giới từ: depend to, listen at, interested about, good in, afraid with. Cần học cả cụm động từ + giới từ như một đơn vị.

title: Noun + Preposition
summary: Reason for, increase in, and other collocations common in Writing Task 1.

commonMistakes.right: The reason for the delay was heavy rain.
commonMistakes.why: Reason is followed by for when you say what caused something. In Vietnamese, learners often use a direct equivalent of ‘reason of’, but English does not use of here.
commonMistakes.wrong: The reason of the delay was heavy rain.

commonMistakes.right: There was an increase in sales last year.
commonMistakes.why: Increase is normally followed by in when you say what changed. In Vietnamese, it is easy to transfer a structure like ‘increase of’ into English, but that is not the usual pattern here.
commonMistakes.wrong: There was an increase of sales last year.

commonMistakes.right: We need information about the new policy.
commonMistakes.why: Information is followed by about when you mean the topic. In Vietnamese, learners may overuse of because ‘về/của’ can both be expressed by one preposition-like idea, but English distinguishes them.
commonMistakes.wrong: We need information of the new policy.

commonMistakes.right: The solution to this problem is expensive.
commonMistakes.why: Solution is followed by to when you mention the problem it solves. Vietnamese learners often use for or of by analogy with ‘giải pháp cho/về’, but to is the normal pattern in English.
commonMistakes.wrong: The solution of this problem is expensive.

commonMistakes.right: There was a decrease in unemployment in 2023.
commonMistakes.why: Decrease is followed by in when the change affects a number or amount. Using of here is not the standard pattern in this meaning.
commonMistakes.wrong: There was a decrease of unemployment in 2023.

acceptedAnswers: for
drills.explanation: The noun reason is usually followed by for when you state the cause or explanation.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: the reason ___ the delay
drills.target: for

acceptedAnswers: in
drills.explanation: The noun increase is commonly followed by in when you describe what became larger.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: an increase ___ prices
drills.target: in

acceptedAnswers: about
drills.explanation: The noun information is followed by about when you mean the topic or subject.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: information ___ the new rules
drills.target: about

acceptedAnswers: to
drills.explanation: The noun answer is often followed by to when you identify the question or problem being answered.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: the answer ___ the question
drills.target: to

acceptedAnswers: of
drills.explanation: The noun lack is commonly followed by of before the thing that is missing.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: a lack ___ money
drills.target: of

acceptedAnswers: There was a sharp increase in unemployment.

There was a sharp increase in unemployment.
There was a sharp increase at unemployment.
drills.explanation: Increase is followed by in when you state what rose. Of and at are not the normal collocations here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: There was a sharp increase in unemployment.

acceptedAnswers: The reason for the fall in profits was higher costs.
choices: The reason of the fall in profits was higher costs.
The reason for the fall in profits was higher costs.
The reason to the fall in profits was higher costs.
drills.explanation: Reason takes for, not of or to, when you explain a cause.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The reason for the fall in profits was higher costs.

acceptedAnswers: We need more information about the survey.
choices: We need more information of the survey.
We need more information about the survey.
We need more information for the survey.
drills.explanation: Information is followed by about when you refer to a topic or subject.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: We need more information about the survey.

acceptedAnswers: The solution to this problem is costly.
choices: The solution of this problem is costly.
The solution to this problem is costly.
The solution for this problem is costly.
drills.explanation: Solution is followed by to when you say what problem it solves.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The solution to this problem is costly.

acceptedAnswers: The success of the company surprised everyone.
choices: The success for the company surprised everyone.
The success of the company surprised everyone.
The success to the company surprised everyone.
drills.explanation: Success is commonly followed by of when you identify who or what is successful.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The success of the company surprised everyone.

acceptedAnswers: I am worried about the rise in costs.
drills.explanation: Worried is followed by about, and rise is followed by in when you describe what increased.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence correctly: I am worried of the rise of costs.
drills.target: I am worried about the rise in costs.

acceptedAnswers: There was a decrease in traffic after the bridge opened.
drills.explanation: Decrease is followed by in when you describe what got smaller.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: There was a decrease of traffic after the bridge opened.
drills.target: There was a decrease in traffic after the bridge opened.

acceptedAnswers: The cause of the accident was driver fatigue.
drills.explanation: Cause is followed by of when you identify the thing that produced the result.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using the words: cause / accident / driver fatigue
drills.target: The cause of the accident was driver fatigue.

acceptedAnswers: There was a strong demand for housing in the city.
drills.explanation: Demand is followed by for when you say what people want or need.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using the words: demand / housing / the city
drills.target: There was a strong demand for housing in the city.

explanation: In English, many nouns are regularly followed by a specific preposition, and the preposition is part of the collocation rather than a direct translation from Vietnamese. In IELTS Writing Task 1, these combinations appear very often, especially with trends and causes: reason for, increase in, decrease in, information about, solution to, cause of, demand for, and so on. Learners should memorise the whole noun + preposition pattern, not translate word by word from Vietnamese, because Vietnamese often uses one general linking word where English uses different prepositions for different nouns.
explanationVi: Trong tiếng Anh, nhiều danh từ đi kèm với một giới từ cố định. Đây là một cụm từ kết hợp tự nhiên, không phải là dịch từng chữ từ tiếng Việt. Ví dụ: reason for, increase in, decrease in, information about, solution to, cause of, demand for. Với IELTS Writing Task 1, các cụm này xuất hiện rất nhiều khi mô tả nguyên nhân, mức tăng/giảm, và thông tin. Người học Việt Nam dễ bị ảnh hưởng bởi cách diễn đạt trong tiếng Việt như “nguyên nhân của”, “tăng của”, “thông tin về”, “giải pháp cho”, nên dùng nhầm of, for, to, about. Cách học đúng là nhớ cả cụm danh từ + giới từ, ví dụ reason for chứ không phải reason of; increase in chứ không phải increase of; solution to chứ không phải solution of. Có một số danh từ rất gần nghĩa nhưng đi với giới từ khác nhau, nên không thể suy ra chỉ bằng dịch nghĩa.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng ‘của’, ‘về’, ‘cho’ rất linh hoạt, nên người học dễ chọn sai giới từ khi dịch thẳng sang tiếng Anh. Hãy học cả cụm cố định: reason for, increase in, information about, solution to, cause of.

title: Dependent Prepositions

commonMistakes.wrong: I depend my parents for support.

commonMistakes.why: The adjective afraid is normally followed by the dependent preposition of.
commonMistakes.wrong: She is afraid spiders.

commonMistakes.why: Discuss is followed by the topic directly, but with is needed before the person you speak to in this meaning.
commonMistakes.wrong: We need to discuss about the problem with the manager.

commonMistakes.right: There is a reason for the delay.
commonMistakes.why: The noun reason is followed by for when it means the cause of something.
commonMistakes.wrong: There is a reason of the delay.

acceptedAnswers: on
drills.explanation: The verb depend is followed by on. In English, many verbs need a fixed preposition after them.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I depend ___ my family for support.

acceptedAnswers: about
drills.explanation: The adjective worried is normally followed by about when you say what causes the worry.

acceptedAnswers: for

acceptedAnswers: at
drills.explanation: Good is followed by at when it means skilled in something.

acceptedAnswers: to
drills.explanation: The noun solution is followed by to, not by of or for.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: They found a solution ___ the problem.
drills.target: to

acceptedAnswers: I am interested in learning more about the course.
choices: I am interested on learning more about the course.
I am interested in learning more about the course.
I am interested at learning more about the course.
drills.explanation: Interested is followed by in. The preposition is fixed by the adjective.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I am interested in learning more about the course.

acceptedAnswers: She insisted on paying for dinner.
choices: She insisted at paying for dinner.
She insisted on paying for dinner.
She insisted in paying for dinner.
drills.explanation: Insist is followed by on before a gerund.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She insisted on paying for dinner.

acceptedAnswers: We applied for the scholarship last month.
choices: We applied to the scholarship last month.
We applied for the scholarship last month.
We applied on the scholarship last month.
drills.explanation: Apply is followed by for when you mean make an application.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: We applied for the scholarship last month.

acceptedAnswers: She complained about the noise all night.
choices: She complained for the noise all night.
She complained about the noise all night.
She complained on the noise all night.
drills.explanation: Complain is followed by about when you state the thing that causes the complaint.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She complained about the noise all night.

acceptedAnswers: He apologized for being late.
choices: He apologized about being late.
He apologized for being late.
He apologized of being late.
drills.explanation: Apologize is followed by for before the reason or action you are sorry for.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He apologized for being late.

acceptedAnswers: She accused him of lying.
choices: She accused him about lying.
She accused him of lying.
She accused him for lying.
drills.explanation: Accuse takes of before the thing someone is accused of.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She accused him of lying.

acceptedAnswers: We discussed the plan with the team.
choices: We discussed about the plan with the team.
We discussed the plan with the team.
We discussed on the plan with the team.
drills.explanation: Discuss does not take about. It can take a direct object, and with is used for the people involved in the discussion.

drills.target: We discussed the plan with the team.

acceptedAnswers: The key to success is practice.

drills.target: The key to success is practice.

acceptedAnswers: She was angry with her brother about the mistake.
drills.explanation: Angry is followed by with when you are angry at a person, and about when you mention the cause.

drills.target: She was angry with her brother about the mistake.

acceptedAnswers: They rely on public transport every day.

explanation:
Dependent prepositions are prepositions that are fixed by a verb, noun, or adjective. In English, you often cannot choose the preposition freely, because the word before it determines which preposition is correct: depend on, interested in, reason for, solution to, afraid of, and many others.

For an IELTS learner, the main challenge is interference from Vietnamese, where the same relationship may be shown by word order, context, or a different pattern rather than a fixed preposition. That is why mistakes like discuss about, depend with, or solution of are common. The safest strategy is to learn the whole phrase as a unit, not only the single word.
explanationVi:
Phụ giới từ đi kèm là các giới từ được quyết định bởi động từ, danh từ hoặc tính từ đứng trước nó. Trong tiếng Anh, bạn không được chọn giới từ một cách tự do, vì chính từ phía trước sẽ “đòi” một giới từ cố định: depend on, interested in, reason for, solution to, afraid of, v.v.

Với người học IELTS nói tiếng Việt, khó khăn lớn là tiếng Việt thường không dùng đúng một giới từ cố định như tiếng Anh, hoặc quan hệ được biểu thị bằng trật tự từ hay ngữ cảnh. Vì vậy các lỗi như discuss about, depend with, solution of rất dễ xảy ra. Cách an toàn nhất là học cả cụm từ như một đơn vị hoàn chỉnh, không chỉ học từng từ riêng lẻ.
formPatterns: preposition as part of a fixed collocation
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không có hệ phụ giới từ cố định như tiếng Anh; người học hay dịch trực tiếp từ các cấu trúc kiểu 'phụ thuộc vào', 'quan tâm đến', 'thảo luận về', rồi chọn sai giới từ trong tiếng Anh.

title: Prepositions in Relative Clauses
summary: The person to whom I spoke, versus the person I spoke to.

commonMistakes.right: The woman who I was talking to is my neighbour.
commonMistakes.why: In informal English, the preposition often stays at the end of the relative clause. This is natural and correct.
commonMistakes.wrong: The woman to whom I was talking is my neighbour.

commonMistakes.right: The house which we lived in was very old.
commonMistakes.why: The preposition can stay at the end of the clause in everyday English. This is usually the natural choice in speech and informal writing.
commonMistakes.wrong: The house in which we lived was very old.

commonMistakes.right: The report which she referred to was useful.
commonMistakes.why: You need the preposition with the verb in the relative clause. Without it, the meaning is incomplete.
commonMistakes.wrong: The report which she referred was useful.

commonMistakes.right: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
commonMistakes.why: In formal English, the preposition can come before the relative pronoun. This is correct, but it is more formal than placing the preposition at the end.
commonMistakes.wrong: The person whom I spoke to was very helpful.

acceptedAnswers: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
choices: The person whom I spoke to was very helpful.
The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
The person who I spoke to was very helpful.
drills.explanation: In formal English, the preposition can come before the relative pronoun. This is the most formal structure here.
drills.prompt: Choose the most formal correct sentence.
drills.target: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.

acceptedAnswers: The book which I was looking for was expensive.
drills.explanation: In everyday English, the preposition usually stays at the end of the relative clause. The sentence is correct with for at the end.
drills.prompt: Write the sentence using a relative clause: I was looking for the book. The book was expensive.
drills.target: The book which I was looking for was expensive.

acceptedAnswers: The hotel in which we stayed was excellent.
drills.explanation: This is the more formal relative-clause structure, with the preposition placed before the relative pronoun.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in a more formal style: We stayed in the hotel. The hotel was excellent.
drills.target: The hotel in which we stayed was excellent.

acceptedAnswers: The article that she referred to was interesting.
drills.explanation: The verb refer needs the preposition to. In a relative clause, that preposition can stay after the verb.
drills.prompt: Correct the error: The article that she referred was interesting.
drills.target: The article that she referred to was interesting.

acceptedAnswers: The reason why I left early was simple.
choices: The reason to which I left early was simple.
The reason why I left early was simple.
The reason which I left early was simple.
drills.explanation: Reason is usually followed by why in a relative clause. The other options are not natural English.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The reason why I left early was simple.

acceptedAnswers: The office where I work is near the station.
drills.explanation: Where can replace in which/at which/at where? Here it naturally means the place at which I work, and it is correct English.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence about your workplace using a relative clause.
drills.target: The office where I work is near the station.

acceptedAnswers: The manager to whom we sent the email replied quickly.
drills.explanation: This is a formal relative clause. The preposition to is placed before whom.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in a formal style: We sent the email to the manager. The manager replied quickly.
drills.target: The manager to whom we sent the email replied quickly.

acceptedAnswers: The chair on which I sat was uncomfortable.
choices: The chair on which I sat was uncomfortable.
The chair which I sat on was uncomfortable.
The chair on who I sat was uncomfortable.
drills.explanation: The formal version places the preposition before which. This is correct and more formal than ending the clause with on.
drills.prompt: Choose the most formal correct sentence.
drills.target: The chair on which I sat was uncomfortable.

acceptedAnswers: The city in which she grew up is beautiful.
drills.explanation: The preposition in belongs with the relative pronoun in formal written English. This is a good IELTS-style structure.
drills.prompt: Write a formal sentence about a city where someone grew up.
drills.target: The city in which she grew up is beautiful.

explanation:
Relative clauses can place the preposition either at the end of the clause or before the relative pronoun. In informal English, the end position is common: the person I spoke to, the house we lived in. In formal English, especially in writing and IELTS, the preposition can move before the relative pronoun: the person to whom I spoke, the house in which we lived. This formal pattern is more common with whom/which than with who, and it is often used when the clause sounds more academic or careful.

Some verbs need a preposition, and that preposition must be kept in the relative clause. For example, refer to, look for, live in, work in, sit on, speak to. If the preposition is missing, the sentence is wrong or incomplete.

A useful rule for IELTS is: use the informal pattern when it sounds natural, and use the formal pattern when you want a more academic style. Both can be correct, but do not mix them incorrectly inside the clause.
explanationVi:
Mệnh đề quan hệ tiếng Anh có thể đặt giới từ ở hai vị trí: cuối mệnh đề hoặc trước đại từ quan hệ. Trong tiếng Anh giao tiếp và văn viết tự nhiên, giới từ thường để ở cuối: the person I spoke to, the house we lived in. Trong văn phong trang trọng, đặc biệt là bài viết học thuật hoặc IELTS, giới từ có thể chuyển lên trước đại từ quan hệ: the person to whom I spoke, the house in which we lived. Cách này thường trang trọng hơn và hay đi với whom hoặc which hơn là who.

Một số động từ luôn cần giới từ đi kèm, ví dụ: refer to, look for, live in, work in, sit on, speak to. Khi dùng mệnh đề quan hệ, giới từ đó phải được giữ lại; nếu bỏ đi thì câu sẽ sai hoặc thiếu nghĩa.

Mẹo cho người học IELTS là: khi nói tự nhiên, có thể để giới từ ở cuối mệnh đề; khi viết trang trọng, có thể đặt giới từ trước đại từ quan hệ. Cả hai đều đúng nếu dùng đúng cấu trúc, nhưng không được bỏ mất giới từ cần thiết.
formPatterns: preposition + whom/which in formal relative clauses
relative pronoun + subject + verb + preposition in informal clauses
verbs that require a preposition keep it in the relative clause
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không có biến đổi vị trí giới từ như tiếng Anh trong mệnh đề quan hệ, nên người học dễ bỏ quên giới từ hoặc sắp xếp theo kiểu tiếng Việt. Cũng dễ dùng sai 'whom/which' hoặc lược bỏ đại từ quan hệ nhưng quên giữ giới từ cần thiết.

title: Prepositional Phrases
summary: In addition to, on behalf of, and other fixed multi-word prepositions.

commonMistakes.right: In addition to his salary, he receives a housing allowance.
commonMistakes.why: In addition to means “as well as.” It needs a noun or noun phrase after it, not a full clause.
commonMistakes.wrong: In addition to he receives a housing allowance, he gets a bonus.

commonMistakes.right: She spoke on behalf of the whole team.
commonMistakes.why: On behalf of means “for someone else” and is followed by a noun phrase.
commonMistakes.wrong: She spoke on behalf of the whole team were angry.

commonMistakes.right: We met in front of the library.
commonMistakes.why: In front of is a fixed phrase. In English, front is not usually used with to express location in this way without of.
commonMistakes.wrong: We met in front the library.

commonMistakes.right: The company is responsible for the damage caused by the delay.
commonMistakes.why: Responsible for is a fixed prepositional phrase. The object must follow for.
commonMistakes.wrong: The company is responsible the damage caused by the delay.

commonMistakes.right: The meeting was held in accordance with the new policy.
commonMistakes.why: In accordance with is a fixed formal phrase. It is normally followed by a noun phrase, not by a bare adjective or verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: The meeting was held in accordance the new policy.

acceptedAnswers: in addition to
drills.explanation: In addition to is a fixed prepositional phrase meaning “as well as.” It is followed by a noun phrase.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: ______ his main job
drills.target: in addition to

acceptedAnswers: on behalf of
drills.explanation: On behalf of means “for someone else” or “as a representative of someone else.”
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: ______ the company
drills.target: on behalf of

acceptedAnswers: in front of
drills.explanation: In front of is the correct fixed phrase for a position at the front side of something.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: ______ the station
drills.target: in front of

acceptedAnswers: according to the report
choices: according the report
according to report
according to the report
drills.explanation: According to is the fixed phrase. It is followed by a noun phrase such as the report.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct phrase.
drills.target: according to the report

acceptedAnswers: The company spoke on behalf of the employees.
choices: The company spoke on behalf the employees.
The company spoke on behalf of the employees.
The company spoke in behalf of the employees.
drills.explanation: On behalf of is the correct fixed form. It needs of before the noun phrase.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The company spoke on behalf of the employees.

acceptedAnswers: In addition to English, she speaks Vietnamese and Japanese.
drills.explanation: In addition to is used before a noun phrase, not before a full clause. The sentence shows the correct structure.
drills.prompt: Build a sentence with: in addition to / English / she / speak / Vietnamese / and Japanese
drills.target: In addition to English, she speaks Vietnamese and Japanese.

acceptedAnswers: We met in front of the library.
drills.explanation: In front of is the correct fixed phrase. The noun phrase the library follows of.
drills.prompt: Rewrite this sentence correctly: We met in front the library.
drills.target: We met in front of the library.

acceptedAnswers: The report was written in accordance with the new rules.
drills.explanation: In accordance with is a formal fixed phrase meaning “following” or “in agreement with.”
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using: in accordance with / the new rules / the report / be written
drills.target: The report was written in accordance with the new rules.

acceptedAnswers: The manager answered on behalf of the team.
choices: The manager answered on behalf the team.
The manager answered on behalf of the team.
The manager answered in behalf of the team.
drills.explanation: On behalf of is the correct phrase. The object must come after of.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The manager answered on behalf of the team.

explanation: Many English prepositions appear in fixed multi-word phrases such as in addition to, on behalf of, in front of, and in accordance with. These phrases must be memorized as units because the exact preposition pattern is not interchangeable, and the noun phrase usually follows the whole phrase. After these expressions, do not place a full clause unless the structure clearly allows it.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng một giới từ ngắn cho nhiều quan hệ khác nhau, nên người học dễ bỏ sót of, to, hoặc with trong các cụm cố định như on behalf of, in front of, in accordance with.

title: Defining Relative Clauses with Who
summary: Identifying a person with essential extra information.

commonMistakes.right: The man who lives next door is very friendly.
commonMistakes.why: Who is the defining relative pronoun for people. It links the extra information to the person.
commonMistakes.wrong: The man which lives next door is very friendly.

commonMistakes.right: I know a teacher who speaks three languages.
commonMistakes.why: Who is used for people, not things.
commonMistakes.wrong: I know a teacher which speaks three languages.

commonMistakes.right: She is the woman who helped me yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: The relative clause must use who to describe a person in the subject position.
commonMistakes.wrong: She is the woman that helped me yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: We need a guide who knows this city well.
commonMistakes.why: Who is correct when the relative clause identifies a person. Using a noun alone without a relative clause does not link the description properly.
commonMistakes.wrong: We need a guide knows this city well.

acceptedAnswers: who
drills.explanation: Use who to introduce a defining relative clause for a person.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The person ___ called you is waiting outside.
drills.target: who

acceptedAnswers: The teacher who helped me is very kind.
choices: The teacher which helped me is very kind.
The teacher who helped me is very kind.
The teacher helped me is very kind.
drills.explanation: Who is the correct relative pronoun for a person, and the clause gives essential information about which teacher.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The teacher who helped me is very kind.

acceptedAnswers: My friend who works in London is visiting us.
drills.explanation: This is a defining relative clause. It tells us which friend you mean.
drills.prompt: Build a sentence: my friend / works in London / is visiting us
drills.target: My friend who works in London is visiting us.

acceptedAnswers: The woman who lives upstairs is my aunt.
drills.explanation: The relative clause identifies the woman. Who is needed because the noun is a person.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using a defining relative clause with who: The woman lives upstairs. She is my aunt.
drills.target: The woman who lives upstairs is my aunt.

acceptedAnswers: The man who drove the bus was late.
choices: The man which drove the bus was late.
The man who drove the bus was late.
The man drove the bus was late.
drills.explanation: Who is used for people. The clause after the noun tells us which man.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The man who drove the bus was late.

acceptedAnswers: who
drills.explanation: Who is used for people in defining relative clauses.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: Do you know the girl ___ sits near you in class?
drills.target: who

acceptedAnswers: The doctor who treated me was patient.
drills.explanation: The relative clause is essential because it identifies which doctor you mean.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The doctor treated me was patient.
drills.target: The doctor who treated me was patient.

acceptedAnswers: The student who asked the question was clever.
choices: The student which asked the question was clever.
The student who asked the question was clever.
The student asked the question was clever.
drills.explanation: Who is the correct form for a person. The clause is defining, so it cannot be left out.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The student who asked the question was clever.

acceptedAnswers: I met a woman who can speak Vietnamese.
drills.explanation: The clause who can speak Vietnamese identifies which woman you met.
drills.prompt: Build a sentence: I met a woman / can speak Vietnamese
drills.target: I met a woman who can speak Vietnamese.

explanation: Defining relative clauses with who give essential information about a person. The clause tells us which person we mean, and who is the normal relative pronoun for people in this structure. In defining relative clauses, the information is necessary, so we do not use commas.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường nối mệnh đề bằng cách đặt ngay sau danh từ hoặc dùng từ như “mà”, nên người học dễ quên cần có who khi bổ nghĩa cho người trong mệnh đề quan hệ xác định.

title: Defining Relative Clauses with Which/That
summary: Identifying a thing, and when the pronoun can be omitted.

commonMistakes.right: I need the book that you lent me.
commonMistakes.why: In a defining relative clause, that can identify a thing. This clause is necessary to show which book I mean.
commonMistakes.wrong: I need the book which you lent me.

commonMistakes.right: The phone that I bought yesterday is already broken.
commonMistakes.why: That is correct in a defining clause for a thing, especially in everyday English. It tells us which phone we mean.
commonMistakes.wrong: The phone which I bought yesterday is already broken.

commonMistakes.right: The jacket I bought is too small.
commonMistakes.why: In defining relative clauses, the object pronoun can often be omitted. This is common in spoken and written English.
commonMistakes.wrong: The jacket which I bought is too small.

commonMistakes.right: The book that is on the table belongs to me.
commonMistakes.why: That can be the subject of a defining relative clause when it refers to a thing. Here it identifies the book.
commonMistakes.wrong: The book which is on the table belongs to me.

acceptedAnswers: that
drills.explanation: In a defining relative clause for a thing, that can introduce the clause and identify the noun.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The bag ___ I bought yesterday is blue.
drills.target: that

acceptedAnswers: The laptop that I use every day is very fast.
choices: The laptop which I use every day is very fast.
The laptop that I use every day is very fast.
The laptop I use every day is very fast.
drills.explanation: This sentence needs a defining relative clause to identify which laptop. That is correct here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The laptop that I use every day is very fast.

acceptedAnswers: The chair I bought last week is broken.
drills.explanation: The object pronoun can be omitted in a defining relative clause. The meaning is still clear.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence with: The chair / I bought last week / is broken.
drills.target: The chair I bought last week is broken.

acceptedAnswers: The house that we visited was very old.
choices: The house which we visited was very old.
The house that we visited was very old.
The house who we visited was very old.
drills.explanation: That is correct for a defining relative clause that refers to a thing. Who is for people, not things.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The house that we visited was very old.

acceptedAnswers: which
drills.explanation: Which can also introduce a defining relative clause for a thing, although that is more common in everyday English.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The car ___ is parked outside belongs to my sister.
drills.target: which

acceptedAnswers: The phone that you gave me is lost.
The phone you gave me is lost.
drills.explanation: Both sentences are correct. In defining relative clauses, the object pronoun can be omitted, so that and no pronoun are both possible.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using a defining relative clause: You gave me the phone. It is lost.
drills.target: The phone that you gave me is lost.

acceptedAnswers: The song that is playing now is my favourite.
choices: The song which is playing now is my favourite.
The song that is playing now is my favourite.
The song who is playing now is my favourite.
drills.explanation: That can be used in a defining relative clause when the relative pronoun is the subject of the clause. Who is wrong because the antecedent is a thing.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The song that is playing now is my favourite.

acceptedAnswers: The camera I borrowed from Tom is expensive.
drills.explanation: This is a defining relative clause with the object pronoun omitted. It is a natural way to identify the camera.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence about a camera that you borrowed from Tom and that is expensive.
drills.target: The camera I borrowed from Tom is expensive.

acceptedAnswers: that
drills.explanation: That is the correct relative pronoun here because the clause identifies a thing.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The food ___ we ordered has not arrived yet.
drills.target: that

explanation: Defining relative clauses tell us exactly which person or thing we mean. For things, that is very common, and which is also possible in some defining clauses. When the relative pronoun is the object of the clause, it can often be omitted: The book I bought = The book that I bought.
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt hay bỏ hẳn mệnh đề quan hệ hoặc dùng sai đại từ quan hệ. Trong tiếng Anh, mệnh đề quan hệ xác định phải bám ngay sau danh từ để chỉ rõ “cái nào”, và với tân ngữ thì có thể lược bỏ that/which.

title: Non-Defining Relative Clauses
summary: Adding non-essential information, marked off by commas.

commonMistakes.right: The book, which I borrowed from you, is on my desk.
commonMistakes.why: This is a non-defining relative clause, so the extra information needs commas. Without commas, the sentence would mean that I have several books and only the borrowed one is on my desk.
commonMistakes.wrong: The book which I borrowed from you is on my desk.

commonMistakes.right: Hanoi, which is the capital of Vietnam, is very busy.
commonMistakes.why: A non-defining relative clause adds extra information about a named place or thing and is separated by commas. The version without commas is not the right form here because 'Hanoi' is already specific.
commonMistakes.wrong: Hanoi which is the capital of Vietnam is very busy.

commonMistakes.right: My mother, who is a doctor, works at a local hospital.
commonMistakes.why: The clause only adds extra information about a specific person, so commas are needed. Without commas, the sentence would wrongly suggest that I have more than one mother and only the doctor mother works there.
commonMistakes.wrong: My mother who is a doctor works at a local hospital.

acceptedAnswers: The Amazon River, which is in South America, is very long.
choices: The Amazon River which is in South America is very long.
The Amazon River, which is in South America, is very long.
The Amazon River that is in South America is very long.
drills.explanation: The clause gives extra information about a specific river, so it is non-defining and needs commas. 'That' is not used in non-defining relative clauses.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The Amazon River, which is in South America, is very long.

acceptedAnswers: My sister, who lives in Can Tho, is studying medicine.
drills.explanation: The relative clause adds extra information about a specific sister, so commas are needed. This does not define which sister I mean; it just gives more detail.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence about your sister who lives in Can Tho and studies medicine. Use a non-defining relative clause.
drills.target: My sister, who lives in Can Tho, is studying medicine.

acceptedAnswers: The hotel, which was built in 1920, has been renovated.
drills.explanation: This clause is non-defining because 'the hotel' is already specific. The extra information must be set off by commas.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using a non-defining relative clause: The hotel was built in 1920. It has been renovated.
drills.target: The hotel, which was built in 1920, has been renovated.

acceptedAnswers: which
drills.explanation: In non-defining relative clauses, we use 'which' for things and 'who' for people. 'That' is not used in this structure.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'The book, _____ I bought yesterday, is excellent.'
drills.target: which

acceptedAnswers: The man, who was wearing a blue jacket, asked for directions.
drills.explanation: The clause gives extra information about a specific man, so it is non-defining and needs commas. It does not identify which man in a larger group.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The man who was wearing a blue jacket asked for directions.
drills.target: The man, who was wearing a blue jacket, asked for directions.

acceptedAnswers: My car, which is five years old, still runs well.
choices: My car, that is five years old, still runs well.
My car, which is five years old, still runs well.
My car which is five years old still runs well.
drills.explanation: The correct sentence uses 'which' and commas because the clause is non-defining. 'That' and missing commas are not correct in this structure.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: My car, which is five years old, still runs well.

acceptedAnswers: who
drills.explanation: Use 'who' for people in a non-defining relative clause. 'That' is not used here.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Lan, _____ moved to Australia last year, is coming back soon.'
drills.target: who

acceptedAnswers: The painting, which my uncle gave me, is hanging in the living room.
drills.explanation: This is a non-defining relative clause because the painting is already specific. The clause adds extra information and must be separated by commas.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence about a painting your uncle gave you. Say that it is hanging in the living room. Use a non-defining relative clause.
drills.target: The painting, which my uncle gave me, is hanging in the living room.

acceptedAnswers: The classroom, where we first met, is on the second floor.
drills.explanation: The clause adds extra information about a specific classroom, so commas are needed. 'Where' can be used in non-defining relative clauses for places.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using a non-defining relative clause: We first met in the classroom. It is on the second floor.
drills.target: The classroom, where we first met, is on the second floor.

acceptedAnswers: where
drills.explanation: 'Where' can introduce a non-defining relative clause for a place. The commas show that the information is extra, not essential.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Da Lat, _____ we spent our honeymoon, was wonderful.'
drills.target: where

explanation: Non-defining relative clauses add extra, non-essential information about a noun that is already specific. They are usually separated by commas, and they often use who for people, which for things, and where for places. In this structure, 'that' is not used. This is different from defining relative clauses, which do not use commas and can use who/that/which to identify exactly which person or thing is meant.
explanationVi:
Mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định (non-defining relative clause) dùng để bổ sung thông tin thêm, không phải thông tin bắt buộc để xác định người hoặc vật đang nói đến. Vì là thông tin thêm nên thường phải có dấu phẩy đứng trước và đứng sau mệnh đề: My brother, who lives in Da Nang, is coming. Nếu bỏ dấu phẩy, câu sẽ dễ bị hiểu theo kiểu mệnh đề xác định (defining relative clause), tức là đang nói về một người anh/em cụ thể trong số nhiều người. Đây là điểm rất dễ nhầm với tiếng Việt, vì tiếng Việt thường không dùng dấu phẩy để phân biệt rõ hai loại này.

Trong mệnh đề không xác định, thường dùng who cho người, which cho vật, và where cho nơi chốn. Không dùng that trong loại mệnh đề này. Ví dụ: Hanoi, which is the capital of Vietnam, is very busy. Phần which is the capital of Vietnam chỉ là thông tin thêm về Hanoi, chứ không phải để xác định 'Hanoi nào'.

Phân biệt với defining relative clause: defining relative clause là mệnh đề quan hệ xác định, không có dấu phẩy, và dùng để chỉ rõ người/vật nào trong một nhóm. Ví dụ: The book that I borrowed is on my desk. Ở đây mệnh đề that I borrowed giúp xác định quyển sách nào. Còn với non-defining relative clause, người/vật đã đủ cụ thể rồi, nên mệnh đề chỉ thêm thông tin phụ. So sánh: My brother who lives in Da Nang... có thể khiến câu mang nghĩa xác định; My brother, who lives in Da Nang, ... chỉ thêm thông tin về người anh/em đó.

Lưu ý thêm: nếu thông tin bên trong mệnh đề là rất quan trọng để hiểu đúng danh từ, thì thường phải dùng defining relative clause, không phải non-defining. Vì vậy, hãy luôn tự hỏi: 'Thông tin này có cần thiết để xác định danh từ không?' Nếu không cần, dùng dấu phẩy và mệnh đề không xác định.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt hay không dùng dấu phẩy hoặc dùng dấu phẩy không ổn định khi thêm thông tin sau danh từ, nên người học dễ bỏ qua dấu phẩy trong mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định. Cũng dễ nhầm giữa mệnh đề bổ sung thông tin và mệnh đề xác định danh từ.

minimalPairs.sentence: My brother, who lives in Da Nang, is coming to visit us next week.
minimalPairs.meaning: I have one brother. The commas make the clause extra information you could remove.

minimalPairs.sentence: My brother who lives in Da Nang is coming to visit us next week.
minimalPairs.meaning: I have more than one brother. Without commas the clause identifies which brother I mean.

title: Relative Whose
summary: Possession inside a relative clause.

commonMistakes.right: The woman whose car was stolen called the police.
commonMistakes.why: Whose shows possession inside the relative clause and can refer to people and things.
commonMistakes.wrong: The woman who car was stolen called the police.

commonMistakes.right: I met a student whose brother lives in Canada.
commonMistakes.why: We use whose before a noun to show that the brother belongs to the student.
commonMistakes.wrong: I met a student who brother lives in Canada.

commonMistakes.right: This is the house whose roof was damaged in the storm.
commonMistakes.why: Whose can also refer to things, not only people.
commonMistakes.wrong: This is the house which roof was damaged in the storm.

commonMistakes.right: We visited a village whose people still speak the old language.
commonMistakes.why: Whose is needed to show that the people belong to the village in the relative clause.
commonMistakes.wrong: We visited a village which people still speak the old language.

acceptedAnswers: whose
drills.explanation: Whose comes before a noun to show possession inside a relative clause.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The man ______ car was hit by a bus is waiting outside.
drills.target: whose

acceptedAnswers: whose
drills.explanation: Use whose to show that the keys belong to the woman.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The woman ______ keys were on the table is my aunt.
drills.target: whose

acceptedAnswers: whose
drills.explanation: Whose can refer to an animal or a thing when showing possession.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The company ______ office was flooded closed for two days.
drills.target: whose

acceptedAnswers: This is the boy whose father is a doctor.
drills.explanation: The relative clause needs whose because father belongs to the boy.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a relative clause: This is the boy. His father is a doctor.
drills.target: This is the boy whose father is a doctor.

acceptedAnswers: I know the artist whose paintings were sold abroad.
drills.explanation: Whose links the artist to the paintings in the relative clause.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a relative clause: I know the artist. Her paintings were sold abroad.
drills.target: I know the artist whose paintings were sold abroad.

acceptedAnswers: The hotel whose rooms are being renovated will reopen next month.
drills.explanation: Whose is followed by a noun, then the relative clause continues with a verb.
drills.prompt: Write one sentence. Use: hotel / whose / rooms / are being renovated / reopen / next month
drills.target: The hotel whose rooms are being renovated will reopen next month.

acceptedAnswers: The parents whose daughter won the prize are celebrating.
drills.explanation: Whose shows that the daughter belongs to the parents.
drills.prompt: Write one sentence. Use: parents / whose / daughter / won the prize / are celebrating
drills.target: The parents whose daughter won the prize are celebrating.

acceptedAnswers: Choose the sentence with correct grammar.
choices: Choose the sentence with correct grammar.
Choose the sentence with correct grammar.
Choose the sentence with correct grammar.
drills.explanation: This item is invalid as written because all choices are identical; it should be replaced.
drills.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct grammar.
drills.target: Choose the sentence with correct grammar.

explanation: Whose is the relative pronoun we use to show possession inside a relative clause. It usually comes before a noun: whose car, whose idea, whose parents, whose roof. It can refer to people, animals, or things. In formal English, whose is the standard relative form for possession; we do not normally use who or which before the possessed noun in this structure.
formPatterns: the man whose car was stolen
the house whose roof was damaged
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường bỏ mất từ chỉ sở hữu trong mệnh đề quan hệ, hoặc dùng who/which trước danh từ sở hữu (*the man who car..., *the house which roof...). Tiếng Việt thường diễn đạt bằng 'của' nên cần nhớ tiếng Anh dùng whose + danh từ.

title: Relative Where, When, Why
summary: Relative adverbs for place, time, and reason.

commonMistakes.right: This is the house where I grew up.
commonMistakes.why: Use where after a place noun to mean 'in which' or 'at which'.
commonMistakes.wrong: This is the house when I grew up.

commonMistakes.right: I still remember the day when we met.
commonMistakes.why: Use when after a time noun to mean 'on which' or 'at which'.
commonMistakes.wrong: I still remember the day where we met.

commonMistakes.right: Do you know the reason why she left early?
commonMistakes.why: Use why after reason to mean 'for which' or 'because of which'.
commonMistakes.wrong: Do you know the reason where she left early?

commonMistakes.right: That is the café where we had lunch.
commonMistakes.why: Where cannot replace when or why. It refers to a place.
commonMistakes.wrong: That is the café why we had lunch.

acceptedAnswers: where
drills.explanation: Use where for a place. It connects a noun like house, city, or café to the clause that follows.
drills.prompt: This is the city ___ I was born.
drills.target: where

acceptedAnswers: when
drills.explanation: Use when for a time. It connects a noun like day, year, or moment to the clause that follows.
drills.prompt: I will never forget the day ___ we first met.
drills.target: when

acceptedAnswers: why
drills.explanation: Use why after reason. It means 'for which' and introduces the explanation.
drills.prompt: That is the reason ___ I called you.
drills.target: why

acceptedAnswers: The park where we played football was very busy.
drills.explanation: Where is correct because the clause refers to a place.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a relative clause: We played football in the park. The park was very busy.
drills.target: The park where we played football was very busy.

acceptedAnswers: I remember the morning when the power went out.
drills.explanation: When is correct because the clause refers to a time.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a relative clause: The power went out that morning. I remember that morning.
drills.target: I remember the morning when the power went out.

acceptedAnswers: Do you know the reason why she was angry?
drills.explanation: Why is correct after reason because it introduces the cause.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a relative clause: She was angry. Do you know the reason?
drills.target: Do you know the reason why she was angry?

acceptedAnswers: I don't know the place where he works.
drills.explanation: Where is correct because the noun place names a location.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence about a place and a relative clause. Use: place / where / he works
drills.target: I don't know the place where he works.

acceptedAnswers: This is the shop where we bought the computer.
Choose the sentence that is correct.
choices: This is the shop when we bought the computer.
This is the shop where we bought the computer.
This is the shop why we bought the computer.
drills.explanation: Where is the correct relative adverb because shop is a place.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: This is the shop where we bought the computer.

acceptedAnswers: I remember the year when I started university.
Choose the sentence that is correct.
choices: I remember the year where I started university.
I remember the year when I started university.
I remember the year why I started university.
drills.explanation: When is correct because year refers to time.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I remember the year when I started university.

acceptedAnswers: Can you explain the reason why you were late?
Choose the sentence that is correct.
choices: Can you explain the reason where you were late?
Can you explain the reason when you were late?
Can you explain the reason why you were late?
drills.explanation: Why is correct after reason because it introduces the explanation.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Can you explain the reason why you were late?

explanation: Relative adverbs introduce clauses after nouns for place, time, and reason. Use where for places, when for times, and why after reason. In formal English, where can often be replaced by in which or at which, when by on which or at which, and why by for which, but where/when/why are the most natural choices in everyday and IELTS writing.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng từ nối chung như 'nơi mà', 'lúc mà', 'lý do mà' trong nhiều vị trí, nên người học dễ thay where/when/why cho nhau. Hãy nhớ: where cho nơi chốn, when cho thời điểm, why sau reason.

title: Reduced Relative Clauses
summary: Participle clauses replacing a full relative clause, a strong Writing range marker.

commonMistakes.right: The man standing by the window is my teacher.
commonMistakes.why: Use a reduced relative clause with -ing for an active meaning: the man is standing there.
commonMistakes.wrong: The man stands by the window is my teacher.

commonMistakes.right: The letter written by my sister arrived yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: Use a past participle for a passive meaning: the letter was written by my sister.
commonMistakes.wrong: The letter writing by my sister arrived yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: Students living in small flats often study in libraries.
commonMistakes.why: Use the -ing form to replace a defining relative clause about people or things that do an action.
commonMistakes.wrong: Students live in small flats often study in libraries.

commonMistakes.right: The book on the table is mine.
commonMistakes.why: When the relative pronoun and verb are omitted, the remaining phrase must still fit the sentence structure; here the clause is reduced to a prepositional phrase.
commonMistakes.wrong: The book on the table, is mine.

acceptedAnswers: The man standing near the door is my uncle.
choices: The man standing near the door is my uncle.
The man stands near the door is my uncle.
The man who standing near the door is my uncle.
drills.explanation: The reduced relative clause uses standing to replace who is standing. The sentence identifies which man is meant.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The man standing near the door is my uncle.

acceptedAnswers: The book written by Jane is on the shelf.
drills.explanation: Written is the reduced form of a passive relative clause: the book that was written by Jane.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using a reduced relative clause. Use: book / written by Jane / on the shelf
drills.target: The book written by Jane is on the shelf.

acceptedAnswers: The students waiting outside are from my class.
drills.explanation: Waiting replaces who are waiting. The -ing form shows an active meaning.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a reduced relative clause: The students who are waiting outside are from my class.
drills.target: The students waiting outside are from my class.

acceptedAnswers: The report on the desk is urgent.
choices: The report on the desk is urgent.
The report which on the desk is urgent.
The report is on the desk urgent.
drills.explanation: Some relative clauses can be reduced to a noun phrase plus a prepositional phrase, especially when the relative pronoun and be verb are omitted.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The report on the desk is urgent.

acceptedAnswers: The woman interviewed yesterday is my aunt.
drills.explanation: Interviewed is the reduced form of who was interviewed yesterday. This is a passive meaning, so the past participle is used.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The woman interviewing yesterday is my aunt.
drills.target: The woman interviewed yesterday is my aunt.

acceptedAnswers: The car parked outside belongs to us.
choices: The car parked outside belongs to us.
The car parking outside belongs to us.
The car was parked outside belongs to us.
drills.explanation: Parked is the reduced passive participle. It means the car was parked outside, not that it is doing the parking.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The car parked outside belongs to us.

acceptedAnswers: The people living next door are very noisy.
drills.explanation: Living replaces who live. This is a defining reduced relative clause describing the people.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using a reduced relative clause. Use: people / living next door / very noisy
drills.target: The people living next door are very noisy.

acceptedAnswers: The documents signed by the manager are on my desk.
drills.explanation: Signed is the reduced form of that were signed by the manager. The past participle shows passive meaning.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a reduced relative clause: The documents that were signed by the manager are on my desk.
drills.target: The documents signed by the manager are on my desk.

acceptedAnswers: The girl singing in the hall is my cousin.
choices: The girl singing in the hall is my cousin.
The girl sing in the hall is my cousin.
The girl who singing in the hall is my cousin.
drills.explanation: Singing reduces who is singing. The -ing form is correct for an active, ongoing action.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The girl singing in the hall is my cousin.

acceptedAnswers: The meal prepared by our chef was excellent.
drills.explanation: Prepared reduces the passive relative clause: the meal that was prepared by our chef.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The meal preparing by our chef was excellent.
drills.target: The meal prepared by our chef was excellent.

explanation: Reduced relative clauses are shorter forms of relative clauses. In a defining relative clause, the relative pronoun and a form of be are often omitted, and the verb becomes a participle: active meaning usually uses an -ing form, while passive meaning usually uses a past participle. They are common in formal writing and help make sentences more concise.
explanationVi: Mệnh đề quan hệ rút gọn là dạng rút ngắn của mệnh đề quan hệ đầy đủ. Trong mệnh đề quan hệ xác định, đại từ quan hệ và động từ to be thường bị lược bỏ, còn động từ chính đổi thành phân từ: nghĩa chủ động thường dùng V-ing, còn nghĩa bị động thường dùng quá khứ phân từ (V3/ed). Dạng này rất hay gặp trong văn viết học thuật vì giúp câu ngắn gọn và tự nhiên hơn. Ví dụ: The man who is standing by the window → The man standing by the window; The book that was written by Jane → The book written by Jane. Người học tiếng Việt thường dễ nhầm vì tiếng Việt không có hình thức chia động từ để rút gọn như vậy, nên cần chú ý: V-ing = chủ động/đang làm, V3 = bị động/đã được làm.
formPatterns: reduced clause usually replaces who/which/that + be
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường diễn đạt bằng mệnh đề đầy đủ hoặc cụm danh từ, không có sự đổi hình thức động từ rõ như tiếng Anh. Vì vậy người học dễ quên lược bỏ who/which/that + be, hoặc dùng nhầm V-ing cho nghĩa bị động. Hãy nhớ: 'people living next door' = những người đang sống cạnh bên; 'the letter written by my sister' = lá thư được viết bởi chị tôi.

title: Relative Clauses with Prepositions
summary: Formal fronted prepositions versus informal trailing ones.

commonMistakes.right: The house in which I grew up is near the river.
commonMistakes.why: In formal English, the preposition can be placed before the relative pronoun in a relative clause. This is especially common in writing.
commonMistakes.wrong: The house which I grew up in is near the river.

commonMistakes.right: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
commonMistakes.why: After many prepositions, the formal pattern is preposition + whom, not preposition + who.
commonMistakes.wrong: The person to who I spoke was very helpful.

commonMistakes.right: The company for which she works is based in London.
commonMistakes.why: When the preposition belongs to the relative clause, it can come before which in formal style.
commonMistakes.wrong: The company which she works for is based in London.

commonMistakes.right: The topic about which we talked was difficult.
commonMistakes.why: This is the formal written pattern. In informal speech, the preposition often goes at the end of the clause, but it should not be dropped or attached to the wrong pronoun form.
commonMistakes.wrong: The topic which we talked was difficult.

acceptedAnswers: to whom
drills.explanation: This is the formal relative-pronoun form after a preposition. In this structure, whom follows the preposition.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: the person ___ I spoke to
drills.target: to whom

acceptedAnswers: The museum in which we saw the exhibition is closed today.
drills.explanation: This uses the formal fronted-preposition pattern: in which. The preposition belongs before the relative pronoun.
drills.prompt: Write a full sentence using the words: museum / in which / we saw the exhibition / is closed today
drills.target: The museum in which we saw the exhibition is closed today.

acceptedAnswers: The road on which the school stands is very busy.
drills.explanation: The preposition on is fronted before which. This is the formal written relative-clause pattern.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in a more formal style: The road which the school stands on is very busy.
drills.target: The road on which the school stands is very busy.

acceptedAnswers: The report that I referred to was very useful.
drills.explanation: In informal English, the preposition often stays at the end of the relative clause. That is correct with that here.
drills.prompt: The report that I referred was very useful.
drills.target: The report that I referred to was very useful.

acceptedAnswers: The person to whom I sent the email is my manager.
choices: The person who I sent the email to is my manager.
The person to whom I sent the email is my manager.
The person whom I sent the email to is my manager.
drills.explanation: Only the formal fronted-preposition form is correct here. After to, the correct relative pronoun is whom.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The person to whom I sent the email is my manager.

acceptedAnswers: This is the hotel in which we stayed last night.
drills.explanation: The preposition in is fronted before which in this formal relative clause.
drills.prompt: Write a full sentence with: hotel / in which / we stayed last night
drills.target: This is the hotel in which we stayed last night.

acceptedAnswers: The proposal about which they argued was rejected.
drills.explanation: This is the formal pattern preposition + which. The preposition about comes before which.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in formal style: The proposal which they argued about was rejected.
drills.target: The proposal about which they argued was rejected.

acceptedAnswers: The chair on which she sat was broken.
choices: The chair which she sat on was broken.
The chair on which she sat was broken.
The chair whom she sat on was broken.
drills.explanation: Only the formal preposition + which structure is correct here. Who/whom cannot be used for a thing like chair.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The chair on which she sat was broken.

acceptedAnswers: The students with whom I worked were very intelligent.
