drills.explanation: With formal relative clauses, the preposition can come before whom when referring to people.
drills.prompt: Write a full sentence using: students / with whom / I worked / were very intelligent
drills.target: The students with whom I worked were very intelligent.

explanation: Relative clauses with prepositions have two main patterns. In formal English, the preposition can come before the relative pronoun: the house in which I grew up, the person to whom I spoke, the company for which she works. This is common in writing and more formal speaking. When the preposition comes first, the pronoun is usually whom for people and which for things. However, in informal English, the preposition often stays at the end of the clause: the house which I grew up in, the person who I spoke to, the company which she works for. Both patterns can be correct, but the fronted-preposition form is more formal. Do not drop the preposition or use who after a fronted preposition. Also note that that is generally not used after a fronted preposition.
explanationVi: Mệnh đề quan hệ với giới từ có hai kiểu chính. Trong tiếng Anh trang trọng, giới từ có thể đứng trước đại từ quan hệ: the house in which I grew up, the person to whom I spoke, the company for which she works. Kiểu này rất hay gặp trong văn viết và trong bài IELTS khi cần giọng văn formal. Khi giới từ đứng trước, chúng ta thường dùng whom cho người và which cho vật/sự việc. Ví dụ: to whom, with whom, in which, on which. Trong tiếng Anh thân mật hơn, giới từ thường đứng ở cuối mệnh đề: the house which I grew up in, the person who I spoke to, the company which she works for. Cả hai kiểu đều đúng, nhưng kiểu đưa giới từ lên trước nghe trang trọng hơn. Người học tiếng Việt thường bị ảnh hưởng bởi cấu trúc dịch từng từ nên dễ bỏ giới từ, hoặc dùng sai who/whom, hoặc dùng that sau giới từ. Cần nhớ rằng sau giới từ đặt trước đại từ quan hệ, ta không dùng that.
formPatterns: informal relative pronoun + clause + trailing preposition
formal written style with fronted preposition
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường đặt giới từ/từ chỉ quan hệ ở vị trí khác hoặc lược bỏ hoàn toàn, nên người học dễ viết kiểu 'the place which I lived in' mà không biết có thể dùng 'the place in which I lived' trong văn trang trọng. Cũng hay nhầm who/whom vì tiếng Việt không có phân biệt tương đương rõ ràng.

title: Quantifier + Relative
summary: Both of which, many of whom, and similar formal constructions.

commonMistakes.right: The company hired ten engineers, many of whom had years of experience.
commonMistakes.why: Use a quantifier plus a relative pronoun to refer back to people in a formal way. The relative clause gives extra information about the noun before it.
commonMistakes.wrong: The company hired ten engineers, many of them had years of experience.

commonMistakes.right: I bought three books, one of which was a first edition.
commonMistakes.why: After a quantifier, use of which / of whom in a non-defining relative clause. The phrase refers back to one item from the group.
commonMistakes.wrong: I bought three books, one which was a first edition.

commonMistakes.right: She gave me two reasons, neither of which was convincing.
commonMistakes.why: Words like both, all, many, most, neither, none, some can be followed by of which / of whom when they refer back to a noun.
commonMistakes.wrong: She gave me two reasons, neither which was convincing.

commonMistakes.right: We discussed five proposals, the most important of which concerned cost.
commonMistakes.why: A quantifier can combine with a relative clause to identify one part of a larger group. The whole structure is formal and precise.
commonMistakes.wrong: We discussed five proposals, the most important which concerned cost.

acceptedAnswers: many of whom
drills.explanation: Use of whom after a quantifier when referring to people. Many of whom is the correct formal structure.
drills.prompt: The class included twelve international students, many ___ were preparing for IELTS.
drills.target: many of whom

acceptedAnswers: both of which
choices: both of which
both which
both of them
drills.explanation: After a quantifier, of which is needed in a non-defining relative clause. Both which is not grammatical here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct phrase.
drills.target: both of which

acceptedAnswers: the details of which were unclear
drills.explanation: This sentence needs a formal quantifier-plus-relative structure. Of which connects the noun details to the relative clause.
drills.prompt:
Rewrite the sentence using a quantifier + relative structure.
The report had several details. The details were unclear.
drills.target: the details of which were unclear

acceptedAnswers: We reviewed four contracts, two of which were expired.
drills.explanation: Two of which refers back to two items from the larger group. The structure is non-defining and adds extra information.
drills.prompt: Build one correct sentence from these words: We / reviewed / four contracts / two of which / were expired.
drills.target: We reviewed four contracts, two of which were expired.

acceptedAnswers: one of whom
drills.explanation: Use of whom because the pronoun refers to people. One of whom is a standard formal pattern.
drills.prompt: The committee interviewed three candidates, one ___ had already worked abroad.
drills.target: one of whom

acceptedAnswers: none of whom
choices: none of whom
none whom
none of them
drills.explanation: None of whom is the correct formal pattern when the relative clause refers to people. None whom is wrong.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct phrase.
drills.target: none of whom

acceptedAnswers: The research included six studies, all of which supported the conclusion.
drills.explanation: All of which is a formal way to refer back to several things in a non-defining relative clause. It makes the link between the studies and the conclusion clear.
drills.prompt:
Correct the sentence.
The research included six studies, all which supported the conclusion.
drills.target: The research included six studies, all of which supported the conclusion.

acceptedAnswers: many of whom
drills.explanation: The phrase needs the preposition of before whom. This is the standard form after a quantifier referring to people.
drills.prompt: Several employees left the company, many ___ had worked there for more than ten years.
drills.target: many of whom

acceptedAnswers: There were five applicants, none of whom met the required standard.
drills.explanation: None of whom is the correct relative structure after a quantifier referring to people. It is more formal than a simple pronoun.
drills.prompt: Build one correct sentence from these words: There were / five applicants / none of whom / met the required standard.
drills.target: There were five applicants, none of whom met the required standard.

examples.en: I met four doctors, three of whom were specialists.
examples.note: of whom refers back to people in the group.
examples.vi: Tôi đã gặp bốn bác sĩ, trong đó ba người là bác sĩ chuyên khoa.

examples.en: We examined six samples, none of which was contaminated.
examples.note: of which refers back to things in the group.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đã kiểm tra sáu mẫu, không mẫu nào trong số đó bị nhiễm bẩn.

explanation:
A quantifier + relative structure is a formal way to refer back to part of a group. The quantifier names how many or how much, and the relative pronoun connects that part to a non-defining clause: many of whom, two of which, none of whom, all of which, and similar forms. Use whom for people and which for things. This structure is common in writing, especially in IELTS Task 2 and academic-style sentences.

Remember the pattern: noun + comma + quantifier + of whom/of which + clause. The clause gives extra information, so it is usually non-defining and separated by commas. You cannot normally use just which or whom without of after the quantifier. For example: many of whom, one of which, both of whom, most of which.

In Vietnamese, this often corresponds to expressions like “trong đó,” “mà trong số đó,” or “có… trong đó…”. Learners may try to translate word by word and omit of, or use them as separate pronouns. English needs the fixed phrase of whom / of which in this formal pattern.
explanationVi:
Cấu trúc “quantifier + relative” là cách diễn đạt trang trọng để nói về một phần trong một nhóm. Lượng từ (quantifier) cho biết số lượng hoặc mức độ, còn đại từ quan hệ nối phần đó với mệnh đề bổ sung: many of whom, two of which, none of whom, all of which, v.v. Dùng whom cho người và which cho vật. Cấu trúc này rất hay gặp trong văn viết học thuật và bài IELTS, đặc biệt là Task 2.

Mẫu cơ bản là: danh từ + dấu phẩy + quantifier + of whom/of which + mệnh đề. Mệnh đề này là mệnh đề không xác định (non-defining), nên thường có dấu phẩy. Sau quantifier, bạn không thể chỉ dùng which hoặc whom một mình trong kiểu này; tiếng Anh cần có of: many of whom, one of which, both of whom, most of which.

Trong tiếng Việt, cấu trúc này thường tương đương với “trong đó”, “mà trong số đó”, hoặc “có… trong đó…”. Người học Việt Nam dễ dịch từng từ nên hay bỏ mất of, hoặc dùng đại từ quan hệ như một từ riêng rẽ. Hãy nhớ đây là một cụm cố định và trang trọng: of whom / of which.
formPatterns: noun + , + quantifier + of whom/of which + clause
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường lược bỏ of vì trong tiếng Việt có thể chỉ cần “trong đó/mà trong số đó”. Cần nhớ tiếng Anh dùng cụm cố định of whom / of which trong mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định.

title: Say vs Tell
summary: Which reporting verb takes an object, a persistent error source.

commonMistakes.right: She told me the answer.
commonMistakes.why: Tell needs a person or other object after it. Say does not take a direct object in this meaning.
commonMistakes.wrong: She said me the answer.

commonMistakes.right: He said that he was tired.
commonMistakes.why: Say is used to report words or a message. Tell needs an object, so this sentence cannot use tell here.
commonMistakes.wrong: He told that he was tired.

commonMistakes.right: Please say hello to your mother.
commonMistakes.why: Say can be followed by a message or by hello, but it cannot take a direct object like a person in this pattern.
commonMistakes.wrong: Please tell hello to your mother.

commonMistakes.right: The teacher told us to open our books.
commonMistakes.why: Tell can be followed by an object and then an infinitive. Say cannot take this structure.
commonMistakes.wrong: The teacher said us to open our books.

acceptedAnswers: She told me the truth.
choices: She said me the truth.
She told me the truth.
She said to me the truth.
drills.explanation: Tell is followed by an object such as me, us, or him. Say does not take a direct object here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She told me the truth.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he was busy.
choices: He told that he was busy.
He said that he was busy.
He told me that he was busy.
drills.explanation: Say is used to report a statement. Tell needs an object, so told that... is wrong.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He said that he was busy.

acceptedAnswers: Did you tell your teacher about the problem?
choices: Did you said your teacher about the problem?
Did you tell your teacher about the problem?
Did you say your teacher about the problem?
drills.explanation: Tell can take a person as the object, so tell your teacher is correct. Say cannot take a direct person object.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Did you tell your teacher about the problem?

acceptedAnswers: Say hello to your parents.
choices: Tell hello to your parents.
Say hello to your parents.
Say your parents hello.
drills.explanation: Say hello is a fixed pattern. Tell cannot be used with hello in this way.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Say hello to your parents.

acceptedAnswers: told
drills.explanation: Tell is used before an object: told me, told us, told him.
drills.prompt: She ___ me the news yesterday.
drills.target: told

acceptedAnswers: said
drills.explanation: Say is used for reporting a statement. It does not need a direct object here.
drills.prompt: He ___ that he was sorry.
drills.target: said

acceptedAnswers: told
drills.explanation: The structure tell someone to do something is correct. Say cannot be followed by an object and to-infinitive in this way.
drills.prompt: The manager ___ us to wait outside.
drills.target: told

acceptedAnswers: say
drills.explanation: The phrase is say hello. Say is correct here, not tell.
drills.prompt: Please ___ hello to your sister for me.
drills.target: say

acceptedAnswers: She told me to wait outside.
drills.explanation: Tell can be followed by an object and to + verb. That is the correct reporting pattern here.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with tell: She said to me, 'Wait outside.'
drills.target: She told me to wait outside.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he was late.
drills.explanation: Use say to report a statement. Tell is not correct without an object in this structure.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with say: He told us, 'I am late.'
drills.target: He said that he was late.

acceptedAnswers: Did she tell you the answer?
drills.explanation: Tell takes an object before the thing reported. This is the correct question form.
drills.prompt: Write a question using tell. Use: she / tell / you / the answer
drills.target: Did she tell you the answer?

acceptedAnswers: I said that I was hungry.
drills.explanation: Say is used to report a statement. It can be followed by that and a clause.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using say. Use: I / say / I / be hungry
drills.target: I said that I was hungry.

acceptedAnswers: The teacher told the students to sit down.
drills.explanation: Tell + object + to + verb is correct. Say cannot take this pattern.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using tell. Use: the teacher / tell / the students / sit down
drills.target: The teacher told the students to sit down.

acceptedAnswers: say
drills.explanation: When you report a statement without a direct object, use say.
drills.prompt: She ___ that she would call later.
drills.target: say

explanation: Say and tell both mean “report,” but they are used differently. Say is usually followed by the words that were spoken, often with that + clause, and it does not take a direct object. Tell is followed by a person or other object: tell me, tell us, tell him, and it can also be followed by to + verb, as in tell someone to do something. In reported speech, this difference is very important: He said that he was tired. / He told me that he was tired. Both are correct, but He told that he was tired is wrong because tell needs an object.
explanationVi: Trong tiếng Việt, “nói” có thể dùng rất linh hoạt nên người học dễ chuyển thẳng sang tiếng Anh và dùng say/tell lẫn lộn. Cần nhớ quy tắc chính: say thường đi với nội dung được nói ra, ví dụ say that..., say hello; còn tell phải có người nghe hoặc đối tượng theo sau, ví dụ tell me, tell us, tell him. Tell cũng dùng trong cấu trúc tell someone to do something: told me to wait, told us to leave. Lỗi rất phổ biến là viết said me hoặc told that. Hai cách này đều sai vì say không nhận tân ngữ trực tiếp, còn tell thì cần tân ngữ. Khi sửa, hãy tự hỏi: có “người” sau động từ không? Nếu có người nghe, thường dùng tell. Nếu chỉ là lời được kể lại, thường dùng say.
formPatterns: reported speech with say vs tell
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt dùng “nói” cho cả say và tell, nên người học hay viết sai kiểu said me hoặc told that. Hãy nhớ: tell cần tân ngữ người nghe; say thường không có tân ngữ trực tiếp.

title: Reported Statements
summary: Backshifting tense when reporting what someone said.

commonMistakes.right: She said that she was tired.
commonMistakes.why: In reported statements, the present tense often changes to a past tense after a past reporting verb like said.
commonMistakes.wrong: She said that she is tired.

commonMistakes.right: He told me that he was busy.
commonMistakes.why: After a past reporting verb, the verb usually moves one tense back in reported speech.
commonMistakes.wrong: He told me that he is busy.

commonMistakes.right: They said that they had finished the work.
commonMistakes.why: A past perfect form is often used to show that the finishing happened before the reporting time.
commonMistakes.wrong: They said that they finished the work.

commonMistakes.right: I said that I could help.
commonMistakes.why: Modal verbs often change in reported statements; can usually becomes could.
commonMistakes.wrong: I said that I can help.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he was busy.
choices: He said that he is busy.
He said that he was busy.
He says that he was busy.
drills.explanation: After the past reporting verb said, the present tense usually changes back to the past tense.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported statement: "I am busy."
drills.target: He said that he was busy.

acceptedAnswers: She said that she had finished her homework.
drills.explanation: Finished becomes had finished in reported speech because the action happened before the reporting moment.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as reported speech: She said, "I finished my homework."
drills.target: She said that she had finished her homework.

acceptedAnswers: They said that they were leaving.
drills.explanation: The present continuous usually changes to the past continuous in reported statements.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as reported speech: They said, "We are leaving."
drills.target: They said that they were leaving.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he could help me.
choices: He said that he can help me.
He said that he could help me.
He said that he helps me.
drills.explanation: Can usually changes to could when we report what someone said.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported statement: "I can help you."
drills.target: He said that he could help me.

acceptedAnswers: She said that she would call later.
drills.explanation: Will usually changes to would in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as reported speech: She said, "I will call later."
drills.target: She said that she would call later.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he had seen the doctor.
drills.explanation: For a past action already completed before the reporting time, English often uses past perfect in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as reported speech: He said, "I saw the doctor."
drills.target: He said that he had seen the doctor.

acceptedAnswers: She said that she was late.
drills.explanation: In reported statements, am/are usually change to was/were after a past reporting verb.
drills.prompt: Write the reported statement. Use: she / say / she / be / late
drills.target: She said that she was late.

acceptedAnswers: They said that they had a new car.
choices: They said that they had a new car.
They said that they have a new car.
They said that they were have a new car.
drills.explanation: The reporting verb is in the past, so have often changes to had in reported statements.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported statement: "We have a new car."
drills.target: They said that they had a new car.

acceptedAnswers: I told him that I was sorry.
drills.explanation: After a past reporting verb, am changes to was in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as reported speech: I told him, "I am sorry."
drills.target: I told him that I was sorry.

acceptedAnswers: The teacher said that the test was difficult.
drills.explanation: A present adjective or state usually changes to the past form in reported statements after said.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as reported speech: The teacher said, "The test is difficult."
drills.target: The teacher said that the test was difficult.

acceptedAnswers: My friend said that he wanted to go home.
drills.explanation: Want stays a main verb, but in reported speech it usually moves one tense back from wants to wanted.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as reported speech: My friend said, "I want to go home."
drills.target: My friend said that he wanted to go home.

acceptedAnswers: The girl said that she had lost her keys.
drills.explanation: Lost becomes had lost because the loss happened before the reporting time.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The girl said that she lost her keys.
drills.target: The girl said that she had lost her keys.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he was tired and wanted to rest.
drills.explanation: When one reported sentence contains two verbs, both usually backshift if needed.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as reported speech: He said, "I am tired and want to rest."
drills.target: He said that he was tired and wanted to rest.

acceptedAnswers: We said that we would meet them tomorrow.
drills.explanation: Will changes to would, while time words like tomorrow often stay the same in some contexts, but often change to the next day in real reporting. This drill keeps tomorrow as the given wording.
drills.prompt: Write the reported statement. Use: we / say / we / will / meet / them / tomorrow
drills.target: We said that we would meet them tomorrow.

explanation: Reported statements tell us what someone said without using their exact words. When the reporting verb is in the past, English usually moves the tense back one step: present becomes past, present continuous becomes past continuous, past becomes past perfect, and modals like can and will often become could and would. This change is called backshifting. The word that is common but optional in many sentences.
explanationVi: Câu tường thuật dùng để kể lại lời nói của người khác mà không lặp lại nguyên văn. Khi động từ tường thuật ở thì quá khứ, tiếng Anh thường lùi thì về một bậc: hiện tại thành quá khứ, hiện tại tiếp diễn thành quá khứ tiếp diễn, quá khứ thành quá khứ hoàn thành, và các động từ khuyết thiếu như can, will thường đổi thành could, would. Quy tắc này gọi là lùi thì (backshifting). Từ that thường được dùng nhưng nhiều trường hợp có thể bỏ đi trong văn nói và văn viết tự nhiên. Người học tiếng Việt hay bị ảnh hưởng vì tiếng Việt thường không đổi thì của động từ theo cách này; trong tiếng Việt, khi tường thuật ta hay chỉ đổi đại từ hoặc thêm từ như ‘rằng’, còn động từ vẫn giữ nguyên. Vì vậy, khi sang tiếng Anh, cần chú ý đổi thì của động từ chính theo mốc thời gian của lời tường thuật.
formPatterns: subject + said that + subject + backshifted verb
subject + told + object + that + subject + backshifted verb
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không lùi thì khi tường thuật. Ví dụ, tiếng Việt nói ‘Anh ấy nói rằng anh ấy mệt’ nhưng động từ ‘mệt’ không đổi hình thức; người học dễ viết ‘He said that he is tired’ thay vì ‘He said that he was tired’. Cũng dễ quên đổi ‘can/will’ thành ‘could/would’ và quên dùng ‘told + object’ khi cần người nghe cụ thể.

title: Reported Questions
summary: Dropping question word order and do-support when reporting.

commonMistakes.right: She asked where I lived.
commonMistakes.why: In reported questions, we use statement word order, not question word order. We also do not use do-support after the reporting verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: She asked where did I live.

commonMistakes.right: He wanted to know if she was coming.
commonMistakes.why: Yes/no reported questions usually use if or whether, not auxiliary inversion.
commonMistakes.wrong: He wanted to know was she coming.

commonMistakes.right: I asked what he had said.
commonMistakes.why: In a reported question about the past, the tense usually shifts back. The direct-question form is not kept.
commonMistakes.wrong: I asked what did he say.

commonMistakes.right: They asked me when the train left.
commonMistakes.why: After a reporting verb, the question becomes a statement, so the subject comes before the verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: They asked me when did the train leave.

acceptedAnswers: where he lived
drills.explanation: A reported question uses statement word order. The verb comes after the subject, not before it.
drills.prompt: Complete the reported question: She asked ______.
drills.target: where he lived

acceptedAnswers: if they were ready
drills.explanation: Yes/no questions are often reported with if or whether. The word order changes to a statement form.
drills.prompt: Complete the reported question: He asked ______.
drills.target: if they were ready

acceptedAnswers: what time the meeting started
drills.explanation: In reported questions, we keep the question word but use statement order. We do not use auxiliary inversion.
drills.prompt: Complete the reported question: She asked ______.
drills.target: what time the meeting started

acceptedAnswers: whether I had finished my homework
drills.explanation: Whether is correct in reported yes/no questions. The tense usually moves back one step in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Complete the reported question: My mother asked ______.
drills.target: whether I had finished my homework

acceptedAnswers: He asked me where I lived.
drills.explanation: The reported question becomes a statement. We use where + subject + verb, not where + auxiliary + subject.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a reported question: “Where do you live?” he asked me.
drills.target: He asked me where I lived.

acceptedAnswers: She asked if the store was open.
drills.explanation: For a yes/no question, reported speech often uses if. The question order changes to statement order.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a reported question: “Is the store open?” she asked.
drills.target: She asked if the store was open.

acceptedAnswers: They asked when the bus would arrive.
drills.explanation: In reported questions, the question word stays, but the sentence becomes a statement. Future meaning is often reported with would.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a reported question: “When will the bus arrive?” they asked.
drills.target: They asked when the bus would arrive.

acceptedAnswers: I asked him what he had done.
drills.explanation: Reported questions usually shift the tense back when the reporting verb is past. We do not keep direct-question word order.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a reported question: “What did you do?” I asked him.
drills.target: I asked him what he had done.

acceptedAnswers: She wanted to know where the keys were.
choices: She wanted to know where were the keys.
She wanted to know where the keys were.
She wanted to know where did the keys were.
drills.explanation: Only the sentence with statement word order is correct. The other choices keep question order, which is wrong in reported questions.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported question.
drills.target: She wanted to know where the keys were.

acceptedAnswers: He asked whether I could help him.
choices: He asked whether could I help him.
He asked whether I could help him.
He asked whether I can help him.
drills.explanation: Reported questions do not use inversion after whether. The modal also usually shifts back from can to could.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported question.
drills.target: He asked whether I could help him.

acceptedAnswers: She asked me why I was late.
choices: She asked me why was I late.
She asked me why I was late.
She asked me why I am late.
drills.explanation: The reported question uses statement order. We keep why, but we do not move the auxiliary before the subject.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported question.
drills.target: She asked me why I was late.

acceptedAnswers: I asked where the station was.
choices: I asked where was the station.
I asked where the station was.
I asked where is the station.
drills.explanation: In reported questions, the subject comes before the verb. The direct-question form is not used after asked.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported question.
drills.target: I asked where the station was.

acceptedAnswers: He asked what time the film started.
drills.explanation: This is the correct full reported question. The original question word remains, but the sentence becomes a statement.
drills.prompt: Build a correct reported question using these words: He / ask / what time / the film / start
drills.target: He asked what time the film started.

acceptedAnswers: They wanted to know if the flight was delayed.
drills.explanation: For a reported yes/no question, use if or whether and statement word order. The past tense is natural here.
drills.prompt: Build a correct reported question using these words: They / want to know / if / the flight / be delayed
drills.target: They wanted to know if the flight was delayed.

explanation:
Reported questions are questions that we say indirectly. In English, the structure changes from question form to statement form: subject before verb, no do-support, and often a backshift in tense when the reporting verb is in the past. For yes/no questions, we usually use if or whether. For wh-questions, we keep the question word such as what, where, when, why, or how, but we still use statement word order after it.

Example: “Where do you live?” → She asked where I lived.
Example: “Did you finish?” → He asked if I had finished.

A very common mistake is to keep direct-question word order after ask, want to know, wonder, or tell me. That is wrong in reported questions. Another common mistake is to add do, does, or did in the reported clause. We do not do that.

The tense usually shifts back in past reporting, but not always. If the situation is still true now, the tense may stay the same in natural English. In exams, however, the safest pattern is to learn the normal backshift first.
explanationVi:
Câu hỏi gián tiếp (reported questions) là cách tường thuật lại một câu hỏi mà không giữ nguyên hình thức câu hỏi trực tiếp. Điểm quan trọng nhất là: sau động từ tường thuật như ask, wonder, want to know, câu bên trong phải đổi sang dạng câu trần thuật, tức là chủ ngữ đứng trước động từ, không đảo trợ động từ như trong câu hỏi trực tiếp.

Ví dụ:
“Where do you live?” → She asked where I lived.
“Did you finish?” → He asked if I had finished.

Người Việt rất hay mắc lỗi vì trong tiếng Việt khi tường thuật câu hỏi, ta có thể giữ cấu trúc gần với câu hỏi trực tiếp hơn, hoặc dịch từng từ từ tiếng Việt sang tiếng Anh. Vì vậy học sinh thường viết sai kiểu: She asked where did I live. Đây là sai vì trong reported question không được đảo did I live. Đúng phải là where I lived.

Với câu hỏi Yes/No, tiếng Anh thường dùng if hoặc whether. Với câu hỏi có từ để hỏi như what, where, when, why, how, ta giữ từ để hỏi đó nhưng vẫn phải dùng thứ tự câu trần thuật:
She asked where he was.
They wanted to know when the train would leave.

Một điểm nữa là thì thường lùi một bậc khi động từ tường thuật ở quá khứ:
now → then
present → past
will → would
can → could
have/has done → had done

Tuy nhiên, việc lùi thì không phải lúc nào cũng bắt buộc nếu sự việc vẫn đúng ở hiện tại, nhưng trong bài thi IELTS, cách an toàn nhất là học mẫu chuẩn trước: đổi về thứ tự câu trần thuật và lùi thì khi cần.

Tóm lại, hãy nhớ 3 bước: giữ từ hỏi, bỏ đảo ngữ, và thường lùi thì. Đây là lỗi rất phổ biến của người Việt khi viết reported questions.
formPatterns: no subject-auxiliary inversion in the reported clause
backshift tense when reporting in the past
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không có hiện tượng đảo trợ động từ như tiếng Anh, nên người học dễ giữ nguyên dạng câu hỏi trực tiếp khi tường thuật: where did I live. Cần nhớ rằng sau ask / wanted to know / wondered, tiếng Anh dùng trật tự câu kể: where I lived, if he was coming. Với câu hỏi Yes/No, dùng if hoặc whether, không dùng đảo ngữ.

title: Reported Commands
summary: Reporting orders and requests with an infinitive.

commonMistakes.right: The teacher told us to open our books.
commonMistakes.why: After told, use to + base verb for a reported command.
commonMistakes.wrong: The teacher told us open our books.

commonMistakes.right: My mother asked me to call her later.
commonMistakes.why: After asked, use to + base verb when reporting a request.
commonMistakes.wrong: My mother asked me call her later.

commonMistakes.right: The officer told the driver not to park there.
commonMistakes.why: Negative reported commands use not to + base verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: The officer told the driver don't park there.

commonMistakes.right: She told him to sit down.
commonMistakes.why: Use the infinitive after told when reporting an order or instruction.
commonMistakes.wrong: She told him sit down.

acceptedAnswers: to
drills.explanation: Reported commands usually use told/asked + object + to + base verb.
drills.prompt: Complete the structure: She told me ___ wait here.
drills.target: to

acceptedAnswers: The teacher told the students to be quiet.
choices: The teacher told the students be quiet.
The teacher told the students to be quiet.
The teacher told the students for be quiet.
drills.explanation: The correct reported command pattern is told + object + to + verb.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The teacher told the students to be quiet.

acceptedAnswers: My father asked me to help him.
drills.explanation: A request is often reported with asked + object + to + verb.
drills.prompt: Use these words to make a correct sentence: father / asked / me / help / him
drills.target: My father asked me to help him.

acceptedAnswers: not to
drills.explanation: For a negative command, use not to before the base verb.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She told us ___ touch the painting.
drills.target: not to

acceptedAnswers: The guard told us not to enter.
choices: The guard told us don't enter.
The guard told us not enter.
The guard told us not to enter.
drills.explanation: After told us, the verb must be in the infinitive form with not to for a negative command.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The guard told us not to enter.

acceptedAnswers: Please close the window.
drills.explanation: This is the direct command that might be reported later, so it should stay in the imperative form here.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a direct command: Tell him to close the window.
drills.target: Please close the window.

acceptedAnswers: The manager told the staff to leave early.
drills.explanation: Reported orders keep the meaning but change to told + object + to + verb.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The manager told the staff leave early.
drills.target: The manager told the staff to leave early.

acceptedAnswers: My friend asked me not to smoke in the car.
drills.explanation: Negative requests in reported speech use asked + object + not to + verb.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: friend / asked / me / not / smoke / in the car
drills.target: My friend asked me not to smoke in the car.

acceptedAnswers: The doctor told me to rest for two days.
choices: The doctor told me to resting for two days.
The doctor told me rest for two days.
The doctor told me to rest for two days.
drills.explanation: The infinitive to rest is required after told me.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The doctor told me to rest for two days.

explanation: Reported commands and requests are usually formed with a reporting verb such as told or asked, then an object, then to + the base verb. In negative commands, use not to + the base verb. This pattern reports orders, instructions, and requests without repeating the exact words.
formPatterns: tell/ask + object + not to + base verb
l1Notes: Người học Việt thường bỏ 'to' sau told/asked, vì trong tiếng Việt có thể nói trực tiếp 'bảo tôi làm...'. Cũng dễ quên 'not to' trong câu phủ định.

title: Time and Place Shifts
summary: Yesterday becoming the day before, here becoming there.

commonMistakes.right: She said that she was tired yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: In reported speech, yesterday usually becomes the day before or the previous day when the reporting time changes.
commonMistakes.wrong: She said that she was tired the day before yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: He told me that he would call the next day.
commonMistakes.why: In reported speech, tomorrow usually becomes the next day or the following day.
commonMistakes.wrong: He told me that he would call tomorrow.

commonMistakes.right: They said that they had arrived there the day before.
commonMistakes.why: In reported speech, here often becomes there, and yesterday becomes the day before.
commonMistakes.wrong: They said that they had arrived here yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: My teacher said that the class would start in that room.
commonMistakes.why: In reported speech, this and here often change to that and there, depending on the context.
commonMistakes.wrong: My teacher said that the class would start in this room.

acceptedAnswers: the day before
drills.explanation: In reported speech, yesterday usually changes to the day before or the previous day.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She said she had met him ____.
drills.target: the day before

acceptedAnswers: the next day
drills.explanation: In reported speech, tomorrow usually changes to the next day or the following day.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He said he would phone me ____.
drills.target: the next day

acceptedAnswers: there
drills.explanation: In reported speech, here often changes to there when the place is no longer the speaker’s location.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She said the keys were ____.
drills.target: there

acceptedAnswers: that
drills.explanation: In reported speech, this often changes to that when you are referring to something away from the original speaker.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He said ____ was his bag.
drills.target: that

acceptedAnswers: She said that she had met him the day before.
choices: She said that she had met him yesterday.
She said that she had met him the day before.
She said that she had met him the day after.
drills.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before in reported speech when the report is made later.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: She said that she had met him the day before.

acceptedAnswers: He told me that he would call the next day.
choices: He told me that he would call tomorrow.
He told me that he would call the next day.
He told me that he would call the day before.
drills.explanation: Tomorrow changes to the next day in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: He told me that he would call the next day.

acceptedAnswers: They said that they had arrived there the day before.
choices: They said that they had arrived here yesterday.
They said that they had arrived there the day before.
They said that they had arrived there yesterday.
drills.explanation: Here changes to there, and yesterday changes to the day before.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: They said that they had arrived there the day before.

acceptedAnswers: My teacher said that the class would start in that room.
choices: My teacher said that the class would start in this room.
My teacher said that the class would start in that room.
My teacher said that the class would start in here.
drills.explanation: This often becomes that in reported speech when the speaker is referring to a place or thing from a different point of view.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: My teacher said that the class would start in that room.

acceptedAnswers: the following week
drills.explanation: In reported speech, next week often becomes the following week or the week after.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She said she would visit us ____.
drills.target: the following week

acceptedAnswers: the previous month
drills.explanation: In reported speech, last month often becomes the previous month or the month before.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He said he had moved house ____.
drills.target: the previous month

acceptedAnswers: She told me that she was working in that office.
drills.explanation: This is a full reported sentence. Here changes to that office because the place is being reported from another point of view.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in reported speech: “I am working in this office.”
drills.target: She told me that she was working in that office.

acceptedAnswers: They said that they had left the hotel the previous day.
drills.explanation: This sentence shows both a time shift and a tense shift. Yesterday becomes the previous day in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in reported speech: “We left the hotel yesterday.”
drills.target: They said that they had left the hotel the previous day.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he would see her the following day.
drills.explanation: Tomorrow becomes the following day in reported speech, and the verb shifts back one tense.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in reported speech: “I will see her tomorrow.”
drills.target: He said that he would see her the following day.

acceptedAnswers: My sister said that she had been there the day before.
drills.explanation: Here becomes there, and yesterday becomes the day before in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in reported speech: “I was here yesterday.”
drills.target: My sister said that she had been there the day before.

explanation: In reported speech, time words and place words often shift because the speaker is reporting from a different time and place. Yesterday usually becomes the day before or the previous day, tomorrow becomes the next day or the following day, and here often becomes there. This is especially important in IELTS speaking and writing because mixed time references can make reported speech sound unnatural or confusing. The verb tense usually moves back too, but the time/place change must still fit the new reporting context.
explanationVi: Trong câu tường thuật, các từ chỉ thời gian và nơi chốn thường phải thay đổi vì người nói đang thuật lại từ một thời điểm và một địa điểm khác. Yesterday thường đổi thành the day before hoặc the previous day; tomorrow đổi thành the next day hoặc the following day; here thường đổi thành there. Ngoài ra, động từ thường lùi thì, nhưng người học Việt Nam hay quên rằng bản thân mốc thời gian và nơi chốn cũng phải đổi theo ngữ cảnh mới. Ví dụ, “I am here today” khi tường thuật lại có thể trở thành “she said that she was there that day”, chứ không giữ nguyên here, today. Đây là lỗi do ảnh hưởng tiếng Việt vì trong tiếng Việt ta thường chỉ cần đổi “hôm qua”, “ngày mai”, “ở đây” theo ngữ cảnh mà không luôn cảm thấy cần một hệ thống đổi tương ứng cố định như trong tiếng Anh gián tiếp.
formPatterns: yesterday -> the day before / the previous day
tomorrow -> the next day / the following day
last week/month/year -> the week/month/year before or the previous week/month/year
next week/month/year -> the following week/month/year or the week/month/year after
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không bắt buộc đổi mốc thời gian và nơi chốn theo kiểu cố định như tiếng Anh gián tiếp, nên người học hay giữ nguyên hôm qua/ngày mai/ở đây/kia khi tường thuật. Cần chú ý đổi theo điểm nhìn của người thuật lại: yesterday -> the day before, tomorrow -> the next day, here -> there, this -> that.

title: Backshift Exceptions
summary: When the tense stays put because the statement is still true.

commonMistakes.right: She said that the earth goes around the sun.
commonMistakes.why: The fact is still true now, so the present simple can stay present in reported speech.
commonMistakes.wrong: She said that the earth went around the sun.

commonMistakes.right: He said that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
commonMistakes.why: Scientific facts and general truths often do not backshift in reported speech because they are still true.
commonMistakes.wrong: He said that water boiled at 100 degrees Celsius.

commonMistakes.right: The teacher said that the meeting starts at 9 a.m.
commonMistakes.why: A fixed timetable or schedule can keep the present tense when the time is still valid.
commonMistakes.wrong: The teacher said that the meeting started at 9 a.m.

commonMistakes.right: My friend said that she lives in Hanoi.
commonMistakes.why: If the situation is still true, the present tense may stay present after a reporting verb in the past.
commonMistakes.wrong: My friend said that she lived in Hanoi.

acceptedAnswers: She said that the earth goes around the sun.
choices: She said that the earth went around the sun.
She said that the earth goes around the sun.
She said that the earth go around the sun.
drills.explanation: The earth still goes around the sun, so the present simple can stay present in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: She said that the earth goes around the sun.

acceptedAnswers: goes
drills.explanation: Use the present simple because the fact is still true.
drills.prompt: She said that the earth ____ around the sun.
drills.target: goes

acceptedAnswers: He said that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
drills.explanation: Scientific facts usually do not backshift when they are still true.
drills.prompt: Rewrite this as reported speech: He said: 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.'
drills.target: He said that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

acceptedAnswers: He said that the meeting starts at 9 a.m.
choices: He said that the meeting starts at 9 a.m.
He said that the meeting started at 9 a.m.
He said that the meeting has started at 9 a.m.
drills.explanation: A fixed schedule can keep the present tense if the timetable is still valid.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: He said that the meeting starts at 9 a.m.

acceptedAnswers: starts
drills.explanation: Use the present simple because the schedule is still current.
drills.prompt: The teacher said that the meeting ____ at 9 a.m.
drills.target: starts

acceptedAnswers: My friend said that she lives in Hanoi.
drills.explanation: If the statement is still true, the present tense can stay present after said.
drills.prompt: Change to reported speech: 'I live in Hanoi.'
drills.target: My friend said that she lives in Hanoi.

acceptedAnswers: He said that the Sun is bigger than the Earth.
choices: He said that the Sun was bigger than the Earth.
He said that the Sun is bigger than the Earth.
He said that the Sun be bigger than the Earth.
drills.explanation: A general truth can stay in the present even in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: He said that the Sun is bigger than the Earth.

acceptedAnswers: is
drills.explanation: The sentence states a general truth, so the present tense stays.
drills.prompt: He said that the Sun ____ bigger than the Earth.
drills.target: is

acceptedAnswers: She said that she works at a hospital.
drills.explanation: If the job is still true now, the present simple may stay present in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: She said that she worked at a hospital.
drills.target: She said that she works at a hospital.

explanation: In reported speech, English often backshifts the tense: present becomes past, and past becomes past perfect. But there are important exceptions. If the statement is still true, the present tense may stay present. This is common with scientific facts, general truths, current jobs or locations, and fixed schedules or timetables. For example, She said that the earth goes around the sun is correct because the fact is still true. He said that the meeting starts at 9 a.m. can also be correct if the timetable is still valid. Do not backshift automatically. First ask: is the information still true now? If yes, the original tense can often remain unchanged.
explanationVi: Trong câu tường thuật, tiếng Anh thường lùi thì: hiện tại chuyển sang quá khứ, quá khứ chuyển sang quá khứ hoàn thành. Nhưng có những ngoại lệ rất quan trọng. Nếu nội dung vẫn đúng ở hiện tại, thì hiện tại có thể giữ nguyên. Điều này thường xảy ra với sự thật khoa học, chân lý chung, nghề nghiệp hay nơi ở còn đúng, và lịch trình cố định còn hiệu lực. Ví dụ, She said that the earth goes around the sun là đúng vì sự thật này vẫn đúng. He said that the meeting starts at 9 a.m. cũng có thể đúng nếu lịch họp vẫn còn hiệu lực. Vì vậy, đừng lùi thì một cách máy móc. Hãy tự hỏi trước: thông tin đó bây giờ còn đúng không? Nếu còn đúng, ta часто giữ nguyên thì gốc.
formPatterns: said that + present simple for facts/truths
said that + present simple for current situations
said that + present simple for schedules
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường quen lùi thì rất máy móc trong câu tường thuật, vì tiếng Việt không có hệ thống lùi thì bắt buộc như tiếng Anh. Dễ sai khi thấy 'said' là tự động đổi mọi động từ sang quá khứ, kể cả sự thật hiển nhiên, lịch cố định hoặc tình trạng vẫn còn đúng.

title: Reporting Verbs
summary: Admit, deny, suggest, and their individual patterns.

commonMistakes.right: She admitted stealing the money.
commonMistakes.why: After admit, we use a gerund (-ing form), not an infinitive.
commonMistakes.wrong: She admitted to steal the money.

commonMistakes.right: He denied breaking the window.
commonMistakes.why: After deny, we use a gerund (-ing form), not an infinitive.
commonMistakes.wrong: He denied to break the window.

commonMistakes.right: I suggested taking a taxi.
commonMistakes.why: After suggest, we use a gerund (-ing form) or a that-clause, not an infinitive.
commonMistakes.wrong: I suggested to take a taxi.

commonMistakes.right: She suggested that we take a taxi.
commonMistakes.why: After suggest, we can use a that-clause with the base verb, not a past tense form.
commonMistakes.wrong: She suggested that we took a taxi.

acceptedAnswers: She admitted stealing the money.
drills.explanation: Admit is followed by a gerund: admit doing something.
drills.prompt: Rewrite this sentence correctly: She admitted to steal the money.
drills.target: She admitted stealing the money.

acceptedAnswers: He denied breaking the window.
drills.explanation: Deny is followed by a gerund, not to + verb.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: He denied to break the window.
drills.target: He denied breaking the window.

acceptedAnswers: I suggested taking a taxi.
choices: I suggested to take a taxi.
I suggested taking a taxi.
I suggested take a taxi.
drills.explanation: Suggest is followed by a gerund or a that-clause, so taking is correct here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I suggested taking a taxi.

acceptedAnswers: She suggested that we take a taxi.
drills.explanation: With suggest + that-clause, English usually uses the base verb after that: that we take.
drills.prompt: Write the sentence from these words: she / suggest / that / we / take / a taxi
drills.target: She suggested that we take a taxi.

acceptedAnswers: They admitted lying about the meeting.
drills.explanation: Admit is followed by a gerund phrase: lying about the meeting.
drills.prompt: Write the sentence from these words: they / admit / lie / about the meeting
drills.target: They admitted lying about the meeting.

acceptedAnswers: She denied knowing anything about it.
drills.explanation: Deny is followed by a gerund form, so knowing is correct.
drills.prompt: Rewrite this sentence correctly: She denied to know anything about it.
drills.target: She denied knowing anything about it.

acceptedAnswers: He suggested going earlier.
choices: He suggested go earlier.
He suggested going earlier.
He suggested to go earlier.
drills.explanation: Suggest is not followed by to + verb here; going is the correct form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He suggested going earlier.

acceptedAnswers: I admitted making a mistake.
choices: I admitted to make a mistake.
I admitted making a mistake.
I admitted make a mistake.
drills.explanation: Admit takes a gerund after it, so making is correct.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I admitted making a mistake.

acceptedAnswers: The teacher suggested that the students study harder.
drills.explanation: After suggest + that-clause, use the base verb study, not studied.
drills.prompt: Write the sentence from these words: the teacher / suggest / that / the students / study / harder
drills.target: The teacher suggested that the students study harder.

explanation: Reporting verbs often control the form that comes after them, and this is a common IELTS error. Admit and deny are usually followed by a gerund: admit doing, deny doing. Suggest can be followed by a gerund or by that + subject + base verb: suggest doing, suggest that we do. English does not usually use to + infinitive after admit, deny, or suggest in these patterns.
explanationVi: Các động từ tường thuật như admit, deny, suggest có “quy tắc đi kèm” riêng sau chúng. Đây là lỗi rất hay gặp ở người Việt vì tiếng Việt không đổi hình thức động từ như tiếng Anh. Với admit và deny, tiếng Anh thường dùng động từ thêm -ing: admitted stealing, denied breaking. Không dùng to + verb sau hai động từ này trong các cấu trúc này. Với suggest, có hai mẫu đúng: suggest doing something và suggest that + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ: She suggested taking a taxi. / She suggested that we take a taxi. Sau that, động từ thường ở dạng nguyên mẫu không “to”: take, study, go. Người học cần nhớ từng động từ đi với mẫu nào, không dịch từng từ từ tiếng Việt sang tiếng Anh.
l1Notes: Người học Việt thường thêm to trước động từ sau “động từ tường thuật” theo kiểu dịch máy từ tiếng Việt. Trong tiếng Việt, cấu trúc như 'thừa nhận làm gì', 'phủ nhận làm gì', 'đề nghị làm gì' không đổi hình thức động từ, nên dễ dẫn đến nhầm sang to + verb trong tiếng Anh.

title: Reported Speech with Modals
summary: How will, can, and must shift under reporting.

commonMistakes.right: She said that she could help me tomorrow.
commonMistakes.why: In reported speech, can usually changes to could, and the time expression tomorrow often changes to the next day or the following day.
commonMistakes.wrong: She said that she can help me tomorrow.

commonMistakes.right: He said that he had to leave early.
commonMistakes.why: Must often changes to had to when the meaning is obligation or necessity in reported speech.
commonMistakes.wrong: He said that he must leave early.

commonMistakes.right: They said that they would call us later.
commonMistakes.why: Will usually changes to would when the reporting verb is in the past.
commonMistakes.wrong: They said that they will call us later.

commonMistakes.right: She asked whether she could borrow my pen.
commonMistakes.why: In reported questions, the modal changes just like in reported statements, and the question word order is removed.
commonMistakes.wrong: She asked whether could she borrow my pen.

acceptedAnswers: She said that she could help me the next day.
choices: She said that she can help me the next day.
She said that she could help me the next day.
She said that she will help me the next day.
drills.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the past, can usually changes to could in reported speech. The time expression tomorrow changes to the next day or the following day.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: She said that she could help me the next day.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he had to finish the report.
drills.explanation: Must often changes to had to when it expresses obligation in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Report this sentence: 'I must finish the report.'
drills.target: He said that he had to finish the report.

acceptedAnswers: would
drills.explanation: In reported speech, will usually changes to would.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She said she ______ call later.
drills.target: would

acceptedAnswers: They said that they could not come to the meeting.
drills.explanation: Can becomes could in reported speech, and the negative form stays negative.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in reported speech: 'We can't come to the meeting.'
drills.target: They said that they could not come to the meeting.

acceptedAnswers: He asked if he could open the window.
choices: He asked if could he open the window.
He asked if he could open the window.
He asked if he can open the window.
drills.explanation: In reported questions, the modal changes form, and the word order becomes statement word order.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported question.
drills.target: He asked if he could open the window.

acceptedAnswers: She said that she would be late.
drills.explanation: Will changes to would in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: She said that she will be late.
drills.target: She said that she would be late.

acceptedAnswers: The doctor said that I had to rest for a week.
drills.explanation: Must often changes to had to in reported speech when it means necessity or obligation.
drills.prompt: Rewrite in reported speech: 'You must rest for a week,' the doctor said.
drills.target: The doctor said that I had to rest for a week.

acceptedAnswers: could
drills.explanation: Can usually changes to could in reported speech.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He said he ______ speak Japanese when he was a child.
drills.target: could

acceptedAnswers: She said that she would see us the following week.
choices: She said that she will see us the following week.
She said that she would see us the following week.
She said that she can see us the following week.
drills.explanation: Will changes to would in reported speech, and next week often changes to the following week.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence.
drills.target: She said that she would see us the following week.

acceptedAnswers: He said that he could not swim.
drills.explanation: The negative modal is reported by changing can to could and keeping the negative form.
drills.prompt: Report this sentence: 'I can't swim.'
drills.target: He said that he could not swim.

explanation: In reported speech, modal verbs often shift one step back in time when the reporting verb is in the past. Can usually becomes could, will becomes would, and must often becomes had to when it means obligation or necessity. In questions, the word order changes to statement order, so the modal comes after the subject: he asked if he could..., not he asked if could he.... Time expressions may also change, for example now to then, tomorrow to the next day, and next week to the following week. Not every modal always changes: for example, modal meaning can stay the same if the speaker is reporting a fixed rule, an offer, or a general truth, but for IELTS practice the main pattern is usually the backshift.
explanationVi: Trong câu tường thuật, các modal verbs thường lùi về “một bậc” khi động từ tường thuật ở quá khứ. Can thường đổi thành could, will đổi thành would, và must thường đổi thành had to khi must mang nghĩa bắt buộc hoặc cần thiết. Trong câu hỏi tường thuật, trật tự từ đổi sang trật tự câu trần thuật, nên modal đứng sau chủ ngữ: he asked if he could..., không phải he asked if could he.... Các trạng ngữ chỉ thời gian cũng có thể đổi, ví dụ now thành then, tomorrow thành the next day, và next week thành the following week. Tuy nhiên, không phải mọi modal lúc nào cũng đổi; đôi khi ý nghĩa đặc biệt như lời đề nghị, quy tắc cố định, hoặc chân lý chung có thể giữ nguyên. Nhưng trong bài IELTS, quy tắc quan trọng nhất thường là lùi thì của modal.
formPatterns: subject + said (that) + subject + could/would/had to + verb
subject + asked if/whether + subject + could/would + verb
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt không có biến đổi thì/modal tương đương trực tiếp như tiếng Anh, nên người học hay giữ nguyên can, will, must trong câu tường thuật. Cũng dễ nhầm trật tự từ trong câu hỏi tường thuật và quên đổi trạng ngữ thời gian như tomorrow, next week.

title: Yes/No Questions
summary: Auxiliary inversion and do-support, where Vietnamese uses a final particle.

commonMistakes.right: Do you like coffee?
commonMistakes.why: In yes/no questions with a main verb, English usually needs do-support and inversion. Vietnamese can ask with a final particle, but English cannot just keep the statement order.
commonMistakes.wrong: You like coffee?

commonMistakes.right: Is she at home?
commonMistakes.why: With be, English inverts the verb and subject directly. A statement order question is not grammatical in standard English.
commonMistakes.wrong: She is at home?

commonMistakes.right: Does he work here?
commonMistakes.why: In the present simple, the main verb does not take -s in questions. The auxiliary does the tense marking, so the verb stays in the base form.
commonMistakes.wrong: Does he works here?

commonMistakes.right: Did they finish the report?
commonMistakes.why: In the past simple, did already shows the past, so the main verb must be in the base form.
commonMistakes.wrong: Did they finished the report?

acceptedAnswers: Do you like coffee?
choices: You do like coffee?
Do you like coffee?
Are you like coffee?
drills.explanation: In a yes/no question with a main verb, use do-support and invert do and the subject.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct question.
drills.target: Do you like coffee?

acceptedAnswers: Is she tired?
drills.explanation: With be, make the verb come before the subject in a yes/no question.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the statement as a yes/no question: She is tired.
drills.target: Is she tired?

acceptedAnswers: Does he speak English?
drills.explanation: In the present simple, use does with he/she/it, and keep the main verb in the base form.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a yes/no question: He speaks English.
drills.target: Does he speak English?

acceptedAnswers: Did they arrive early?
choices: Did they arrived early?
Did they arrive early?
Do they arrive early?
drills.explanation: In the past simple, did marks the past, so arrive stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct question.
drills.target: Did they arrive early?

acceptedAnswers: Do you have a ticket?
drills.explanation: This is a normal yes/no question with do-support.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: You have a ticket?
drills.target: Do you have a ticket?

acceptedAnswers: Are they in the kitchen?
choices: They are in the kitchen?
Are they in the kitchen?
Do they in the kitchen?
drills.explanation: With be, move the verb before the subject.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct question.
drills.target: Are they in the kitchen?

acceptedAnswers: Does she know the answer?
drills.explanation: Does is used with she/he/it in the present simple, and know stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: Write the yes/no question. Use: she / know / the answer
drills.target: Does she know the answer?

acceptedAnswers: Did you watch the film?
drills.explanation: Did already carries the past meaning, so watch does not change form.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a yes/no question: You watched the film.
drills.target: Did you watch the film?

acceptedAnswers: Is it raining?
choices: It is raining?
Is it raining?
Does it raining?
drills.explanation: With be in the present continuous, invert is and the subject.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct question.
drills.target: Is it raining?

acceptedAnswers: Do they play tennis on Sundays?
drills.explanation: When the main verb is play in the present simple, use do-support and keep play in the base form.
drills.prompt: Make a yes/no question from these words: they / play / tennis / on Sundays
drills.target: Do they play tennis on Sundays?

acceptedAnswers: Is there a problem?
choices: There is a problem?
Is there a problem?
Does there a problem?
drills.explanation: With there + be, English inverts is and there.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct question.
drills.target: Is there a problem?

acceptedAnswers: Did she send the email?
drills.explanation: In the past simple question, did is enough to show the past, so send stays base form.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a yes/no question: She sent the email.
drills.target: Did she send the email?

acceptedAnswers: Does Tom live near here?
drills.explanation: For a third-person singular subject in the present simple, use does and the base verb live.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: Does Tom lives near here?
drills.target: Does Tom live near here?

acceptedAnswers: Can you help me?
choices: Can you help me?
You can help me?
Do you can help me?
drills.explanation: Modal verbs like can move before the subject and do not need do-support.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct question.
drills.target: Can you help me?

explanation: Yes/no questions in English usually need a change in word order. If the verb is be, can, will, or another modal, put the auxiliary before the subject: Is she tired? Can you swim? If the sentence has a main verb in the present simple or past simple, English usually needs do-support: Do you like tea? Did they finish? In these questions, the main verb stays in the base form, so not likes, finishes, or finished. Vietnamese often asks a yes/no question with the same basic sentence order and a final particle such as không, so Vietnamese learners may forget inversion or add the wrong verb form. Remember: auxiliary first, subject second, and base verb after do/does/did.
explanationVi: Trong tiếng Anh, câu hỏi Yes/No thường phải đổi trật tự từ. Nếu động từ là be, can, will hoặc một động từ tình thái khác, ta đặt trợ động từ trước chủ ngữ: Is she tired? Can you swim? Nếu câu có động từ chính ở hiện tại đơn hoặc quá khứ đơn, tiếng Anh thường cần do-support: Do you like tea? Did they finish? Khi đó, động từ chính phải ở dạng nguyên thể, không thêm -s, không chia quá khứ. Tiếng Việt thường hỏi Yes/No bằng cùng trật tự câu cơ bản và thêm hạt từ ở cuối như không, nên người học dễ quên đảo trợ động từ hoặc chia sai động từ. Hãy nhớ: trợ động từ đứng trước, chủ ngữ đứng sau, và động từ chính ở dạng nguyên thể sau do/does/did.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng hạt từ ở cuối câu hỏi (như “không”) thay vì đảo trợ động từ, nên người học dễ giữ nguyên trật tự câu khẳng định trong tiếng Anh. Cũng dễ thêm -s/-ed vào động từ chính sau do/does/did, nhưng tiếng Anh không làm vậy.

title: Wh- Questions
summary: Question words plus inverted word order.

commonMistakes.right: Where do you live?
commonMistakes.why: In wh- questions with do/does/did, English uses the question word first, then the auxiliary do/does/did, then the subject and base verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: Where you live?

commonMistakes.right: What does she want?
commonMistakes.why: With he/she/it in the present simple, use does, not do, and the main verb stays in the base form.
commonMistakes.wrong: What do she want?

commonMistakes.right: Why are they late?
commonMistakes.why: With be verbs, the verb comes before the subject in a question. Vietnamese often keeps normal word order, but English must invert it.
commonMistakes.wrong: Why they are late?

commonMistakes.right: When did he arrive?
commonMistakes.why: In past simple questions, use did + base verb. The main verb does not change to past form again.
commonMistakes.wrong: When did he arrived?

acceptedAnswers: Where do you live?
choices: Where you live?
Where do you live?
Where does you live?
drills.explanation: Use where + do + subject + base verb in a present simple question.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Where do you live?

acceptedAnswers: does
What does she do?
drills.explanation: With she, use does. The main verb stays in the base form: do.
drills.prompt: What ___ she do?
drills.target: does

acceptedAnswers: did
When did they arrive?
drills.explanation: In past simple questions, did comes before the subject, and arrive stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: When ___ they arrive?
drills.target: did

acceptedAnswers: Why is he tired?
drills.explanation: With the verb be, put the verb before the subject in the question.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence as a question: He is tired. Use Why.
drills.target: Why is he tired?

acceptedAnswers: Who is calling?
choices: Who calling is?
Who is calling?
Who does calling?
drills.explanation: With the verb be or an -ing verb, keep the auxiliary before the subject.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Who is calling?

acceptedAnswers: Where do they work?
drills.explanation: Wh- question + do + subject + base verb is the normal present simple pattern.
drills.prompt: Write a question. Use where / they / work.
drills.target: Where do they work?

acceptedAnswers: Who did you see?
drills.explanation: In past simple questions, use did + subject + base verb, even when the question word is who.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence as a question: You saw who? Use Who.
drills.target: Who did you see?

acceptedAnswers: What time does the train leave?
choices: What time the train does leave?
What time does the train leave?
What time do the train leave?
drills.explanation: The question word comes first, then does, then the subject, then the base verb leave.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: What time does the train leave?

acceptedAnswers: How often do you exercise?
drills.explanation: How often is followed by do/does in present simple questions.
drills.prompt: Write a question. Use how often / you / exercise.
drills.target: How often do you exercise?

acceptedAnswers: Where did she go?
drills.explanation: Did is used for past simple questions, and go stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: Where did she went?
drills.target: Where did she go?

acceptedAnswers: What is your name?
choices: What your name is?
What is your name?
What does your name?
drills.explanation: With the verb be, the verb comes before the subject in the question.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: What is your name?

acceptedAnswers: Why do you want this job?
drills.explanation: In a wh- question, use the question word first, then do/does, then the subject, then the base verb.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence as a question: You want this job because it is interesting. Use Why.
drills.target: Why do you want this job?

acceptedAnswers: does
When does the class start?
drills.explanation: The auxiliary does comes before the subject, and start stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: When ___ the class start?
drills.target: does

acceptedAnswers: How does she get to work?
choices: How she does get to work?
How does she get to work?
How do she get to work?
drills.explanation: With she, use does, not do, and keep get in the base form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: How does she get to work?

explanation: Wh- questions in English usually start with a question word such as what, where, when, why, who, or how. After the question word, English often changes the normal subject-verb order: we use an auxiliary like do, does, or did, then the subject, then the base verb. For the verb be, the be verb itself moves before the subject. This is different from Vietnamese, where questions often keep the same word order as statements and rely more on question words or particles. A common IELTS error is to say Where you live? or What she wants? Instead, English needs Where do you live? and What does she want? Remember that in past simple questions, did shows the past time, so the main verb stays in the base form: Where did you go?, not Where did you went?
explanationVi: Trong câu hỏi wh- ở tiếng Anh, từ hỏi như what, where, when, why, who, how đứng ở đầu câu. Sau từ hỏi, tiếng Anh thường đảo trật tự: dùng trợ động từ do/does/did, rồi đến chủ ngữ, rồi động từ nguyên mẫu. Với động từ to be, chính be đứng trước chủ ngữ. Điều này khác tiếng Việt, vì tiếng Việt thường giữ trật tự gần giống câu kể hơn và chỉ thêm từ hỏi hoặc tiểu từ câu hỏi. Vì vậy người học Việt Nam hay viết Where you live? hoặc What she wants?, nhưng tiếng Anh phải là Where do you live? và What does she want? Ở thì quá khứ đơn, did đã mang nghĩa quá khứ nên động từ chính phải ở dạng nguyên mẫu: Where did you go?, không phải Where did you went?
l1Notes: Người Việt hay giữ trật tự câu kể khi đặt câu hỏi: quên đảo trợ động từ và quên dùng do/does/did. Dễ nhầm thêm does với she/he/it, và dễ dùng động từ quá khứ sau did.

title: Negative Forms
summary: Not, do not, and contraction across tenses.

commonMistakes.right: She does not like coffee.
commonMistakes.why: In the present simple, the negative usually needs do not/does not. The main verb stays in the base form after does not.
commonMistakes.wrong: She not likes coffee.

commonMistakes.right: I did not see him yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: In the past simple, the negative usually needs did not. The main verb stays in the base form after did not.
commonMistakes.wrong: I did not saw him yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: He is not at home now.
commonMistakes.why: With the verb be, make the negative with not directly after am/is/are/was/were. Do not use do/does/did with be.
commonMistakes.wrong: He does not at home now.

commonMistakes.right: We do not have any money.
commonMistakes.why: With have as a main verb in standard English, the negative in the present simple uses do not/does not. Do not make the verb itself negative.
commonMistakes.wrong: We have not any money.

acceptedAnswers: does not
drills.explanation: In the present simple, the third person singular negative is does not + base verb.
drills.prompt: She ____ like fish.
drills.target: does not

acceptedAnswers: do not
drills.explanation: In the present simple negative with I/you/we/they, use do not + base verb.
drills.prompt: They ____ play tennis on Mondays.
drills.target: do not

acceptedAnswers: did not
drills.explanation: In the past simple negative, use did not + base verb.
drills.prompt: I ____ see the email yesterday.
drills.target: did not

acceptedAnswers: She does not work on Sundays.
drills.explanation: With third person singular in the present simple, the negative uses does not and the main verb stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: Write a negative sentence: she / work / on Sundays
drills.target: She does not work on Sundays.

acceptedAnswers: He did not call me last night.
drills.explanation: After did not, the main verb must stay in the base form, so call is correct and called is not.
drills.prompt: Write a negative sentence: he / call / me / last night
drills.target: He did not call me last night.

acceptedAnswers: The train was not late.
drills.explanation: With the verb be in the past, make the negative with was not or were not.
drills.prompt: Write a negative sentence: the train / be / late
drills.target: The train was not late.

acceptedAnswers: We do not have enough time.
choices: We not have enough time.
We do not have enough time.
We does not have enough time.
drills.explanation: The correct present simple negative uses do not with we. The verb have stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: We do not have enough time.

acceptedAnswers: He is not hungry now.
choices: He does not hungry now.
He is not hungry now.
He are not hungry now.
drills.explanation: With be, use is not for he. Do not add do/does with be.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He is not hungry now.

acceptedAnswers: I do not know the answer.
choices: I does not know the answer.
I do not know the answer.
I not know the answer.
drills.explanation: In the present simple negative with I, use do not + base verb.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I do not know the answer.

acceptedAnswers: They did not understand the question.
choices: They did not understood the question.
They did not understand the question.
They do not understood the question.
drills.explanation: After did not, use the base form of the verb. Understood is wrong here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: They did not understand the question.

acceptedAnswers: Do not open the window.
drills.explanation: A negative imperative uses do not + base verb.
drills.prompt: Write a negative command using open / the window.
drills.target: Do not open the window.

acceptedAnswers: It is not raining.
drills.explanation: With be in the present, put not after is/am/are.
drills.prompt: Change to a negative sentence: It is raining.
drills.target: It is not raining.

acceptedAnswers: I do not like horror films.
drills.explanation: This is the normal present simple negative: do not + base verb like.
drills.prompt: I not like horror films.
drills.target: I do not like horror films.

explanation:
To make a sentence negative in English, the form depends on the verb and tense. With the verb be, put not after am/is/are/was/were: He is not at home. With other verbs in the present simple, use do not or does not: I do not know, She does not like. In the past simple, use did not: They did not go. After do not/does not/did not, the main verb stays in the base form, not the past form and not the third-person -s form.

Contractions are very common in speaking and writing: do not = don’t, does not = doesn’t, did not = didn’t, is not = isn’t, are not = aren’t, was not = wasn’t, were not = weren’t. In IELTS, both full forms and contractions are correct unless the style is very formal. The important rule is: do not mix the negative helper with the wrong verb form.

Tiếng Việt thường không dùng trợ động từ trong câu phủ định theo kiểu tiếng Anh, nên người học hay viết sai như I not like, She not works, hoặc I did not went. Trong tiếng Anh, câu phủ định thường cần trợ động từ do/does/did, hoặc dùng not trực tiếp với động từ to be. Sau do/does/did, động từ chính luôn ở dạng nguyên mẫu. Sau to be, đặt not ngay sau am/is/are/was/were. Hãy nhớ: present simple dùng do not/does not; past simple dùng did not; còn be thì không dùng do/does/did.
explanationVi:
Để tạo câu phủ định trong tiếng Anh, cách dùng phụ thuộc vào loại động từ và thì. Với động từ to be, đặt not ngay sau am/is/are/was/were: He is not at home. Với các động từ thường ở hiện tại đơn, dùng do not hoặc does not: I do not know, She does not like. Ở quá khứ đơn, dùng did not: They did not go. Sau do not/does not/did not, động từ chính phải ở dạng nguyên mẫu, không chia quá khứ và không thêm -s ngôi thứ ba.

Dạng rút gọn rất phổ biến trong nói và viết: do not = don’t, does not = doesn’t, did not = didn’t, is not = isn’t, are not = aren’t, was not = wasn’t, were not = weren’t. Trong IELTS, cả dạng đầy đủ và dạng rút gọn đều đúng, trừ khi văn phong quá trang trọng. Điểm quan trọng nhất là không được kết hợp sai giữa trợ động từ phủ định và hình thức động từ chính.

Người Việt thường bị ảnh hưởng bởi tiếng mẹ đẻ vì tiếng Việt không dùng trợ động từ phủ định giống tiếng Anh, nên hay viết sai như I not like, She not works, hoặc I did not went. Trong tiếng Anh, câu phủ định thường cần do/does/did, hoặc dùng not trực tiếp với động từ to be. Sau do/does/did, động từ chính luôn ở nguyên mẫu. Sau to be, đặt not ngay sau am/is/are/was/were. Hãy nhớ: hiện tại đơn dùng do not/does not; quá khứ đơn dùng did not; còn với be thì không dùng do/does/did.
formPatterns: negative imperative: do not + base verb
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không có trợ động từ phủ định tương ứng với do/does/did, và từ “không” đứng trước động từ chính. Vì vậy người học dễ viết I not like, She not works, hoặc did not went. Cần nhấn mạnh rằng tiếng Anh phải dùng trợ động từ phủ định đúng thì, và sau đó động từ chính không đổi dạng.

title: Subject Questions
summary: Who broke it, with no auxiliary and no inversion.

commonMistakes.right: Who called you last night?
commonMistakes.why: Who is the subject of the verb called, so English does not use do/does/did or inversion here. In Vietnamese, learners often try to add an auxiliary because most questions use a question word plus question structure, but subject questions keep normal subject-verb order.
commonMistakes.wrong: Who did call you last night?

commonMistakes.right: Who broke the window?
commonMistakes.why: Who is the subject, so the verb stays in normal past tense form without did. The auxiliary did is used in ordinary wh-questions when who or what is not the subject, but not in subject questions.
commonMistakes.wrong: Who did break the window?
