commonMistakes.right: What happened to your phone?
commonMistakes.why: What is the subject of happened, so there is no auxiliary and no inversion. A wh-question about the object or complement would use an auxiliary, but subject questions do not.
commonMistakes.wrong: What did happen to your phone?

commonMistakes.right: Which team won the match?
commonMistakes.why: Which team is the subject of won, so English uses normal subject-verb order. Adding did makes the sentence ungrammatical in this subject-question pattern.
commonMistakes.wrong: Which team did win the match?

acceptedAnswers: Who broke the glass?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject of broke, so the question uses normal subject-verb order with no auxiliary.
drills.prompt: Write the question. Use subject-question form. who / break / the glass
drills.target: Who broke the glass?

acceptedAnswers: Who
Who phoned you yesterday?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject of phoned, so English does not add did.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: ____ phoned you yesterday?
drills.target: Who

acceptedAnswers: Who is responsible for the noise?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject of is, so the sentence keeps normal order. In a wh-question about the subject, do not invert subject and auxiliary.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a subject question: The person responsible for the noise is who?
drills.target: Who is responsible for the noise?

acceptedAnswers: What happened after the meeting?
drills.explanation: What is the subject of happened, so there is no auxiliary did. This is different from an object question such as What did you do after the meeting?
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a subject question: Something happened after the meeting.
drills.target: What happened after the meeting?

acceptedAnswers: Who took my pen?
choices: Who did take my pen?
Who took my pen?
Who did took my pen?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject of took, so no auxiliary is used. The other options are ungrammatical in this subject-question pattern.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct subject question.
drills.target: Who took my pen?

acceptedAnswers: Which student answered the question?
drills.explanation: Which student is the subject of answered, so the question keeps normal subject-verb order.
drills.prompt: Build a subject question from these words: which student / answer / the question
drills.target: Which student answered the question?

acceptedAnswers: Who made this cake?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject, so the verb stays in normal past form without did.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: Who did made this cake?
drills.target: Who made this cake?

acceptedAnswers: What caused the delay?
choices: What did cause the delay?
What caused the delay?
What did caused the delay?
drills.explanation: What is the subject of caused, so no auxiliary is needed. In a wh-question where what is not the subject, English would use do/does/did.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct subject question.
drills.target: What caused the delay?

acceptedAnswers: Who
Who lives next door?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject of lives, so there is no auxiliary. The verb agrees with who in the third-person singular form lives.
drills.prompt: Complete the question: ____ lives next door?
drills.target: Who

acceptedAnswers: Who opened the email?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject of opened, so the question uses normal word order. This is different from an object wh-question like What did she open?
drills.prompt: Write the question. Use subject-question form. who / open / the email
drills.target: Who opened the email?

acceptedAnswers: Who left early?
choices: Who did leave early?
Who left early?
Who did left early?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject of left, so no auxiliary did is used. The other two options are not grammatical subject questions.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Who left early?

acceptedAnswers: Who is calling from Singapore?
drills.explanation: Who is the subject of is calling, so English keeps the auxiliary after the subject-question word. Do not move is before who.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a subject question: Someone is calling from Singapore.
drills.target: Who is calling from Singapore?

acceptedAnswers: Which car belongs to Minh?
drills.explanation: Which car is the subject of belongs, so there is no inversion. A Vietnamese learner may expect a question word plus auxiliary, but that is not how subject questions work in English.
drills.prompt: Build a subject question from these words: which car / belong to / Minh
drills.target: Which car belongs to Minh?

explanation: Subject questions ask about the subject of the verb: the person or thing doing the action or being described. In English, these questions keep normal subject-verb order, so there is no do/does/did and no inversion. For example, Who broke it? is correct because who is the subject of broke. This is different from ordinary wh-questions where the wh-word is not the subject, such as What did you buy? or Who did you see? In those questions, English uses an auxiliary and changes the word order. With subject questions, do not add an auxiliary unless the main verb itself already has one, such as Who is calling? or Who has finished?
explanationVi: Câu hỏi chủ ngữ là câu hỏi hỏi về chủ ngữ của động từ: người hoặc vật thực hiện hành động hoặc được nói đến. Trong tiếng Anh, loại câu hỏi này giữ trật tự bình thường của câu khẳng định, nên không dùng do/does/did và không đảo trợ động từ. Ví dụ, Who broke it? đúng vì who là chủ ngữ của broke. Điều này khác với wh-questions thông thường khi từ hỏi không phải là chủ ngữ, ví dụ What did you buy? hoặc Who did you see? Trong những câu đó, tiếng Anh cần trợ động từ và đảo trật tự. Với subject questions, không thêm trợ động từ, trừ khi động từ chính đã có trợ động từ sẵn như Who is calling? hoặc Who has finished? Nói ngắn gọn: nếu từ hỏi là chủ ngữ thì giữ nguyên trật tự S-V; nếu từ hỏi không phải chủ ngữ thì dùng trợ động từ và đảo vị trí.
formPatterns: If the main verb has an auxiliary already, keep it after the wh-word
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường chuyển thói quen từ câu hỏi tiếng Việt sang tiếng Anh: nghĩ rằng hễ có từ để hỏi thì phải thêm trợ động từ hoặc đảo ngữ. Trong tiếng Việt, vị trí từ hỏi linh hoạt hơn và không có hệ thống do/does/did như tiếng Anh, nên dễ viết sai kiểu Who did break it? thay vì Who broke it? Cần nhớ: nếu từ hỏi là chủ ngữ, tiếng Anh không đảo.

minimalPairs.meaning: The wh-word is the subject, so no auxiliary is used.
minimalPairs.sentence: Who called you?

minimalPairs.meaning: The wh-word is not the subject, so an auxiliary is used.
minimalPairs.sentence: Who did you call?

minimalPairs.meaning: The wh-word is the subject, so no auxiliary is used.
minimalPairs.sentence: What happened?

minimalPairs.meaning: The wh-word is not the subject, so an auxiliary is used.
minimalPairs.sentence: What did you happen to see?

title: Question Tags
summary: Matching auxiliary and reversing polarity.

commonMistakes.right: You like coffee, don't you?
commonMistakes.why: In a question tag, the auxiliary must match the main clause, and the tag must reverse the polarity. The statement is positive, so the tag is negative.
commonMistakes.wrong: You like coffee, do you?

commonMistakes.right: She isn't coming, is she?
commonMistakes.why: A negative statement normally takes a positive tag. Using another negative tag does not form a standard question tag.
commonMistakes.wrong: She isn't coming, isn't she?

commonMistakes.right: We have finished, haven't we?
commonMistakes.why: The tag must use the correct auxiliary from the main clause. In the present perfect, the auxiliary is have.
commonMistakes.wrong: We have finished, don't we?

commonMistakes.right: Open the window, will you?
commonMistakes.why: Imperatives often take will you? or won't you? depending on tone. Do you? is not the usual tag for an imperative.
commonMistakes.wrong: Open the window, do you?

acceptedAnswers: aren't they
drills.explanation: The statement is positive and uses are, so the tag is negative and repeats the same auxiliary.
drills.prompt: They are late, _____?
drills.target: aren't they

acceptedAnswers: did he
drills.explanation: The main clause is negative with didn't, so the tag is positive and uses did.
drills.prompt: He didn't call, _____?
drills.target: did he

acceptedAnswers: She likes tea, doesn't she?
drills.explanation: The tag must match the auxiliary in the main clause. The statement is positive, so the tag is negative.
drills.prompt: Add the correct question tag: She likes tea.
drills.target: She likes tea, doesn't she?

acceptedAnswers: We haven't met before, have we?
drills.explanation: A negative clause takes a positive tag. The auxiliary have is repeated in the tag.
drills.prompt: Add the correct question tag: We haven't met before.
drills.target: We haven't met before, have we?

acceptedAnswers: She is your sister, isn't she?
drills.explanation: With the verb be, the tag repeats be. A positive statement takes a negative tag.
drills.prompt: Add the correct question tag: She is your sister.
drills.target: She is your sister, isn't she?

acceptedAnswers: isn't it
drills.explanation: The statement is positive, so the tag is negative. The pronoun it refers to the weather.
drills.prompt: It's cold today, _____?
drills.target: isn't it

acceptedAnswers: tagging
choices: tagging
tag
to tag
drills.explanation: After enjoy, English uses a gerund (-ing form), not an infinitive.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct verb form: She enjoys _____ photos.
drills.target: tagging

acceptedAnswers: Does he work in a bank?
drills.explanation: This is a yes/no question with do-support, not a question tag. The correct tag form would be different: He works in a bank, doesn't he?
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: He works in a bank, does he?
drills.target: Does he work in a bank?

acceptedAnswers: won't you
drills.explanation: Imperatives commonly take will you? or won't you? as tags. The positive command takes a negative tag here.
drills.prompt: Close the door, _____?
drills.target: won't you

acceptedAnswers: won't they
will they
drills.explanation: The main clause uses a modal verb, so the tag repeats the same auxiliary. A positive statement takes a negative tag.
drills.prompt: They can finish by Friday, _____?
drills.target: won't they

acceptedAnswers: didn't she
drills.explanation: The past simple main verb needs did in the tag. The statement is positive, so the tag is negative.
drills.prompt: Anna bought a new phone, _____?
drills.target: didn't she

acceptedAnswers: aren't I
drills.explanation: With I am, the standard tag is aren't I? even though the auxiliary is am. This is an irregular but very common pattern.
drills.prompt: I'm late, _____?
drills.target: aren't I

acceptedAnswers: She can swim, can't she?
drills.explanation: The modal can becomes can't in the negative tag. The auxiliary must match the main clause.
drills.prompt: Add the correct question tag: She can swim.
drills.target: She can swim, can't she?

acceptedAnswers: He doesn't speak French, does he?
drills.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive tag. The auxiliary do carries the tag because the main verb is in the present simple.
drills.prompt: Add the correct question tag: He doesn't speak French.
drills.target: He doesn't speak French, does he?

acceptedAnswers: is there
drills.explanation: With there is / there are, the tag uses there plus the matching auxiliary. The clause is negative, so the tag is positive.
drills.prompt: There isn't a problem, _____?
drills.target: is there

acceptedAnswers: You finished early, didn't you?
drills.explanation: The past simple auxiliary is did. Since the statement is positive, the tag is negative.
drills.prompt: Add the correct question tag: You finished early.
drills.target: You finished early, didn't you?

explanation: Question tags are short questions added to the end of a statement. In English, the tag usually repeats the auxiliary verb from the main clause and changes polarity: positive statement + negative tag, negative statement + positive tag. If the main clause has no auxiliary, use do/does/did in the tag. For be, modal verbs, perfect tenses, and there is/are, repeat the correct auxiliary form. The pronoun in the tag must match the subject of the statement: he, she, it, they, we, you, I. This pattern is very important for IELTS because speakers use tags to check information, soften statements, and keep conversation flowing. Exception: with I am, the usual tag is aren't I? The tag for imperatives is often will you?, won't you?, or can/could you? depending on tone.
explanationVi: Câu hỏi đuôi (question tags) là một câu hỏi ngắn thêm ở cuối câu khẳng định hoặc phủ định. Trong tiếng Anh, trợ động từ ở câu đuôi thường phải khớp với trợ động từ ở mệnh đề chính và đảo sang cực tính ngược lại: câu chính khẳng định + câu đuôi phủ định, câu chính phủ định + câu đuôi khẳng định. Nếu mệnh đề chính không có trợ động từ, ta dùng do/does/did trong câu đuôi. Với động từ be, động từ khuyết thiếu (can, will, must...), thì hoàn thành, và cấu trúc there is/are, phải lặp lại đúng trợ động từ tương ứng. Đại từ trong câu đuôi cũng phải đúng với chủ ngữ của câu chính: he, she, it, they, we, you, I. Đây là điểm rất quan trọng cho IELTS vì người nói dùng question tags để xin xác nhận, làm câu nói mềm hơn, và giữ nhịp hội thoại. Ngoại lệ đáng nhớ: với I am, dạng thường dùng là aren't I? Câu mệnh lệnh thường dùng will you?, won't you?, hoặc can/could you? tùy sắc thái.
formPatterns: auxiliary in main clause repeated in tag
do/does/did used when main clause has no auxiliary
pronoun in tag matches subject of main clause
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường thêm đuôi hỏi kiểu “phải không?”, “đúng không?” một cách không đổi, nên hay quên rằng tiếng Anh phải đổi trợ động từ, đổi phủ định/khẳng định, và giữ đúng đại từ trong câu đuôi. Tiếng Việt cũng không có hệ thống trợ động từ tương tự do/does/did, nên rất dễ dùng sai dạng như làm câu đuôi theo nghĩa mà không theo hình thức.

title: Indirect Questions
summary: Could you tell me where ... , keeping statement word order.

commonMistakes.right: Could you tell me where the station is?
commonMistakes.why: In an indirect question, the subject comes before the verb, like in a statement. We say where the station is, not where is the station.
commonMistakes.wrong: Could you tell me where is the station?

commonMistakes.right: I don't know what time the train leaves.
commonMistakes.why: After what time, the word order is statement order: the train leaves. Do not use question order in an indirect question.
commonMistakes.wrong: I don't know what time does the train leave.

commonMistakes.right: She asked me if I was free on Friday.
commonMistakes.why: Indirect yes/no questions usually use if or whether, followed by statement word order. We say if I was free, not if was I free.
commonMistakes.wrong: She asked me if was I free on Friday.

commonMistakes.right: Do you know how much this costs?
commonMistakes.why: In an indirect question, how much is followed by statement word order. We say this costs, not does this cost.
commonMistakes.wrong: Do you know how much does this cost?

acceptedAnswers: where the library is
drills.explanation: An indirect question keeps statement word order: subject + verb. Here, the correct order is where the library is.
drills.prompt: Complete the indirect question: Could you tell me __________?
drills.target: where the library is

acceptedAnswers: I don't know where he lives.
drills.explanation: In an indirect question, the order is he lives, not does he live. The whole sentence is a statement inside the question phrase.
drills.prompt: Write the full sentence. Use indirect-question word order: he / live / where.
drills.target: I don't know where he lives.

acceptedAnswers: Can you tell me what time the meeting starts?
drills.explanation: What time is followed by statement order: the meeting starts. There is no auxiliary do here.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as an indirect question: What time does the meeting start?
drills.target: Can you tell me what time the meeting starts?

acceptedAnswers: Do you know if the shop is open on Sundays?
choices: Do you know if the shop is open on Sundays?
Do you know if is the shop open on Sundays?
Do you know whether the shop open on Sundays?
drills.explanation: After if, the verb follows the subject: the shop is open. The other choices use question order or missing verb form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct indirect question.
drills.target: Do you know if the shop is open on Sundays?

acceptedAnswers: I asked her where she had parked her car.
drills.explanation: In reported questions, the verb usually shifts back in time: had parked. The word order stays statement order, with she had parked.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: I asked her where had she parked her car.
drills.target: I asked her where she had parked her car.

acceptedAnswers: whether
drills.explanation: Whether is used in indirect yes/no questions, especially in more formal English. It introduces the clause before statement word order.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She asked me __________ I wanted to join them.
drills.target: whether

acceptedAnswers: Could you explain why he left early?
choices: Could you explain why he left early?
Could you explain why did he leave early?
Could you explain why he leaves early?
drills.explanation: After why, indirect questions use statement word order: he left early. Do not use did he leave.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Could you explain why he left early?

acceptedAnswers: I wonder how much this costs.
drills.explanation: How much is followed by statement order: this costs. The sentence does not use auxiliary do in an indirect question.
drills.prompt: Write the full sentence using these words: I / wonder / how much / this / cost.
drills.target: I wonder how much this costs.

acceptedAnswers: Can you tell me when the plane arrives?
drills.explanation: When introduces an indirect question, so the verb comes after the subject: the plane arrives. This is different from direct-question order.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as an indirect question: When does the plane arrive?
drills.target: Can you tell me when the plane arrives?

explanation: Indirect questions are questions inside another sentence, often after phrases like can you tell me, do you know, I wonder, or she asked. The key rule is that the word order changes from question order to statement order: subject comes before the verb. For example, we say where the station is, not where is the station. In yes/no indirect questions, we usually use if or whether: She asked me if I was free. Remember that reported questions often follow the normal backshift in tense, but the most important point is the statement word order after the question word.
explanationVi: Câu hỏi gián tiếp là câu hỏi nằm bên trong một câu khác, thường sau các cụm như can you tell me, do you know, I wonder, she asked. Điểm quan trọng nhất là trật tự từ phải đổi sang trật tự câu khẳng định: chủ ngữ đứng trước động từ. Vì vậy ta nói where the station is, không nói where is the station. Với câu hỏi yes/no gián tiếp, ta thường dùng if hoặc whether: She asked me if I was free. Hãy nhớ rằng câu tường thuật/câu hỏi gián tiếp thường còn có sự lùi thì, nhưng trọng tâm của điểm này là trật tự câu khẳng định sau từ để hỏi. Người Việt hay bị ảnh hưởng bởi cách đặt từ kiểu trực tiếp trong tiếng Anh, nên dễ viết sai như where is..., what time does..., if was I....
formPatterns: Can you tell me + question word + subject + verb...
Do you know + if/whether + subject + verb...
I wonder + question word + subject + verb...
asked + someone + question word + subject + verb...
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường giữ trật tự kiểu câu hỏi trực tiếp khi dịch sang tiếng Anh, nên người học dễ đặt động từ trước chủ ngữ sau từ để hỏi. Cần nhớ tiếng Anh trong câu hỏi gián tiếp dùng trật tự câu khẳng định.

title: Negative Questions
summary: Expressing surprise or seeking confirmation.

commonMistakes.right: Isn't this the right train?
commonMistakes.why: In a negative question, the speaker often expects confirmation or shows surprise. The auxiliary comes before the subject, and the not is contracted in speech and writing.
commonMistakes.wrong: Is this not the right train?

commonMistakes.right: Don't you know her?
commonMistakes.why: The auxiliary do/does/did carries the negation in present and past simple questions. We do not usually ask this idea with a simple positive question plus not at the end.
commonMistakes.wrong: Do you know her not?

commonMistakes.right: Aren't you coming with us?
commonMistakes.why: Negative questions can sound surprised or can check that the listener is still coming. In English, the negative form is placed on the auxiliary, not the main verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: Are you not coming with us?

commonMistakes.right: Why didn't you call me?
commonMistakes.why: With wh-questions, the negative comes on the auxiliary after the question word. The order is question word + negative auxiliary + subject + main verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: Why you didn't call me?

acceptedAnswers: Isn't it too late to leave now?
drills.explanation: This is the normal negative question form: auxiliary + not + subject + main verb. It can express surprise or a check for confirmation.
drills.prompt: Build a negative question. Use: it / too late / leave now
drills.target: Isn't it too late to leave now?

acceptedAnswers: Didn't she finish the report?
drills.explanation: In past simple questions, did carries the negation. The main verb stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a negative question: She finished the report.
drills.target: Didn't she finish the report?

acceptedAnswers: Aren't they coming to the meeting?
drills.explanation: Negative questions often sound like the speaker expects a positive answer or is surprised by the situation.
drills.prompt: Build a negative question. Use: they / coming / to the meeting
drills.target: Aren't they coming to the meeting?

acceptedAnswers: Why don't we take a taxi?
drills.explanation: In a suggestion with we, the negative question form is natural and common. The auxiliary do takes the negation.
drills.prompt: Build a negative question. Use: why / we / take a taxi
drills.target: Why don't we take a taxi?

acceptedAnswers: Didn't you say the class was at 3?
choices: Didn't you say the class was at 3?
Do you not say the class was at 3?
You didn't say the class was at 3?
drills.explanation: Choose the correct negative question form. The question word order is correct, and did is used for past simple.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Didn't you say the class was at 3?

acceptedAnswers: Aren't you coming with us?
choices: Aren't you coming with us?
Are you coming with us not?
Do you not coming with us?
drills.explanation: The negative comes on the auxiliary be, not on the main verb. The other options are ungrammatical.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Aren't you coming with us?

acceptedAnswers: Isn't this the place you wanted?
drills.explanation: This form shows surprise and checks information. The negative is placed on the auxiliary is.
drills.prompt: Build a negative question. Use: this / the place / you wanted
drills.target: Isn't this the place you wanted?

acceptedAnswers: Don't they know the answer?
drills.explanation: For present simple questions with they, do becomes don't in the negative question.
drills.prompt: Rewrite as a negative question: They know the answer.
drills.target: Don't they know the answer?

acceptedAnswers: Why isn't he answering his phone?
drills.explanation: With wh-questions, put the negative after the question word and before the subject. The main verb stays in the -ing form here because it is a continuous action.
drills.prompt: Build a negative question. Use: why / he / answering his phone
drills.target: Why isn't he answering his phone?

acceptedAnswers: Isn't she your teacher?
drills.explanation: A short negative question can be used to confirm something the speaker thinks may be true.
drills.prompt: Build a negative question. Use: she / your teacher
drills.target: Isn't she your teacher?

explanation: Negative questions are questions with not on the auxiliary verb: isn't, aren't, don't, didn't, isn't, wasn't, and so on. They are often used to show surprise, doubt, or to confirm something the speaker expects to be true. In wh-questions, the question word comes first, then the negative auxiliary, then the subject.
formPatterns: Use do/does/did for simple tenses; use be for be-questions; use modal + not for modal questions
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường chuyển trực tiếp kiểu câu hỏi phủ định sang tiếng Anh bằng cách đặt not ở cuối câu hoặc dùng trật tự từ tiếng Việt. Trong tiếng Anh, not đi sau trợ động từ, và câu hỏi vẫn phải giữ trật tự đảo của trợ động từ và chủ ngữ.

title: Double Negatives
summary: Why hardly and barely already carry the negation.

commonMistakes.right: He hardly ever goes out on weeknights.
commonMistakes.why: Hardly already has a negative meaning, so you do not add another negative word like 'not' in the same clause.
commonMistakes.wrong: He hardly ever doesn't go out on weeknights.

commonMistakes.right: She can barely hear the speaker from the back row.
commonMistakes.why: Barely already means 'only just' and carries a negative sense, so 'can't barely' is incorrect.
commonMistakes.wrong: She can't barely hear the speaker from the back row.

commonMistakes.right: I hardly knew anyone at the party.
commonMistakes.why: Hardly makes the sentence negative in meaning, so adding 'not' gives a double negative that is ungrammatical in standard English.
commonMistakes.wrong: I hardly didn't know anyone at the party.

commonMistakes.right: We barely had enough time to finish the test.
commonMistakes.why: Barely already expresses a near-negation, so adding another negative word creates an incorrect double negative.
commonMistakes.wrong: We barely didn't have enough time to finish the test.

acceptedAnswers: He hardly ever goes out on weeknights.
choices: He hardly ever doesn't go out on weeknights.
He hardly ever goes out on weeknights.
He doesn't hardly ever goes out on weeknights.
drills.explanation: Hardly already carries a negative meaning, so the sentence does not need another negative word.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He hardly ever goes out on weeknights.

acceptedAnswers: She can barely hear the speaker from the back row.
choices: She can't barely hear the speaker from the back row.
She can barely hear the speaker from the back row.
She can hardly can't hear the speaker from the back row.
drills.explanation: Barely already means 'only just' and has a negative sense, so it should not be combined with another negative word.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She can barely hear the speaker from the back row.

acceptedAnswers: I hardly knew anyone at the party.
choices: I hardly didn't know anyone at the party.
I hardly knew anyone at the party.
I didn't hardly know anyone at the party.
drills.explanation: Hardly already makes the clause negative in meaning, so adding 'not' creates an incorrect double negative.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I hardly knew anyone at the party.

acceptedAnswers: We barely had enough time to finish the test.
choices: We barely didn't have enough time to finish the test.
We barely had enough time to finish the test.
We didn't barely have enough time to finish the test.
drills.explanation: Barely is already negative in meaning, so the sentence should not add another negative form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: We barely had enough time to finish the test.

acceptedAnswers: not
drills.explanation: Hardly already has a negative meaning, so you do not add another negative word in the same clause.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence with one word: He hardly ever goes out on weeknights, so he does ___ need much money for transport.
drills.target: not

acceptedAnswers: barely
drills.explanation: Barely already carries a negative sense, so it is the correct adverb here.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence with one word: I could ___ finish the exam before the bell rang.
drills.target: barely

acceptedAnswers: She hardly spoke to anyone at the meeting.
drills.explanation: Hardly already shows that the amount was very small, so no extra negative word is needed.
drills.prompt: Build a correct sentence using: she / hardly / speak / to anyone / at the meeting
drills.target: She hardly spoke to anyone at the meeting.

acceptedAnswers: The children barely touched their lunch.
drills.explanation: Barely is enough to show that they ate only a very small amount, so the sentence should stay positive in form.
drills.prompt: Build a correct sentence using: the children / barely / touch / their lunch
drills.target: The children barely touched their lunch.

acceptedAnswers: I hardly ever get any free time on weekdays.
drills.explanation: Hardly ever already has negative meaning, so the sentence should not add 'not' or another negative form.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence correctly without changing the meaning: I don't get much free time on weekdays.
drills.target: I hardly ever get any free time on weekdays.

acceptedAnswers: She could barely stand after the long hike.
drills.explanation: Barely shows that she was only just able to stand, which is the natural way to express this meaning.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: She couldn't barely stand after the long hike.
drills.target: She could barely stand after the long hike.

explanation: Hardly and barely already carry a negative meaning. In standard English, you normally do not add another negative word like not in the same clause, because that creates an incorrect double negative. This is especially important in formal writing and IELTS tasks.
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt đôi khi thêm not sau hardly/barely để nhấn mạnh phủ định, nhưng trong tiếng Anh chuẩn điều đó thường sai.

title: Echo Questions
summary: Short follow-up questions that show interest in speech.

commonMistakes.right: A: I got the job. B: You did? That's great news.
commonMistakes.why: An echo question repeats the auxiliary or modal to show interest. "Did you?" is not the wrong form here; the mistake is making the follow-up a full wh-question when you only want surprise or interest.
commonMistakes.wrong: A: I got the job. B: Why did you get the job? That's great news.

commonMistakes.right: A: She can speak French. B: Can she? I didn't know that.
commonMistakes.why: An echo question mirrors the auxiliary and subject. Using a statement instead of the short question does not work as an echo question.
commonMistakes.wrong: A: She can speak French. B: She can speak French? I didn't know that.

commonMistakes.right: A: They have moved to Canada. B: Have they? I hope they are happy there.
commonMistakes.why: With the present perfect, the echo question repeats "have" before the subject. A statement with rising intonation is not a true echo question pattern in written English.
commonMistakes.wrong: A: They have moved to Canada. B: They moved to Canada? I hope they are happy there.

commonMistakes.right: A: He is coming tomorrow. B: Is he? I thought he was busy.
commonMistakes.why: For the present simple of be, the echo question uses the same form of be before the subject. Repeating the full statement as a question is not the correct echo form.
commonMistakes.wrong: A: He is coming tomorrow. B: He is coming tomorrow? I thought he was busy.

acceptedAnswers: Do you?
choices: Do you?
You do?
Do you do?
drills.explanation: An echo question repeats the auxiliary to show interest or surprise. Here, the correct short question is formed with do + subject.
drills.prompt:
Choose the correct echo question.
A: I like coffee.
B: ____
drills.target: Do you?

acceptedAnswers: Are you?
drills.explanation: With the verb be, the echo question repeats the same form of be before the subject.
drills.prompt:
A: I'm ready.
B: ____
drills.target: Are you?

acceptedAnswers: Can she?
drills.explanation: The modal verb can moves to the front in the echo question, followed by the subject.
drills.prompt:
A: She can swim very well.
B: ____
drills.target: Can she?

acceptedAnswers: Has he?
choices: Has he?
Does he has?
He has?
drills.explanation: In the present perfect, the auxiliary have comes before the subject. The other options are not correct echo-question forms.
drills.prompt:
Choose the correct echo question.
A: He has left already.
B: ____
drills.target: Has he?

acceptedAnswers: Did they?
drills.explanation: For a past simple statement, the echo question uses did plus the subject.
drills.prompt:
A: They visited Paris last year.
B: ____
drills.target: Did they?

acceptedAnswers: Will it?
choices: Will it?
It will?
Does it will?
drills.explanation: A future with will is echoed by moving will before the subject.
drills.prompt:
Choose the correct echo question.
A: It will rain later.
B: ____
drills.target: Will it?

acceptedAnswers: Didn't you?
drills.explanation: Negative echo questions are common when the speaker is surprised or checking information. The auxiliary stays negative and comes before the subject.
drills.prompt:
A: You didn't call me.
B: ____
drills.target: Didn't you?

acceptedAnswers: Were they?
choices: Were they?
Did they were?
They were?
drills.explanation: The past form of be is echoed with were before the subject.
drills.prompt:
Choose the correct echo question.
A: They were late.
B: ____
drills.target: Were they?

acceptedAnswers: You do?
Do you?
drills.explanation: A full echo question can be written with normal word order or as a short answer-like follow-up in informal speech. The key is that it repeats the auxiliary and subject to show interest.
drills.prompt:
Rewrite the follow-up as a correct echo question.
A: I work from home.
B: You work from home?
drills.target: You do?

acceptedAnswers: Isn't it?
drills.explanation: Negative echoes can also be used to confirm what was said, especially with be. The auxiliary is negative and comes before the subject.
drills.prompt:
A: It is cold today.
B: ____
drills.target: Isn't it?

explanation: Echo questions are short follow-up questions that repeat the auxiliary verb, modal verb, or form of be from the previous sentence. They are used to show interest, surprise, or to check information: I can help. Can you? / She has arrived. Has she? / It is late. Is it? In written English, use the correct question form rather than a statement with rising intonation.
formPatterns: affirmative statement + echo question with auxiliary/modal + subject
negative statement + negative echo question for surprise or confirmation
be / have / do / modal is repeated in the echo question
the echo question usually has the same tense as the original statement

title: Verb + Infinitive
summary: Decide to, hope to, and the pattern list. Vietnamese makes no such distinction.

commonMistakes.right: I want to study English.
commonMistakes.why: After want, use to + verb. In Vietnamese, the main verb is often used directly, so learners may leave out to.
commonMistakes.wrong: I want study English.

commonMistakes.right: She decided to move to Hanoi.
commonMistakes.why: After decide, use to + verb. Vietnamese often uses a verb phrase without a clear infinitive marker, so to is sometimes omitted.
commonMistakes.wrong: She decided move to Hanoi.

commonMistakes.right: We hope to finish the project soon.
commonMistakes.why: After hope, use to + verb. The Vietnamese equivalent does not need a separate infinitive marker, which can lead to omission.
commonMistakes.wrong: We hope finish the project soon.

commonMistakes.right: He needs to practise more.
commonMistakes.why: After need, use to + verb. Do not use the bare verb form here.
commonMistakes.wrong: He needs practise more.

acceptedAnswers: to
drills.explanation: After want, need, decide, hope, and many other verbs, English uses to + verb. The word to marks the infinitive.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I want ___ learn IELTS vocabulary.
drills.target: to

acceptedAnswers: I want to improve my speaking.
drills.explanation: Want is followed by to + verb. The full infinitive is to improve.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: want / improve / my speaking
drills.target: I want to improve my speaking.

acceptedAnswers: She hopes to get a higher band score.
drills.explanation: Hope is followed by to + verb. Get is the correct infinitive form here.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using hope: She has the intention of getting a higher band score.
drills.target: She hopes to get a higher band score.

acceptedAnswers: We decided to leave early.
choices: We decided leave early.
We decided to leave early.
We decided leaving early.
drills.explanation: Decide is followed by to + verb, so to leave is correct. The other options miss the infinitive form or use the wrong verb pattern.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: We decided to leave early.

acceptedAnswers: to
drills.explanation: After verbs like decide, hope, want, need, plan, and try, English commonly uses to before the next verb.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: They plan ___ study in Australia.
drills.target: to

acceptedAnswers: He needs to study harder for the exam.
drills.explanation: Need is followed by to + verb in this pattern. Study is the correct infinitive form.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: He needs study harder for the exam.
drills.target: He needs to study harder for the exam.

acceptedAnswers: I hope to travel to Japan next year.
choices: I hope travel to Japan next year.
I hope to travel to Japan next year.
I hope traveling to Japan next year.
drills.explanation: Hope takes to + verb, so to travel is correct. The other choices use the wrong verb pattern.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I hope to travel to Japan next year.

acceptedAnswers: to
drills.explanation: The infinitive marker to comes before the base verb in these patterns. It is not used alone as the main verb.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She wants ___ become a doctor.
drills.target: to

acceptedAnswers: She wants to become a doctor.
choices: She wants become a doctor.
She wants to become a doctor.
She wants becoming a doctor.
drills.explanation: Want is followed by to + verb, so to become is correct. The other options use the wrong structure.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She wants to become a doctor.

acceptedAnswers: I decided to take the bus.
drills.explanation: Decided is the past tense of decide, and it is followed by to + verb. Take is the correct infinitive here.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: decided / take / the bus
drills.target: I decided to take the bus.

acceptedAnswers: to
drills.explanation: Many common verbs are followed by to + verb. In this sentence, to is needed before study.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: We decided ___ study together.
drills.target: to

acceptedAnswers: They plan to start a new course.
drills.explanation: Plan is followed by to + verb. Start is the correct infinitive form.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: plan / start / a new course
drills.target: They plan to start a new course.

acceptedAnswers: You need to speak more clearly.
drills.explanation: Need is followed by to + verb, and more clearly is the correct adverb form after speak.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: You need speak more clearly.
drills.target: You need to speak more clearly.

acceptedAnswers: They hope to pass the exam.
They hope to pass the exam
drills.explanation: Hope is followed by to + verb. Pass is the correct infinitive here.
drills.prompt: Rewrite using hope: They are wishing that they pass the exam.
drills.target: They hope to pass the exam.

explanation:
Verb + infinitive means that some verbs are followed by to + the base form of the verb. Common examples are want to, need to, decide to, hope to, plan to, and try to. After these verbs, English does not use the bare verb form: we say decide to go, not decide go. In IELTS writing and speaking, this pattern is very common and needs to become automatic.

A useful way to remember it is to learn the whole phrase, not just the verb. For example, learn want to do, hope to go, need to study, decide to leave. Vietnamese often uses a verb phrase without a separate marker like to, so learners may forget to add to in English. That omission is a frequent error.

There are also some verbs that can be followed by a noun + to + verb, such as ask someone to do something, tell someone to do something, and allow someone to do something. This lesson focuses mainly on the basic pattern with one verb followed by another.
explanationVi:
Trong tiếng Anh, một số động từ phải đi với to + động từ nguyên mẫu. Nghĩa là sau want, need, decide, hope, plan, try... ta dùng to + verb. Ví dụ: I want to study, She decided to leave, We hope to win. Không dùng dạng động từ trần sau các động từ này: I want study, She decided leave là sai.

Điểm này dễ sai với người Việt vì tiếng Việt thường không có từ tương đương với to. Trong tiếng Việt, ta có thể nói “muốn học”, “quyết định đi”, “hy vọng đỗ” mà không cần một từ đánh dấu nguyên mẫu riêng. Vì vậy người học hay bỏ quên to trong tiếng Anh.

Cách nhớ tốt nhất là học theo cụm cố định: want to do, need to check, decide to leave, hope to get, plan to work. Khi làm bài viết và nói IELTS, hãy kiểm tra xem động từ đứng trước có cần to không. Nếu thuộc nhóm này, luôn nhớ thêm to trước động từ tiếp theo.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không có từ đánh dấu nguyên mẫu như to, nên người học hay bỏ to sau want, need, decide, hope, plan. Cũng dễ nhầm giữa ý nghĩa “muốn/quyết định/hy vọng” với hình thức động từ đi sau nó. Nên học cả cụm động từ: want to do, decide to leave, hope to pass.

title: Verb + Gerund
summary: Enjoy, avoid, and the verbs taking -ing.

commonMistakes.right: I enjoy reading books in my free time.
commonMistakes.why: Enjoy is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive. In English we say enjoy doing something, not enjoy to do something.
commonMistakes.wrong: I enjoy to read books in my free time.

commonMistakes.right: She avoids eating too much sugar.
commonMistakes.why: Avoid is followed by a gerund. The verb after avoid should be in -ing form.
commonMistakes.wrong: She avoids to eat too much sugar.

commonMistakes.right: He admitted breaking the window.
commonMistakes.why: Admit is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive. The -ing form is the correct pattern here.
commonMistakes.wrong: He admitted to break the window.

commonMistakes.right: They suggested going by train.
commonMistakes.why: Suggest is followed by a gerund. We use suggest doing something, not suggest to do something.
commonMistakes.wrong: They suggested to go by train.

acceptedAnswers: reading
drills.explanation: After enjoy, we use a gerund. The verb is in -ing form.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I enjoy ____ after dinner.
drills.target: reading

acceptedAnswers: I avoid eating fast food.
choices: I avoid eating fast food.
I avoid to eat fast food.
I avoid eat fast food.
drills.explanation: Avoid is followed by a gerund. The correct pattern is avoid + verb-ing.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I avoid eating fast food.

acceptedAnswers: She suggested meeting earlier.
drills.explanation: Suggest is followed by a gerund. Meeting is the correct verb form here.
drills.prompt: Use these words to make a correct sentence: She / suggest / meet / earlier.
drills.target: She suggested meeting earlier.

acceptedAnswers: avoiding
drills.explanation: After the preposition of, we use a gerund. Avoiding fits the structure of the sentence.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He is afraid of ____ public speaking.
drills.target: avoiding

acceptedAnswers: He admitted stealing the money.
drills.explanation: Admit is followed by a gerund. The sentence needs stealing, not to steal.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: He admitted to steal the money.
drills.target: He admitted stealing the money.

acceptedAnswers: I dislike waiting in traffic.
choices: I dislike to wait in traffic.
I dislike waiting in traffic.
I dislike wait in traffic.
drills.explanation: Dislike can take a gerund. The -ing form is the correct choice here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I dislike waiting in traffic.

acceptedAnswers: swimming
drills.explanation: Enjoy is followed by a gerund. Swimming is the correct form after enjoy.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: My brother enjoys ____ in the sea.
drills.target: swimming

acceptedAnswers: We suggested taking a taxi.
drills.explanation: Suggest is followed by a gerund. Taking a taxi is the correct structure.
drills.prompt: Use these words to make a correct sentence: We / suggest / take / a taxi.
drills.target: We suggested taking a taxi.

acceptedAnswers: She stopped smoking last year.
choices: She stopped smoking last year.
She stopped to smoke last year.
drills.explanation: This is a meaning contrast. Stopped smoking means she quit the habit.
drills.prompt: Choose the sentence that means she quit the habit.
drills.target: She stopped smoking last year.

acceptedAnswers: She stopped to smoke last year.
choices: She stopped smoking last year.
She stopped to smoke last year.
drills.explanation: This is a meaning contrast. Stopped to smoke means she paused another activity in order to smoke.
drills.prompt: Choose the sentence that means she paused another activity in order to smoke.
drills.target: She stopped to smoke last year.

acceptedAnswers: finishing
drills.explanation: Finish is followed by a gerund. Finishing is the correct form in this sentence.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: They finished ____ their homework before dinner.
drills.target: finishing

acceptedAnswers: He suggested seeing a doctor.
choices: He suggested seeing a doctor.
He suggested to see a doctor.
He suggested see a doctor.
drills.explanation: Suggest is followed by a gerund, so seeing is correct.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He suggested seeing a doctor.

acceptedAnswers: I dislike getting up early.
I hate getting up early.
drills.explanation: Dislike and hate can both be followed by a gerund. Both sentences are correct English.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a verb that can also take a gerund: I do not like getting up early.
drills.target: I dislike getting up early.

acceptedAnswers: She avoids driving at night.
drills.explanation: Avoid is followed by a gerund. Driving is the correct form after avoids.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: She avoids to drive at night.
drills.target: She avoids driving at night.

explanation:
Many English verbs are followed by a gerund, which is the -ing form used as the object of the verb. Common examples are enjoy, avoid, finish, dislike, admit, suggest, mind, and consider: enjoy reading, avoid eating, finish working, suggest going. After these verbs, the infinitive with to is usually wrong: we say I enjoy reading, not I enjoy to read. This point is especially important for Vietnamese learners because Vietnamese often uses a verb form that looks closer to a bare verb or an action phrase, so the English -ing pattern must be memorized with each verb.

Some verbs change meaning with an infinitive, but this lesson is about verbs that take gerund forms. For contrast, verb + infinitive means patterns like want to go, decide to study, hope to pass. Those verbs are different from the verbs in this lesson. Also remember the meaning contrast in pairs like stop smoking vs stop to smoke: both are correct, but they mean different things.
explanationVi:
Trong tiếng Anh, một số động từ phải đi với động từ thêm -ing (gerund), không dùng to + động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ: enjoy reading, avoid eating, finish doing, suggest going, admit stealing. Đây là lỗi rất hay gặp với người Việt vì trong tiếng Việt sau các từ như “thích”, “tránh”, “gợi ý”, “xong” thường dùng động từ khá tự nhiên, nhưng trong tiếng Anh phải nhớ đúng mẫu đi kèm của từng động từ. Với nhóm này, hãy học cả cụm: enjoy doing, avoid doing, suggest doing, admit doing, finish doing.

Điều quan trọng là phải phân biệt với verb + infinitive. Verb + infinitive dùng to + động từ: want to go, decide to study, hope to pass. Còn verb + gerund dùng động từ thêm -ing: enjoy going, avoid eating, suggest studying. Không được đổi lẫn hai mẫu này. Ngoài ra, có một số cặp đặc biệt đổi nghĩa theo cấu trúc, ví dụ stop smoking nghĩa là bỏ hút thuốc, còn stop to smoke nghĩa là dừng lại để hút thuốc. Hai câu này đều đúng nhưng nghĩa khác nhau.
formPatterns: verb + gerund after prepositions: of doing
contrast with verb + infinitive: want to do, decide to do
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường bị ảnh hưởng bởi cách dùng động từ trong tiếng Việt nên dễ viết sai kiểu to + V sau enjoy/avoid/suggest/finish/admit/dislike. Cần ghi nhớ cụm cố định của từng động từ. Đặc biệt phân biệt với verb + infinitive: muốn làm gì = want to do, nhưng thích/ghét/tránh/làm xong/gợi ý thường đi với V-ing trong bài này.

minimalPairs.meaning: She quit the habit completely.
minimalPairs.sentence: She stopped smoking.

minimalPairs.meaning: She paused what she was doing in order to smoke.
minimalPairs.sentence: She stopped to smoke.

title: Verbs Taking Both Forms
summary: Remember, forget, and stop, where the choice changes the meaning.

commonMistakes.right: I remembered to call my mother.
commonMistakes.why: Remember + to-infinitive means you did not forget to do the action. In Vietnamese, learners often use the same idea for both nhớ làm and nhớ đã làm, but English makes this distinction.
commonMistakes.wrong: I remembered calling my mother.

commonMistakes.right: I remember meeting her at the conference.
commonMistakes.why: Remember + gerund means you have a memory of the past action. It does not mean you did the action now or that you must do it later.
commonMistakes.wrong: I remember to meet her at the conference.

commonMistakes.right: She stopped smoking last year.
commonMistakes.why: Stop + gerund means to quit an activity or habit completely. Vietnamese learners may translate it as dừng để làm gì đó, but English uses the gerund here for quitting.
commonMistakes.wrong: She stopped to smoke last year.

commonMistakes.right: He stopped to answer the phone.
commonMistakes.why: Stop + to-infinitive means to pause one activity in order to do another. It does not mean he quit answering the phone as a habit.
commonMistakes.wrong: He stopped answering the phone.

commonMistakes.right: I forgot to send the email.
commonMistakes.why: Forget + to-infinitive means you did not remember to do the action, so it was not done.
commonMistakes.wrong: I forgot sending the email.

acceptedAnswers: I remembered to lock the door.
drills.explanation: Remember + to-infinitive means you did the remembering before the action, so the action happened because you did not forget it.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence with remember + to-infinitive. Use: remember / lock / the door.
drills.target: I remembered to lock the door.

acceptedAnswers: I remember locking the door.
drills.explanation: Remember + gerund means you have a memory of the past action itself.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence with remember + gerund. Use: remember / lock / the door.
drills.target: I remember locking the door.

acceptedAnswers: He forgot to buy milk.
drills.explanation: Forget + to-infinitive means he did not remember to do the action, so it was not done.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence with forget + to-infinitive. Use: he / forget / buy / milk.
drills.target: He forgot to buy milk.

acceptedAnswers: He forgot buying milk.
drills.explanation: Forget + gerund means he has no memory of doing the action. This is different from forgetting to do something.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence with forget + gerund. Use: he / forget / buy / milk.
drills.target: He forgot buying milk.

acceptedAnswers: She stopped to rest.
choices: She stopped resting.
She stopped to rest.
She stops to rest.
drills.explanation: Stop + to-infinitive means pause one activity in order to do another. Only one option has that meaning.
drills.prompt: Choose the sentence that means she paused what she was doing in order to rest.
drills.target: She stopped to rest.

acceptedAnswers: She stopped smoking.
choices: She stopped to smoke.
She stopped smoking.
She stops smoking.
drills.explanation: Stop + gerund means quit a habit or activity completely. Only one option means she quit smoking.
drills.prompt: Choose the sentence that means she quit the habit.
drills.target: She stopped smoking.

acceptedAnswers: I remember meeting him in Hanoi.
choices: I remember meeting him in Hanoi.
I remembered to meet him in Hanoi.
I stop meeting him in Hanoi.
drills.explanation: Remember + gerund means you have a memory of the meeting. Remember + to-infinitive would mean you did not forget to meet him, which is a different idea.
drills.prompt: Choose the sentence that means the speaker has a memory of the action.
drills.target: I remember meeting him in Hanoi.

acceptedAnswers: She stopped working at six.
choices: She stopped to work at six.
She stopped working at six.
She remembered working at six.
drills.explanation: Stop + gerund means to quit the activity. Stop + to-infinitive would mean she paused something else in order to work.
drills.prompt: Choose the sentence that means the person quit the activity.
drills.target: She stopped working at six.

acceptedAnswers: Did you remember to send the report?
drills.explanation: Use remember + to-infinitive when you ask whether the person did not forget to do something.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so it asks about not forgetting an action: You sent the report, and I want to know whether you did not forget. Start with: Did you remember...
drills.target: Did you remember to send the report?

acceptedAnswers: I remember seeing her at the airport.
drills.explanation: Use remember + gerund to show a memory of a past event, not a planned future action.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so it shows a memory of the event: I have a memory of seeing her at the airport.
drills.target: I remember seeing her at the airport.

acceptedAnswers: I stopped to check my phone.
drills.explanation: Stop + to-infinitive means pause one action in order to do another action.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so it means you paused another activity in order to check your phone.
drills.target: I stopped to check my phone.

acceptedAnswers: I stopped checking my phone.
drills.explanation: Stop + gerund means quit the activity completely.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so it means you quit the habit of checking your phone.
drills.target: I stopped checking my phone.

acceptedAnswers: to open
drills.explanation: After remember, to-infinitive means the action was something you did not forget to do.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She remembered ___ the window before she left.
drills.target: to open

acceptedAnswers: opening
drills.explanation: After remember, a gerund shows a memory of the action that happened in the past.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: She remembers ___ the window before she left.
drills.target: opening

acceptedAnswers: to answer
drills.explanation: After stop, to-infinitive shows a pause in order to do another action.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He stopped ___ the phone to look at the screen.
drills.target: to answer

acceptedAnswers: answering
drills.explanation: After stop, a gerund shows that the activity ended completely.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He stopped ___ the phone because he was tired.
drills.target: answering

explanation: Some verbs can take both a to-infinitive and a gerund, but the meaning changes. With remember, forget, and stop, the form after the verb is not just grammar; it changes the message. Remember + to-infinitive usually means you did not forget to do something. Remember + gerund means you have a memory of something that happened. Forget works in the same contrast: forget to do = not do it because you did not remember; forget doing = have no memory of doing it. Stop + to-infinitive means pause one action in order to do another, while stop + gerund means quit an activity or habit. This is different from verb-plus-infinitive patterns like want to do, and verb-plus-gerund patterns like enjoy doing, where the choice is mainly grammatical and the meaning is stable. For Vietnamese learners, the main risk is translating all these as một mẫu duy nhất like nhớ/quên/dừng + V, but English separates the meanings clearly.
explanationVi: Một số động từ trong tiếng Anh có thể đi với cả to-infinitive và gerund, nhưng nghĩa sẽ thay đổi. Với remember, forget và stop, không chỉ là chọn cấu trúc đúng; chính dạng theo sau động từ làm thay đổi ý. Remember + to-infinitive thường có nghĩa là “không quên làm việc gì đó”. Remember + gerund có nghĩa là “có ký ức về việc đã xảy ra”. Forget cũng có sự đối lập tương tự: forget to do = quên nên không làm; forget doing = không còn nhớ là mình đã làm. Stop + to-infinitive nghĩa là “dừng lại để làm việc khác”, còn stop + gerund nghĩa là “ngừng hẳn một thói quen hay hoạt động”. Điểm này khác với verb-plus-infinitive như want to do, và verb-plus-gerund như enjoy doing, vì ở đó lựa chọn chủ yếu là cấu trúc cố định; còn ở đây lựa chọn làm đổi nghĩa. Người học Việt hay nhầm vì trong tiếng Việt nhiều khi chỉ dùng một mẫu chung như “nhớ/quên/dừng + V”, nhưng tiếng Anh tách nghĩa rất rõ.
formPatterns: remember + to-infinitive = not forget to do something
remember + gerund = have a memory of something that happened
forget + to-infinitive = not remember to do something
forget + gerund = have no memory of doing something
stop + to-infinitive = pause one action in order to do another
stop + gerund = quit an activity or habit
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng cùng một động từ như “nhớ”, “quên”, “dừng” với một động từ theo sau, nên người học dễ nghĩ tiếng Anh cũng giống vậy. Cần nhắc rõ: remember/forget/stop có thể đổi nghĩa tùy theo to-infinitive hay gerund.

minimalPairs.meaning: The speaker did not forget to do the action.

minimalPairs.sentence: I remember calling my mother.

minimalPairs.meaning: He paused one action in order to do another.
minimalPairs.sentence: She stopped to answer the phone.

title: Infinitive of Purpose
summary: Expressing why with to plus verb.

commonMistakes.right: I went to the library to study.
commonMistakes.why: Use to + verb after a purpose clause to explain why you did something.
commonMistakes.wrong: I went to the library for study.

commonMistakes.right: She saved money to buy a laptop.
commonMistakes.why: Use the infinitive after to when the second action is the purpose.
commonMistakes.wrong: She saved money for buy a laptop.

commonMistakes.right: He left early to catch the bus.
commonMistakes.why: Use to + base verb to show purpose, not a finite verb form.
commonMistakes.wrong: He left early so he catch the bus.

commonMistakes.right: They turned on the heater to warm the room.
commonMistakes.why: After to, English uses the base form of the verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: They turned on the heater to warmed the room.

acceptedAnswers: to study
drills.explanation: To express purpose, English uses to + base verb.
drills.prompt: I went to the library ___ for my exam.

acceptedAnswers: to catch the bus

acceptedAnswers: I called my friend to ask for help.
drills.explanation: A purpose clause can come at the end of the sentence and show why the action happened.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence: gọi bạn để xin giúp đỡ.
drills.target: I called my friend to ask for help.

acceptedAnswers: to buy
drills.explanation: To + base verb is the normal form for purpose.
drills.prompt: She saved money ___ a laptop.
drills.target: to buy

acceptedAnswers: They moved to the city to find work.
drills.explanation: The second to-infinitive explains the purpose of moving.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence to show purpose: They moved to the city because they wanted to find work.
drills.target: They moved to the city to find work.

acceptedAnswers: to warm
drills.explanation: After to, use the base form of the verb.
drills.prompt: They turned on the heater ___ the room.
drills.target: to warm

acceptedAnswers: She went to the market to buy vegetables.
drills.explanation: The infinitive of purpose tells us why she went to the market.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence: cô ấy đi chợ để mua rau.

acceptedAnswers: He studied hard to pass the exam.
Choose the correct sentence.
choices: He studied hard to pass the exam.
He studied hard for pass the exam.
He studied hard to passing the exam.
drills.explanation: Only to + base verb is correct here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He studied hard to pass the exam.

acceptedAnswers: I opened the window to get some fresh air.
drills.explanation: The infinitive phrase shows the purpose of opening the window.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: I opened the window for get some fresh air.
drills.target: I opened the window to get some fresh air.

explanation: We use the infinitive of purpose to say why someone does something. The structure is to + base verb: I went to the shop to buy milk. It answers the question Why? and often comes after the main action. After to, use the base form of the verb, not -ing or a past tense form.
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường chuyển trực tiếp cấu trúc “để + động từ” sang tiếng Anh và quên dùng to + động từ nguyên mẫu.

title: Gerund as Subject
summary: Swimming is good for you, and its singular agreement.

commonMistakes.right: Swimming is good exercise.
commonMistakes.why: A gerund phrase can be the subject of a sentence. In this structure, the verb after it is singular: is.
commonMistakes.wrong: Swimming are good exercise.

commonMistakes.right: Reading helps me relax.
commonMistakes.why: When a gerund phrase is the subject, it takes a singular verb like helps, not help.
commonMistakes.wrong: Reading help me relax.

commonMistakes.right: Driving at night is tiring.
commonMistakes.why: The whole gerund phrase acts as one subject, so the main verb should be singular.
commonMistakes.wrong: Driving at night are tiring.

commonMistakes.right: Being late makes a bad impression.
commonMistakes.why: A gerund phrase can begin with being and still function as a singular subject.
commonMistakes.wrong: Being late make a bad impression.

acceptedAnswers: Swimming is good exercise.
choices: Swimming are good exercise.
Swimming is good exercise.
Swimming be good exercise.
drills.explanation: The gerund phrase Swimming is the subject, so the verb is singular: is.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Swimming is good exercise.

acceptedAnswers: Reading helps me relax.
drills.explanation: The gerund phrase Reading is the subject, so the verb must be singular: helps.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence using reading / help / me / relax. Use reading as the subject.
drills.target: Reading helps me relax.

acceptedAnswers: Driving at night is tiring.
drills.explanation: A gerund phrase can be a subject. Because the subject is singular, the verb is singular too: is tiring.
drills.prompt: Rewrite this sentence so it starts with a gerund phrase as the subject: It is tiring to drive at night.
drills.target: Driving at night is tiring.

acceptedAnswers: Being late makes a bad impression.
choices: Being late make a bad impression.
Being late makes a bad impression.
Being late making a bad impression.
drills.explanation: The gerund phrase Being late is a singular subject, so the verb must be makes.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Being late makes a bad impression.

acceptedAnswers: Practicing every day improves my English.
drills.explanation: The gerund phrase Practicing every day is the subject, so the verb is singular: improves.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence about practice / every day / improve / my English. Make practice the subject.
drills.target: Practicing every day improves my English.

acceptedAnswers: Traveling by train is cheaper than flying.
choices: Traveling by train are cheaper than flying.
Traveling by train is cheaper than flying.
Traveling by train be cheaper than flying.
drills.explanation: Traveling by train is a gerund phrase used as one singular subject, so the verb is is.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Traveling by train is cheaper than flying.

acceptedAnswers: Studying in a quiet place helps me focus.
drills.explanation: The gerund phrase Studying in a quiet place is the subject. The main verb must agree with this singular subject: helps.
drills.prompt: Build a sentence with studying in a quiet place / help / me / focus. Use the gerund phrase as the subject.
drills.target: Studying in a quiet place helps me focus.

acceptedAnswers: takes
Learning a new language takes time.
drills.explanation: Learning a new language is the subject of the sentence, so the verb is singular: takes.
drills.prompt: Learning a new language ____ time.
drills.target: takes

acceptedAnswers: Running in the morning is good for your health.
choices: Running in the morning are good for your health.
Running in the morning is good for your health.
Running in the morning be good for your health.
drills.explanation: The gerund phrase Running in the morning functions as a singular subject, so the verb should be is.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Running in the morning is good for your health.

explanation:
A gerund phrase can work as the subject of a sentence. When it does, the whole phrase is treated as singular, so the main verb is usually singular too: Swimming is..., Reading helps..., Being late makes....

This is common in English because the activity itself is the topic of the sentence. In IELTS writing and speaking, gerund subjects are useful for general statements, reasons, and opinions.

Remember that the subject is the whole gerund phrase, not just the -ing verb. For example, Driving at night is tiring, not Driving at night are tiring.
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt hay dùng động từ nguyên thể hoặc quên chia động từ theo chủ ngữ trong tiếng Anh. Với chủ ngữ là cụm gerund, tiếng Anh vẫn phải chia động từ số ít: Swimming is..., không phải Swimming are....

title: Preposition + Gerund
summary: Why every verb after a preposition takes -ing.

commonMistakes.right: I’m interested in learning English.
commonMistakes.why: After a preposition, the verb must be in the -ing form. 'In learn' is not grammatical here.
commonMistakes.wrong: I’m interested in learn English.

commonMistakes.right: She left without saying goodbye.
commonMistakes.why: After the preposition 'without', English uses a gerund, not the base verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: She left without say goodbye.

commonMistakes.right: He apologized for being late.
commonMistakes.why: After 'for', the verb should take -ing when it follows a preposition.
commonMistakes.wrong: He apologized for be late.

commonMistakes.right: They discussed moving to a new office.
commonMistakes.why: After 'about', 'discuss' does not take an infinitive; the following verb needs -ing after the preposition.
commonMistakes.wrong: They discussed about move to a new office.

acceptedAnswers: in learning
drills.explanation: After a preposition, English uses a gerund (-ing form). 'In' is a preposition, so the verb after it becomes 'learning'.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: interested ____ English

acceptedAnswers: I’m good at cooking.
drills.explanation: The preposition 'at' must be followed by a gerund. 'Cooking' is the correct form here.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: good at / cook
drills.target: I’m good at cooking.

acceptedAnswers: She is afraid of flying.
drills.explanation: After the preposition 'of', the verb takes -ing. 'Flying' is the correct gerund form.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence correctly: She is afraid of fly.
drills.target: She is afraid of flying.

acceptedAnswers: He succeeded in passing the exam.
choices: He succeeded in pass the exam.
He succeeded in passing the exam.
He succeeded to pass the exam.

drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He succeeded in passing the exam.

without use

drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: ____ a calculator
drills.target: without using

drills.explanation: After the preposition 'about', the following verb takes -ing.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: talk about / move to Hanoi
drills.target: They talked about moving to Hanoi.

acceptedAnswers: She left after finishing her homework.
drills.explanation: After 'after', the verb should be in gerund form when it follows a preposition.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence correctly: She left after finish her homework.
drills.target: She left after finishing her homework.

acceptedAnswers: before eating
drills.explanation: After the preposition 'before', use a gerund.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: ____ dinner
drills.target: before eating

acceptedAnswers: We can improve by practicing every day.
choices: We can improve by practice every day.
We can improve by practicing every day.

drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

drills.explanation: After 'of', English uses the -ing form in this structure.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: tired of / wait
drills.target: I’m tired of waiting.

acceptedAnswers: She is used to living alone.
drills.explanation: In the pattern 'be used to', 'to' is a preposition, so it must be followed by a gerund.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence correctly: She is used to live alone.
drills.target: She is used to living alone.

acceptedAnswers: I’m interested in reading history books.
drills.explanation: After 'in', use a gerund. The verb 'read' becomes 'reading'.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: interested in / read history books
drills.target: I’m interested in reading history books.

acceptedAnswers: They left without paying.
They left without paying the bill.
choices: They left without pay.
They left without paying.
They left without to pay.
drills.explanation: After the preposition 'without', only the gerund is correct.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: They left without paying.

acceptedAnswers: She is good at speaking English.
drills.explanation: After 'at', the verb takes -ing. 'Speaking' is the correct gerund.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: good at / speak English
drills.target: She is good at speaking English.

explanation:
When a verb comes after a preposition, English normally uses the gerund form (-ing). The preposition can be one word, like in, at, of, for, about, without, before, after, by, or a two-word pattern such as be used to, be interested in, be afraid of, and look forward to. In these structures, the word after the preposition is not an infinitive and is not the base verb.

This is a common problem for Vietnamese learners because Vietnamese often does not change the verb form after a linking word in the same way English does. So a learner may say 'interested in learn' or 'good at speak'. In English, that is wrong: after a preposition, the verb must usually become -ing. Some expressions are fixed and must be memorized, especially be used to, be interested in, be afraid of, succeed in, and spend time on.
explanationVi:
Trong tiếng Anh, khi động từ đứng sau một giới từ thì động từ đó thường phải đổi sang dạng V-ing. Giới từ có thể là một từ như in, at, of, for, about, without, before, after, by, on, hoặc là cả cụm cố định như be used to, be interested in, be afraid of, look forward to. Điểm quan trọng là sau giới từ, ta không dùng động từ nguyên mẫu và cũng không dùng “to + V”.

Người Việt rất dễ sai ở chỗ này vì trong tiếng Việt, sau các từ tương đương với giới từ, động từ thường không đổi hình thức. Vì vậy người học hay nói kiểu 'interested in learn', 'good at speak', 'without say', hoặc 'talk about go'. Trong tiếng Anh, các câu đó sai; phải dùng V-ing: 'interested in learning', 'good at speaking', 'without saying', 'talking about going'. Có một số cụm cố định cần nhớ vì chúng rất hay gặp trong IELTS: be used to + V-ing, be afraid of + V-ing, be interested in + V-ing, be good at + V-ing, succeed in + V-ing, spend time on + V-ing.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt không biến đổi động từ sau giới từ/tiểu từ theo kiểu thêm -ing như tiếng Anh, nên người học dễ dùng động từ nguyên mẫu sau in, at, of, for, about, without, before, after, by, on.

title: Bare Infinitive
summary: After modals, let, make, and certain perception verbs.

drills.target: She can speak English fluently.

acceptedAnswers: I saw them leave the room.

acceptedAnswers: Choose the sentence that is correct.

Choose the sentence that is correct.
Choose the sentence that is correct.

drills.prompt: Choose the sentence that is correct.
drills.target: Choose the sentence that is correct.

drills.target: My mother made me study harder.

drills.explanation: After hear, both bare infinitive and -ing forms can be correct in some contexts, but the bare infinitive is a common pattern for a complete action. In this lesson, both answers are acceptable because they are both grammatical, but the bare infinitive form is the target pattern.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using a bare infinitive if possible: She heard the baby cry.
drills.target: She heard the baby cry.

acceptedAnswers: They must finish the report today.
choices: They must to finish the report today.
They must finish the report today.

drills.target: They must finish the report today.

acceptedAnswers: Help me open the window.

explanation: A bare infinitive is the base form of the verb without to: go, see, make, let, come, help. In English, it often appears after modal verbs such as can, must, should, and may. It also follows let and make, and it is common after perception verbs like see, hear, and watch when the action is perceived directly. After these words, adding to is usually wrong.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng một động từ nguyên mẫu sau các từ như có thể, phải, để cho, làm cho, thấy/nghe, nên người học dễ thêm to một cách máy móc trong tiếng Anh.

commonMistakes.why: The perfect infinitive is needed because the waiting happened before the apology now being made.
commonMistakes.wrong: I am sorry to keep you waiting.

acceptedAnswers: She seems to have forgotten her keys.

acceptedAnswers: They must have left already.

They must have left already.

drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: They must have left already.

acceptedAnswers: I am sorry to have kept you waiting.
drills.explanation: The apology is about an action that happened earlier, so the perfect infinitive is needed.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using a perfect infinitive: I kept you waiting, and I am sorry about that.
drills.target: I am sorry to have kept you waiting.

acceptedAnswers: She appears to have left early.
drills.explanation: Appears points to the present judgment, while the leaving happened earlier, so have left is correct.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using a perfect infinitive: It looks like she left early.
drills.target: She appears to have left early.

acceptedAnswers: to have been
drills.explanation: To have been is the perfect infinitive form of be. It shows the state existed before another time.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He is believed ______ in the room when the alarm started.
drills.target: to have been

acceptedAnswers: She is said to have won the prize.
choices: She is said to win the prize.
She is said to have won the prize.
She is said winning the prize.
drills.explanation: The perfect infinitive shows that winning happened before the speaking or reporting now.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She is said to have won the prize.

explanation:
The perfect infinitive is to have + past participle, for example to have done, to have finished, to have been. It is used when the action happened before the time of the main verb: before a feeling, judgment, report, deduction, or another past event. In IELTS writing and speaking, this form helps you show clear time relationships and sound more precise.

Use it after verbs and adjectives such as seem, appear, be said, be believed, be sorry, be happy, and be pleased when the earlier action matters. Compare She seems to be tired now with She seems to have been tired all day. The first talks about now; the second shows an earlier state before now. Also note that must have + past participle is often used for a logical guess about the past, for example They must have left already.

Do not use the simple infinitive if the earlier time is important. I am sorry to keep you waiting suggests a present or ongoing action, but I am sorry to have kept you waiting shows the waiting happened first and the apology comes after it.
explanationVi:
Thể perfect infinitive là to have + past participle, ví dụ to have done, to have finished, to have been. Nó dùng để diễn tả một hành động hoặc trạng thái xảy ra trước thời điểm của động từ chính. Nói cách khác, việc đó đã xảy ra sớm hơn một mốc thời gian khác: trước một cảm xúc, một nhận xét, một lời tường thuật, một suy luận, hoặc một hành động trong quá khứ.

Trong tiếng Anh học thuật và IELTS, cấu trúc này rất hữu ích vì nó giúp bạn diễn đạt quan hệ thời gian chính xác hơn. Ví dụ: She seems to have forgotten her keys nghĩa là “có vẻ như cô ấy đã quên chìa khóa rồi”, và việc quên xảy ra trước lúc người nói đưa ra nhận xét seems. Tương tự, He was happy to have finished the report early nghĩa là “anh ấy vui vì đã hoàn thành báo cáo sớm”, tức là hành động hoàn thành xảy ra trước cảm xúc vui đó.

Một lỗi hay gặp với người Việt là dùng động từ nguyên mẫu đơn giản khi cần nhấn mạnh hành động đã xảy ra trước. Ví dụ, I am sorry to keep you waiting nghe tự nhiên hơn khi đang nói về việc gây phiền ngay lúc này, nhưng I am sorry to have kept you waiting đúng hơn khi muốn nói lời xin lỗi về việc đã làm người khác phải đợi trong quá khứ. Ngoài ra, must have + V3 thường dùng để suy đoán về một việc đã xảy ra trong quá khứ, như They must have left already = “chắc họ đã đi rồi”.
formPatterns: seem/appear/be said/be believed + to have + past participle
be sorry/happy/pleased + to have + past participle
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không bắt buộc đổi hình thức động từ để thể hiện “đã xảy ra trước” trong mệnh đề phụ, nên người học dễ dùng to do thay vì to have done. Hãy chú ý ý nghĩa “đã xảy ra trước” khi dịch từ đã, rồi, từng, vừa... sang tiếng Anh trong cấu trúc với seem, appear, be sorry, be happy, be said, be believed.

title: Too and Enough + Infinitive
summary: Excess and sufficiency followed by to plus verb.

commonMistakes.right: The box is too heavy to carry.
commonMistakes.why: Too + adjective + to + verb shows excess, so the action is not possible or practical.
commonMistakes.wrong: The box is enough heavy to carry.

commonMistakes.right: She is old enough to drive.
commonMistakes.why: Enough comes after the adjective and before to + verb. Too means the opposite idea of excess.
commonMistakes.wrong: She is too old to drive.

commonMistakes.right: The soup is too hot to drink now.
commonMistakes.why: Too + adjective + to + verb means there is too much of the quality for the action to happen comfortably or safely.
commonMistakes.wrong: The soup is enough hot to drink now.

commonMistakes.right: He was too tired to finish the homework.
commonMistakes.why: Too cannot be used with enough in this structure. Use too + adjective + to + verb for excess, or adjective + enough + to + verb for sufficiency.
