commonMistakes.why: After many verbs, English uses a reflexive pronoun when the person does the action for their own benefit. Vietnamese often does not use a special pronoun here.
commonMistakes.wrong: She bought her a new phone.

commonMistakes.right: The children taught themselves to swim.
commonMistakes.why: When the subject does the action alone, use a reflexive pronoun, not a simple object pronoun.
commonMistakes.wrong: The children taught them to swim.

commonMistakes.right: Tom and Anna helped each other with the homework.
commonMistakes.why: Use each other for two people giving mutual action. Do not use a reflexive pronoun for this meaning.
commonMistakes.wrong: Tom and Anna helped themselves with the homework.

acceptedAnswers: myself
drills.explanation: Use myself when the subject is I and the same person receives the action.
drills.prompt: I taught ______ to cook pasta.
drills.target: myself

acceptedAnswers: herself
drills.explanation: Herself refers back to she.
drills.prompt: She looked at ______ in the mirror.
drills.target: herself

acceptedAnswers: themselves
drills.explanation: Themselves is the reflexive pronoun for they.
drills.prompt: They enjoyed ______ at the party.
drills.target: themselves

acceptedAnswers: We prepared ourselves for the exam.
choices: We prepared ourself for the exam.
We prepared ourselves for the exam.
We prepared themself for the exam.
drills.explanation: The subject we needs the reflexive pronoun ourselves. Ourself and themself are wrong here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: We prepared ourselves for the exam.

acceptedAnswers: He blamed himself for the mistake.
choices: He blamed himself for the mistake.
He blamed him for the mistake.
He blamed his for the mistake.
drills.explanation: Himself is needed because the subject and object are the same person.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He blamed himself for the mistake.

acceptedAnswers: The baby hurt itself.
choices: The baby hurt himself.
The baby hurt itself.
The baby hurt themselves.
drills.explanation: For an animal or baby when sex is unknown or not relevant, itself is the safe reflexive form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The baby hurt itself.

acceptedAnswers: My sister washed herself before dinner.
My sister washed herself before dinner
drills.explanation: A reflexive pronoun is needed because my sister did the washing for her own body.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using a reflexive pronoun: My sister washed my sister before dinner.
drills.target: My sister washed herself before dinner.

acceptedAnswers: The children dressed themselves for the photo.
The children dressed themselves for the photo
drills.explanation: The subject and object are the same, so themselves is correct.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The children dressed them for the photo.
drills.target: The children dressed themselves for the photo.

acceptedAnswers: They taught themselves English.
They taught themselves English
drills.explanation: When people learn without help, themselves shows that they did it on their own.
drills.prompt: Build a sentence: they / taught / English / themselves
drills.target: They taught themselves English.

acceptedAnswers: by
drills.explanation: The phrase by yourself means alone or without help.
drills.prompt: She lives ______ herself in a small flat.
drills.target: by

acceptedAnswers: Please help yourself to some tea.
choices: Please help you to some tea.
Please help yourself to some tea.
Please help himself to some tea.
drills.explanation: Help yourself is the natural fixed expression meaning take what you want.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Please help yourself to some tea.

acceptedAnswers: Each other
drills.explanation: Each other is used for two people or things acting on one another.
drills.prompt: Tom and Mai are talking to ______ after the meeting.
drills.target: Each other

acceptedAnswers: They looked at themselves in the photo.
choices: They looked at each other in the photo.
They looked at themselves in the photo.
They looked at them in the photo.
drills.explanation: The picture shows the group looking at their own image, so themselves is correct. Each other would mean mutual looking at different people.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: They looked at themselves in the photo.

acceptedAnswers: I made myself a sandwich.
choices: I made me a sandwich.
I made myself a sandwich.
I made my sandwich.
drills.explanation: Myself is needed because the action is for the speaker’s own benefit.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I made myself a sandwich.

explanation: Reflexive pronouns refer back to the subject of the same clause: I → myself, you → yourself/yourselves, he → himself, she → herself, it → itself, we → ourselves, they → themselves. Use them when the subject and object are the same person or thing, or when you mean “alone” in phrases like by yourself and on your own. Use each other for two people or things doing something to one another. Do not use a reflexive pronoun when a normal object pronoun is needed, and do not use it just because Vietnamese often leaves this relationship unstated.
explanationVi: Trong tiếng Anh, đại từ phản thân dùng để chỉ lại chính chủ ngữ của câu hoặc mệnh đề: I → myself, you → yourself/yourselves, he → himself, she → herself, it → itself, we → ourselves, they → themselves. Khi chủ ngữ và tân ngữ là cùng một người/vật, tiếng Anh thường phải dùng đại từ phản thân: I hurt myself, She taught herself English. Tiếng Việt thường không có một hình thức riêng tương đương như vậy, nên người học hay bỏ sót hoặc dùng nhầm me, him, her, them. Ngoài ra, by yourself, on your own còn mang nghĩa “một mình, tự mình, không có ai giúp”. Còn each other dùng cho hai người hoặc hai vật tác động qua lại lẫn nhau. Không dùng each other để thay cho đại từ phản thân. Cũng không dùng reflexive pronoun chỉ vì trong tiếng Việt ý đó được hiểu ngầm.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt không có hệ thống đại từ phản thân tách biệt như tiếng Anh; quan hệ chủ ngữ–tân ngữ và ý ‘tự mình’ thường được diễn đạt bằng ngữ cảnh hoặc cấu trúc khác, nên người học dễ bỏ mất myself/yourself/himself... hoặc dùng sai me/him/her/them.

title: Indefinite Pronouns
summary: Someone, anything, nobody, and the singular verb they take.

commonMistakes.right: Someone is calling you.
commonMistakes.why: Indefinite pronouns like someone, somebody, anyone, anybody, nobody, and everyone are usually singular, so they take a singular verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: Someone are calling you.

commonMistakes.right: Anything is possible.
commonMistakes.why: Anything is singular here, so the verb must be is, not are.
commonMistakes.wrong: Anything are possible.

commonMistakes.right: Nobody knows the answer.
commonMistakes.why: Nobody is singular, so the verb must be knows, not know.
commonMistakes.wrong: Nobody know the answer.

commonMistakes.right: Everyone has finished the test.
commonMistakes.why: Everyone is singular, so it takes has, not have.
commonMistakes.wrong: Everyone have finished the test.

acceptedAnswers: someone
drills.explanation: Someone is an indefinite pronoun for one unknown person. It usually takes a singular verb.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: _____ is waiting outside.
drills.target: someone

acceptedAnswers: anything
drills.explanation: Anything refers to an unspecified thing, and it is singular in this sentence.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: _____ is possible if you work hard.
drills.target: anything

acceptedAnswers: Nobody knows the answer.
choices: Nobody know the answer.
Nobody knows the answer.
Nobody are knowing the answer.
drills.explanation: Nobody is singular, so the verb must be knows.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Nobody knows the answer.

acceptedAnswers: Everyone is ready.
choices: Everyone are ready.
Everyone is ready.
Everyone be ready.
drills.explanation: Everyone is singular, so it takes is.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Everyone is ready.

acceptedAnswers: Somebody has taken my phone.
choices: Somebody have taken my phone.
Somebody has taken my phone.
Somebody take my phone.
drills.explanation: Somebody is singular, so the verb must be has.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Somebody has taken my phone.

acceptedAnswers: Anybody can answer this question.
choices: Anybody can answer this question.
Anybody can answers this question.
Anybody are able to answer this question.
drills.explanation: Anybody is singular in form, so it takes can or another singular verb form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Anybody can answer this question.

acceptedAnswers: Nobody is home.
drills.explanation: Nobody is singular, so it takes is.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence correctly: Nobody are home.
drills.target: Nobody is home.

acceptedAnswers: Someone has left their umbrella.
drills.explanation: Someone is singular, so has is correct. Their is often used for a person whose gender is unknown or not important.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence correctly: Someone have left their umbrella.
drills.target: Someone has left their umbrella.

acceptedAnswers: anything
drills.explanation: Anything is the correct singular indefinite pronoun in this question.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: Do you need _____ else?
drills.target: anything

acceptedAnswers: Nobody wants to go first.
drills.explanation: Nobody is singular, so wants is correct.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence with: nobody / want / go first
drills.target: Nobody wants to go first.

explanation: Indefinite pronouns such as someone, anybody, nobody, and everyone usually refer to one unknown person or thing, so they normally take singular verbs: Someone is here, Nobody knows, Everyone has. In English, this is true even when the meaning feels like “many people” or “all people.” Some forms, like everyone and nobody, always behave as singular in standard grammar. In questions and negatives, words like anything and anybody are also singular in form.
l1Notes: Trong tiếng Việt, danh từ/đại từ không đổi theo số ít số nhiều và động từ cũng không chia theo chủ ngữ, nên người học dễ viết sai kiểu “Someone are” hoặc “Nobody know”. Cần nhớ rằng các đại từ bất định này thường đi với động từ số ít trong tiếng Anh.

title: Dummy It vs There
summary: It is raining against There is a problem. Neither empty subject exists in Vietnamese.

commonMistakes.right: It is raining.
commonMistakes.why: Use dummy it for weather, time, distance, and similar impersonal expressions. We do not say there is raining.
commonMistakes.wrong: There is raining.

commonMistakes.right: It is a problem.
commonMistakes.why: Use dummy it when you describe a situation or condition. There is is for existence, not for a simple description like this.
commonMistakes.wrong: There is a problem.

commonMistakes.right: It is five o'clock.
commonMistakes.why: Use dummy it for time. We do not use there is before a clock time.
commonMistakes.wrong: There is five o'clock.

commonMistakes.right: It is very cold today.
commonMistakes.why: Use dummy it for weather and general conditions. There is is not used to describe the weather.
commonMistakes.wrong: There is very cold today.

acceptedAnswers: It is raining.
choices: There is raining.
It is raining.
There are raining.
drills.explanation: Weather expressions use dummy it. The verb form after it is usually a normal be or another weather verb like raining.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: It is raining.

acceptedAnswers: It is 7 p.m.
drills.explanation: Use dummy it to talk about time. There is is not used before a clock time.
drills.prompt: Write the correct sentence: 7 p.m.
drills.target: It is 7 p.m.

acceptedAnswers: It is cold. There is a problem.
It is cold.
There is a problem.
drills.explanation: Convert each phrase into a correct sentence. The first needs dummy it because it describes a condition. The second uses there is because it presents the existence of a problem.
drills.prompt: Write two correct sentences: cold / a problem
drills.target: It is cold. There is a problem.

acceptedAnswers: There is a book on the table.
choices: It is a book on the table.
There is a book on the table.
It are a book on the table.
drills.explanation: Use there is to introduce the existence of one thing. It is cannot introduce a new object in this way.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: There is a book on the table.

acceptedAnswers: It is dark now.
drills.explanation: Dummy it is used for general conditions such as light, weather, and time. We do not say there is dark now.
drills.prompt: Rewrite with the correct dummy subject: Dark now.
drills.target: It is dark now.

acceptedAnswers: It is 10 kilometres from here to the station.
drills.explanation: Use dummy it for distance. There is is not used to say how far something is.
drills.prompt: Write the correct sentence: 10 kilometres / from here / to the station
drills.target: It is 10 kilometres from here to the station.

acceptedAnswers: There are two students in the room.
choices: There is two students in the room.
There are two students in the room.
It are two students in the room.
drills.explanation: Use there are with plural nouns. It is not used to introduce the number of people or things in a place.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: There are two students in the room.

acceptedAnswers: It is my turn.
drills.explanation: Use dummy it for a situation or event such as turns, time, and weather. There is my turn is not correct English.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: There is my turn.
drills.target: It is my turn.

acceptedAnswers: It is possible to finish today.
drills.explanation: Dummy it can introduce an adjective phrase and infinitive clause. There is is not used for this structure.
drills.prompt: Rewrite with dummy it: possible to finish today
drills.target: It is possible to finish today.

acceptedAnswers: There is a lot of noise outside.
choices: It is a lot of noise outside.
There is a lot of noise outside.
There are a lot of noise outside.
drills.explanation: Use there is to introduce the existence of an uncountable amount or a singular noun phrase. It is does not work here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: There is a lot of noise outside.

acceptedAnswers: It is important to study every day.
drills.explanation: Dummy it is common with impersonal adjectives like important, necessary, and possible. There is is incorrect here.
drills.prompt: Write the correct sentence: important / study every day
drills.target: It is important to study every day.

acceptedAnswers: There is a restaurant near my house.
drills.explanation: Use there is to say that something exists or is present in a place. This is different from dummy it, which does not introduce a new object.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: It is a restaurant near my house.
drills.target: There is a restaurant near my house.

acceptedAnswers: It is easy to learn English. There is a book on the desk.
It is easy to learn English.
There is a book on the desk.
drills.explanation: The first sentence uses dummy it because it describes a general situation. The second sentence uses there is because it introduces a thing in a place.
drills.prompt: Write two correct sentences: easy to learn English / a book on the desk
drills.target: It is easy to learn English. There is a book on the desk.

explanation:
Dummy it is a fake subject used when English needs a subject but there is no real person or thing doing the action. We use it for weather, time, distance, and general conditions: It is raining. It is 8 p.m. It is cold. It is important to study. The important point is that it does not refer to anything. It only fills the subject position.

There is and there are are different. They are used to say that something exists or is in a place: There is a problem. There are two students. In these sentences, there really is a thing or people being introduced. Do not use there is for weather or time, and do not use it when you want to introduce a thing in a place.

For Vietnamese learners, this is difficult because Vietnamese does not have an empty subject like English it or there. You may want to translate directly from Vietnamese and leave the subject out, but English usually requires a subject. So choose it for impersonal descriptions, and choose there is/there are for existence and location.
explanationVi:
Đây là điểm rất dễ nhầm vì tiếng Việt không có chủ ngữ rỗng giống như tiếng Anh. Trong tiếng Anh, phải có chủ ngữ trong câu, nên người học hay dịch trực tiếp từ tiếng Việt và bỏ chủ ngữ, hoặc dùng there is ở mọi nơi.

Dummy it là it “giả”, không chỉ một vật hay người cụ thể. Ta dùng it với thời tiết, thời gian, khoảng cách, và các câu mô tả tình trạng chung: It is raining. It is 7 p.m. It is cold. It is important to study every day. Ở đây it chỉ để lấp vị trí chủ ngữ, không mang nghĩa “nó”.

There is / there are lại dùng để nói có một vật/người nào đó tồn tại hoặc ở một nơi nào đó: There is a problem. There are two students in the room. Đây là cấu trúc giới thiệu sự tồn tại của danh từ. Nó khác với dummy it vì there is/there are không dùng cho thời tiết, thời gian hay các câu mô tả kiểu It is cold.

Cần nhớ rõ: không nói There is raining, There is 7 p.m., hay There is cold. Cũng không nói It is a book on the table khi muốn giới thiệu một đồ vật. Hãy chọn it cho mô tả vô nhân xưng, và chọn there is/there are cho sự tồn tại hoặc sự hiện diện.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không có chủ ngữ hình thức tương đương it/there trong các câu kiểu 'Trời đang mưa', 'Bây giờ là 7 giờ', 'Có một quyển sách trên bàn'. Vì vậy người học hay bỏ chủ ngữ hoặc dùng there is cho mọi trường hợp. Trong tiếng Anh, hãy nhớ: thời tiết, giờ giấc, khoảng cách, trạng thái chung dùng it; còn có cái gì đó tồn tại/ở đâu đó mới dùng there is/there are.

title: One and Ones
summary: Avoiding repetition with the red one and the small ones.

commonMistakes.right: I want the red one, not the blue one.
commonMistakes.why: Use one/ones to replace a countable noun after an adjective, so you do not repeat the noun.
commonMistakes.wrong: I want the red, not the blue.

commonMistakes.right: These shoes are too small. Do you have bigger ones?
commonMistakes.why: Use ones to replace a plural countable noun after an adjective.
commonMistakes.wrong: These shoes are too small. Do you have bigger?

commonMistakes.right: I bought a shirt and two white ones.
commonMistakes.why: Ones can replace plural countable nouns, but one cannot replace a plural noun.
commonMistakes.wrong: I bought a shirt and two white one.

commonMistakes.right: The new model is cheaper than the old one.
commonMistakes.why: Use one to replace a singular countable noun; do not leave the noun out completely.
commonMistakes.wrong: The new model is cheaper than the old.

acceptedAnswers: the red one
drills.explanation: Use one after an adjective to replace a singular countable noun that was mentioned before.
drills.prompt: I like the blue shirt, but I want _____ .
drills.target: the red one

acceptedAnswers: the small ones
drills.explanation: Use ones after an adjective to replace a plural countable noun.
drills.prompt: These shoes are too big. I need _____ .
drills.target: the small ones

acceptedAnswers: The black one is mine.
choices: The black is mine.
The black one is mine.
The black ones is mine.
drills.explanation: One replaces a singular noun such as bag, shirt, or car after an adjective.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The black one is mine.

acceptedAnswers: I want the large ones.
choices: I want the large one.
I want the large ones.
I want the large.
drills.explanation: Ones replaces a plural noun, so the sentence needs ones, not one.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I want the large ones.

acceptedAnswers: This pen is mine, and that one is yours.
drills.explanation: One can point back to a singular noun when the noun is already understood from context.
drills.prompt: Write a full sentence using one to avoid repeating pen: This pen is mine, and ...
drills.target: This pen is mine, and that one is yours.

acceptedAnswers: These are old ones, but those are new ones.
drills.explanation: Ones can replace a repeated plural noun in both parts of a sentence.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence to avoid repeating bags: These are old bags, but those are new bags.
drills.target: These are old ones, but those are new ones.

acceptedAnswers: Which one do you want?
choices: Which do you want?
Which one do you want?
Which ones do you want?
drills.explanation: Use one when asking about a single countable thing and the noun is understood.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Which one do you want?

acceptedAnswers: I need the green ones.
drills.explanation: Ones is used after adjectives to replace a plural noun such as books, shoes, or apples.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: I need the green.
drills.target: I need the green ones.

acceptedAnswers: The smaller one is cheaper.
choices: The smaller is cheaper.
The smaller one is cheaper.
The smaller ones is cheaper.
drills.explanation: When the noun is singular, use one after the adjective phrase to replace it.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The smaller one is cheaper.

acceptedAnswers: Do you prefer the short ones or the long ones?
drills.explanation: Use ones after each adjective because both nouns are plural and the noun is repeated.
drills.prompt: Write a full sentence using ones to avoid repeating ties: Do you prefer the short ...
drills.target: Do you prefer the short ones or the long ones?

explanation: One and ones are used to avoid repeating countable nouns. Use one for singular nouns and ones for plural nouns, usually after an adjective or after words like this, that, these, those, or which. Do not use one/ones for uncountable nouns; in that case, English usually repeats the noun or uses another phrase.
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường lặp lại danh từ nhiều lần hoặc lược bỏ quá nhiều, nên người học dễ bỏ quên one/ones sau tính từ: the red one, the small ones.

title: Subject-Verb Agreement
summary: Making the verb match its subject. One of the four grammar systems Vietnamese does not mark at all.

commonMistakes.right: She works in a bank.
commonMistakes.why: In the present simple, a singular third-person subject usually takes -s on the verb. Vietnamese does not change the verb form for subject agreement, so learners often forget this.
commonMistakes.wrong: She work in a bank.

commonMistakes.right: They live near my house.
commonMistakes.why: A plural subject takes the base verb form in the present simple. Vietnamese does not mark number on the verb, so learners may add -s by mistake.
commonMistakes.wrong: They lives near my house.

commonMistakes.right: My brother is very tall.
commonMistakes.why: The verb be must agree with a singular subject: is with he, she, it, or one person/thing. Vietnamese learners often use one verb form for all subjects.
commonMistakes.wrong: My brother are very tall.

commonMistakes.right: The students are ready.
commonMistakes.why: The verb be must agree with a plural subject: are with we, you, they, or plural nouns. Vietnamese does not change the verb for number agreement.
commonMistakes.wrong: The students is ready.

acceptedAnswers: She works in a bank.
choices: She work in a bank.
She works in a bank.
She working in a bank.
drills.explanation: She is a singular third-person subject, so the present simple verb takes -s: works.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She works in a bank.

acceptedAnswers: They live near my house.
choices: They lives near my house.
They live near my house.
They living near my house.
drills.explanation: They is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: live.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: They live near my house.

acceptedAnswers: My brother is very tall.
choices: My brother are very tall.
My brother is very tall.
My brother am very tall.
drills.explanation: My brother is singular, so the correct form of be is is.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: My brother is very tall.

acceptedAnswers: The students are ready.
choices: The students is ready.
The students are ready.
The students am ready.
drills.explanation: The students is plural, so the correct form of be is are.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The students are ready.

acceptedAnswers: does
drills.explanation: With he, she, or it in the present simple, the auxiliary do becomes does.
drills.prompt: She ___ not like spicy food.
drills.target: does

acceptedAnswers: do
drills.explanation: With I, you, we, or they in the present simple, the auxiliary is do.
drills.prompt: They ___ not want any help.
drills.target: do

acceptedAnswers: has
drills.explanation: The singular subject Tom needs has, not have.
drills.prompt: Tom ___ a new phone.
drills.target: has

acceptedAnswers: have
drills.explanation: The plural subject my parents needs have, not has.
drills.prompt: My parents ___ two cars.
drills.target: have

acceptedAnswers: The cat sleeps on the sofa.
drills.explanation: The subject The cat is singular, so the verb needs -s: sleeps.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence. Use: The cat / sleep / on the sofa.
drills.target: The cat sleeps on the sofa.

acceptedAnswers: The teachers are in the classroom.
drills.explanation: The subject The teachers is plural, so use are.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence. Use: The teachers / be / in the classroom.
drills.target: The teachers are in the classroom.

acceptedAnswers: He studies English every day.
drills.explanation: He is singular, so the verb in the present simple takes -s: studies.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement: He study English every day.
drills.target: He studies English every day.

acceptedAnswers: The baby cries at night.
drills.explanation: The baby is singular, so the present simple verb needs -s: cries.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: The baby crys at night.
drills.target: The baby cries at night.

acceptedAnswers: The boys play football after school.
choices: The boys plays football after school.
The boys play football after school.
The boys is play football after school.
drills.explanation: Boys is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: play.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The boys play football after school.

acceptedAnswers: My sister and I are tired.
drills.explanation: My sister and I is a compound subject, so the verb is plural: are.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence. Use: My sister and I / be / tired.
drills.target: My sister and I are tired.

explanation: Subject-verb agreement means the verb must match the subject in number and person. In the present simple, singular third-person subjects usually take -s on the verb, while plural subjects do not. The verb be also changes: am, is, are. This is different from Vietnamese, which does not mark verbs for subject agreement, so English learners often forget -s or choose the wrong form of be.
explanationVi: Trong tiếng Anh, động từ phải hòa hợp với chủ ngữ về số ít/số nhiều và ngôi. Ở thì hiện tại đơn, chủ ngữ số ít ngôi thứ ba như he, she, it, hoặc danh từ số ít thường thêm -s vào động từ: She works, He studies, The baby cries. Nhưng với I, you, we, they và danh từ số nhiều thì không thêm -s: They work, We study. Động từ to be còn đặc biệt hơn: I am, he/she/it is, we/you/they are. Tiếng Việt không chia động từ theo chủ ngữ, nên người học rất dễ quên -s hoặc dùng sai is/are/am. Cần nhớ rõ: đây là ngữ pháp của tiếng Anh hiện tại đơn, khác với tiếng Việt, nơi động từ không đổi theo chủ ngữ.
formPatterns: Singular third-person subject + present simple verb + -s/es
I am, he/she/it is, we/you/they are
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt không biến đổi động từ theo chủ ngữ, nên người học hay bỏ quên -s/es với ngôi thứ ba số ít hoặc dùng sai am/is/are.

title: Be About To
summary: Imminent future with be about to and be on the point of.

commonMistakes.right: The train is about to leave.
commonMistakes.why: Be about to means something will happen very soon. Use the base verb after to, not an -ing form.
commonMistakes.wrong: The train is about leaving.

commonMistakes.right: I was about to call you when you phoned.
commonMistakes.why: Use was/were about to for a past moment right before another event. About to does not take the present participle.
commonMistakes.wrong: I was about calling you when you phoned.

commonMistakes.right: She is on the point of crying.
commonMistakes.why: Be on the point of is a fixed phrase meaning something is about to happen, especially with actions or reactions. It is followed by a noun or an -ing form.
commonMistakes.wrong: She is on the point to cry.

commonMistakes.right: We are about to start.
commonMistakes.why: Be about to is followed by the base form of the verb. Do not put to after start in this structure.
commonMistakes.wrong: We are about to to start.

acceptedAnswers: The meeting is about to begin.
choices: The meeting is about to begin.
The meeting is about begin.
The meeting about to begins.
drills.explanation: Be about to is used for something that will happen very soon, and the verb after to is in the base form.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The meeting is about to begin.

acceptedAnswers: She was about to leave when I arrived.
drills.explanation: Was about to shows that the action was imminent in the past. The verb after to stays in the base form.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence: she / be about to / leave / when I arrived
drills.target: She was about to leave when I arrived.

acceptedAnswers: about to
drills.explanation: The fixed pattern is be about to + base verb.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: He is ______ call the doctor.
drills.target: about to

acceptedAnswers: They are about to announce the results.
drills.explanation: This structure describes an event that is going to happen very soon. The verb after to is announce, not announcing or announced.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using be about to: They will announce the results very soon.
drills.target: They are about to announce the results.

acceptedAnswers: I was about to eat dinner when the phone rang.
choices: I was about to eat dinner when the phone rang.
I was about eat dinner when the phone rang.
I was about to eating dinner when the phone rang.
drills.explanation: The correct form is was about to + base verb. The other options break the structure.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I was about to eat dinner when the phone rang.

acceptedAnswers: is about to
drills.explanation: In the present, the structure is am/is/are about to + base verb.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: The show ______ start.
drills.target: is about to

acceptedAnswers: We are on the point of leaving.
drills.explanation: Be on the point of is followed by a noun or an -ing form. Here, leaving is correct.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using be on the point of: We are just about to leave.
drills.target: We are on the point of leaving.

acceptedAnswers: The storm is on the point of breaking.
choices: The storm is on the point to break.
The storm is on the point of breaking.
The storm is about of breaking.
drills.explanation: Be on the point of is a fixed phrase. It is followed by an -ing form here, not to break.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The storm is on the point of breaking.

acceptedAnswers: The team is about to score.
drills.explanation: This is a full sentence with be about to. It means the team will score very soon.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence: the team / be about to / score
drills.target: The team is about to score.

examples.en: The bus is about to arrive.

explanation: Be about to describes something that is going to happen very soon. It is followed by the base form of the verb: is about to leave, was about to call. In the past, was/were about to shows that something was imminent before another event happened.
formPatterns: be on the point of + noun / -ing form
l1Notes: Người học Việt Nam có thể dùng sai dạng động từ sau about to, như thêm -ing hoặc thêm to lần nữa. Nhớ rằng about to luôn đi với động từ nguyên mẫu: is about to leave, was about to call.

title: Be Able To
summary: Ability in the tenses where can is impossible, such as after will or have.

commonMistakes.right: I will be able to finish the report tomorrow.
commonMistakes.why: After will, use be able to, not can. Can does not normally express future ability.
commonMistakes.wrong: I will can finish the report tomorrow.

commonMistakes.right: She was able to solve the problem after a long time.
commonMistakes.why: After was/were, use be able to for a specific past success. Can does not have a past form in this structure.
commonMistakes.wrong: She was can solve the problem after a long time.

commonMistakes.right: I have been able to drive since I was eighteen.
commonMistakes.why: After have/has/had, use be able to for ability over a time period. Can cannot follow have in this way.
commonMistakes.wrong: I have can drive since I was eighteen.

commonMistakes.right: He wants to be able to speak English fluently.
commonMistakes.why: After to, use be able to. Can cannot be used as an infinitive in this structure.
commonMistakes.wrong: He wants to can speak English fluently.

acceptedAnswers: I will be able to call you later.
choices: I will can call you later.
I will be able to call you later.
I can will call you later.
drills.explanation: Use be able to after will. Can is not used for future ability in this structure.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I will be able to call you later.

acceptedAnswers: She was able to finish the test on time.
drills.explanation: Use was able to for a successful action in the past. Can does not fit after was.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence about a past success: she / finish the test on time
drills.target: She was able to finish the test on time.

acceptedAnswers: able to
drills.explanation: After be, use able to. This is the form needed with many tenses where can is impossible.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I am ____ speak to the manager now.
drills.target: able to

acceptedAnswers: I have been able to swim since I was a child.
drills.explanation: Have been able to shows ability over a period of time. Can cannot be used after have in this meaning.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using be able to: I can swim since I was a child.
drills.target: I have been able to swim since I was a child.

acceptedAnswers: He wants to be able to drive at night.
choices: He wants to can drive at night.
He wants to be able to drive at night.
He wants can drive at night.
drills.explanation: After to, use be able to. Can cannot be used as an infinitive.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He wants to be able to drive at night.

acceptedAnswers: Was she able to hear the teacher clearly?
drills.explanation: In questions about a past successful ability, use was/were able to.
drills.prompt: Write a question about past ability: she / hear the teacher clearly
drills.target: Was she able to hear the teacher clearly?

acceptedAnswers: He is not able to join us today.
choices: He is not can join us today.
He is not able to join us today.
He is able not to join us today.
drills.explanation: Use not able to, not can, after be in this structure. The negative goes before able.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He is not able to join us today.

acceptedAnswers: When I get a job, I will be able to save money.
drills.explanation: This sentence needs future ability after will. Be able to is correct; can is not.
drills.prompt: Rewrite with be able to: When I get a job, I can save money.
drills.target: When I get a job, I will be able to save money.

acceptedAnswers: She has been able to speak French for three years.
drills.explanation: Has been able to is correct for an ability that continues up to now. Can is not used after has.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence: she / speak French / for three years
drills.target: She has been able to speak French for three years.

explanation: Be able to is the grammar form for ability when can cannot be used, especially after will, have, to, or in perfect tenses. Use can for present ability in simple sentences, but use be able to for future ability, past successful ability, and patterns like want to be able to or have been able to.
formPatterns: want/need/hope/intend to be able to + verb
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường dùng một mẫu tương tự cho cả khả năng hiện tại, quá khứ và tương lai, nên người học dễ dùng can sau will hoặc have. Cần nhớ can không có dạng sau will/have/to; phải đổi sang be able to.

minimalPairs.meaning: General present ability. Can is the natural choice in simple present.
minimalPairs.sentence: I can speak English.

minimalPairs.meaning: Future ability. Be able to is needed because can does not normally follow will.
minimalPairs.sentence: I will be able to speak English next year.

minimalPairs.meaning: A successful ability in a specific past situation.
minimalPairs.sentence: She was able to find a taxi.

minimalPairs.meaning: A general past ability, especially with habits or repeated actions. Could is often used here, not one successful action.
minimalPairs.sentence: She could swim when she was five.

title: Be Used To and Get Used To
summary: Familiarity with a situation, against used to for a past habit. A persistent three-way confusion.

commonMistakes.right: I am used to the noise now.
commonMistakes.why: be used to means 'be familiar with' or 'be accustomed to'. After be used to, use a noun, pronoun, or gerund (-ing form), not the base verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: I am used to hear the noise now.

commonMistakes.right: She got used to living in London quickly.
commonMistakes.why: get used to means 'become familiar with' or 'become accustomed to'. After get used to, use a noun, pronoun, or gerund (-ing form), not the base verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: She got used to live in London quickly.

commonMistakes.right: He used to smoke every day, but he stopped years ago.
commonMistakes.why: used to talks about a past habit or state that is no longer true. It does not mean 'be familiar with' or 'become familiar with'.
commonMistakes.wrong: He used to smoking every day, but he stopped years ago.

commonMistakes.right: I am used to driving on the left.
commonMistakes.why: be used to is followed by a noun or gerund. A base verb after to is not correct in this structure.
commonMistakes.wrong: I am used to drive on the left.

acceptedAnswers: I am used to waking up early.
drills.explanation: be used to means 'be familiar with'. After to, use the gerund waking.
drills.prompt: Build a correct sentence with: I / be used to / wake up early.
drills.target: I am used to waking up early.

acceptedAnswers: She got used to the new timetable.
drills.explanation: get used to means 'become familiar with'. The object here is the noun phrase the new timetable.
drills.prompt: Build a correct sentence with: She / get used to / the new timetable.
drills.target: She got used to the new timetable.

acceptedAnswers: He used to play football every weekend.
drills.explanation: used to describes a past habit that is no longer true.
drills.prompt: Build a correct sentence with: He / used to / play football every weekend.
drills.target: He used to play football every weekend.

acceptedAnswers: I am used to the noise.
choices: I am used to the noise.
I am used to the noise yesterday.
I used to the noise.
I am use to the noise.
drills.explanation: be used to means 'be accustomed to'. The correct structure is be used to + noun or gerund.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I am used to the noise.

acceptedAnswers: They will get used to working at night.
drills.explanation: get used to can be used in the future. Working is the correct gerund after used to.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using get used to: They will become familiar with working at night.
drills.target: They will get used to working at night.

acceptedAnswers: I am not used to spicy food.
drills.explanation: The negative form is be not used to + noun or gerund. This means the speaker is not familiar with spicy food.
drills.prompt: Build a correct negative sentence: I / not be used to / spicy food.
drills.target: I am not used to spicy food.

acceptedAnswers: She is used to taking the bus every day.
choices: She is used to take the bus every day.
She is used to taking the bus every day.
She used to taking the bus every day.
She is use to taking the bus every day.
drills.explanation: After be used to, the verb must be in gerund form. Taking is correct here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She is used to taking the bus every day.

acceptedAnswers: We got used to the cold weather.
drills.explanation: get used to shows the change from unfamiliar to familiar. The past tense got fits a completed adjustment.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: We got use to the cold weather.
drills.target: We got used to the cold weather.

acceptedAnswers: used to
drills.explanation: used to refers to a past habit or past state that is no longer true. It is not the same as be used to, which means 'be familiar with'.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I ______ live in Hanoi when I was a child.
drills.target: used to

acceptedAnswers: be used to
drills.explanation: be used to means 'be familiar with' or 'be accustomed to'. It is followed by a noun or gerund, not a base verb.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: I am ______ the traffic here.
drills.target: be used to

acceptedAnswers: get used to
drills.explanation: get used to means 'become familiar with' or 'become accustomed to'.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: It takes time to ______ a new work schedule.
drills.target: get used to

acceptedAnswers: I used to work late every night.
choices: I used to work late every night.
I am used to work late every night.
I got used to work late every night.
I use to work late every night.
drills.explanation: Only used to is correct for a past habit. The other options use the wrong form after to or the wrong tense.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I used to work late every night.

acceptedAnswers: She got used to getting up early.
She is used to getting up early.
drills.explanation: Both sentences are correct, but they mean different things. got used to means she became familiar with the new routine; is used to means she is now familiar with it.
drills.prompt: Write two correct sentences that contrast these meanings: becoming familiar with early rising; now familiar with early rising. Use she / get used to / get up early.
drills.target: She got used to getting up early.

explanation: be used to means 'be familiar with' or 'be accustomed to'. get used to means 'become familiar with' or 'become accustomed to'. used to is different: it describes a past habit or past state that is no longer true. After be used to and get used to, use a noun, pronoun, or gerund (-ing form), not a base verb. This contrast is important for IELTS because Vietnamese learners often mix up quen với, quen dần với, and đã từng.
explanationVi: Cụm be used to có nghĩa là “quen với / đã quen với”, nói về trạng thái hiện tại: điều gì đó không còn lạ nữa. Cụm get used to có nghĩa là “dần quen với”, nhấn mạnh quá trình trở nên quen. Còn used to là cấu trúc khác hẳn: nó nói về thói quen hoặc trạng thái trong quá khứ nhưng bây giờ không còn nữa. Vì vậy, used to + V nguyên mẫu là nói về quá khứ, còn be/get used to phải theo sau bằng danh từ hoặc V-ing. Đây là lỗi rất hay gặp với người Việt vì trong tiếng Việt “quen”, “đã quen”, “dần quen”, và “đã từng” dễ bị lẫn vào nhau.
formPatterns: negative: be not used to + noun/gerund
l1Notes: Người học Việt Nam thường nhầm giữa “quen với” (be used to), “dần quen với” (get used to), và “đã từng / thường xuyên trong quá khứ” (used to). Một lỗi rất phổ biến là dùng động từ nguyên mẫu sau to, như trong *I am used to hear...* thay vì *I am used to hearing...*.

minimalPairs.meaning: She became familiar with the new job after some time.
minimalPairs.sentence: She got used to the new job.

minimalPairs.meaning: She is now familiar with the new job.
minimalPairs.sentence: She is used to the new job.

minimalPairs.meaning: I had this habit in the past, but I do not now.
minimalPairs.sentence: I used to wake up at 5 a.m.

minimalPairs.meaning: I am familiar with waking up at 5 a.m. now.
minimalPairs.sentence: I am used to waking up at 5 a.m.

title: Modals of Regret and Criticism
summary: Should have and could have done, for what did not happen but ought to have.

commonMistakes.right: You should have called me yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: should have + past participle is used to criticise a past action that did not happen or was done badly.
commonMistakes.wrong: You should call me yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: We could have finished the report last night, but we left early.
commonMistakes.why: could have + past participle shows a past possibility that was possible but did not happen.
commonMistakes.wrong: We could finish the report last night, but we left early.

commonMistakes.right: She should have taken an umbrella because it rained heavily.
commonMistakes.why: After should have, English uses a past participle, not the base form of the verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: She should have take an umbrella because it rained heavily.

commonMistakes.right: I could have helped you, but you never asked.
commonMistakes.why: Could have + past participle is needed for a missed past ability or opportunity.
commonMistakes.wrong: I could help you, but you never asked.

acceptedAnswers: should have
drills.explanation: Use should have + past participle to criticise a past action or say something was the right thing to do but did not happen.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct modal phrase: You _______ told me earlier.
drills.target: should have

acceptedAnswers: could have
drills.explanation: Use could have + past participle to show a past possibility or ability that existed but was not used.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct modal phrase: They _______ won the match if they had played better.
drills.target: could have

acceptedAnswers: You should have studied harder for the exam.
drills.explanation: This sentence criticises a past decision. Should have is followed by the past participle studied.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence to criticise a past choice: study harder / for the exam / you / should have
drills.target: You should have studied harder for the exam.

acceptedAnswers: I could have sent the email earlier, but I forgot.
drills.explanation: Could have + past participle shows a missed opportunity in the past.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so it shows a missed past opportunity: I was able to send the email earlier, but I forgot.
drills.target: I could have sent the email earlier, but I forgot.

acceptedAnswers: She should have been more careful with the money.
drills.explanation: Should have can criticise a past action or behaviour. The verb after have must be in the past participle form, here been.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: She should be more careful with the money.
drills.target: She should have been more careful with the money.

acceptedAnswers: He should have left earlier.
Choose the correct sentence.
choices: He should have to leave earlier.
He should have left earlier.
He should left earlier.
drills.explanation: Should have is followed by the past participle left. The other options are ungrammatical.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He should have left earlier.

acceptedAnswers: You could have asked for help.
drills.explanation: Could have + past participle is used for a past possibility that was available but not taken.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence: ask for help / you / could have
drills.target: You could have asked for help.

acceptedAnswers: We should have seen the doctor sooner.
drills.explanation: This is a natural criticism of a past decision. Seen is the past participle after should have.
drills.prompt: Rewrite using should have: We did not see the doctor sooner, and that was the wrong decision.
drills.target: We should have seen the doctor sooner.

acceptedAnswers: They could have stayed at home because the storm was dangerous.
drills.explanation: Could have shows a past option that was possible. The sentence explains that staying at home was possible but did not happen.
drills.prompt: Write a sentence about a missed safe option: stay at home / they / could have / because the storm was dangerous
drills.target: They could have stayed at home because the storm was dangerous.

acceptedAnswers: You should have told the truth.
drills.explanation: Should have + past participle is the standard form for regret or criticism about a past action.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: You should told the truth.
drills.target: You should have told the truth.

explanation: Modals of regret and criticism are used to talk about a past action that did not happen, or happened badly, and to say what was the right thing to do. The most common form is should have + past participle, for example You should have studied harder. It often sounds like criticism, advice after the event, or regret about a past choice. Could have + past participle is different: it means something was possible or available in the past, but it did not happen, for example We could have won the match. Do not use the base verb after should have or could have. After these forms, English needs the past participle: gone, done, seen, told, left, studied.
explanationVi: Cấu trúc modal of regret and criticism dùng để nói về một việc trong quá khứ lẽ ra nên làm nhưng đã không làm, hoặc một việc đáng lẽ có thể xảy ra nhưng không xảy ra. Dạng phổ biến nhất là should have + past participle, ví dụ You should have studied harder. Câu này thường mang sắc thái trách móc, phê bình nhẹ, hoặc hối tiếc sau khi mọi việc đã xảy ra. Could have + past participle thì khác: nó nói về một khả năng trong quá khứ, tức là việc đó đã có thể xảy ra nhưng thực tế không xảy ra, ví dụ We could have won the match. Sau should have và could have, tiếng Anh phải dùng past participle chứ không dùng động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ đúng là should have told, could have gone, should have been, chứ không phải should tell hay could go.
formPatterns: criticise a past action: You should have + past participle
missed past possibility: We could have + past participle
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt hay bỏ hẳn have sau should/could (ví dụ *You should told me) vì trong tiếng Việt không có một cấu trúc tương đương cố định. Một lỗi khác là dùng động từ nguyên mẫu sau should have/could have thay vì quá khứ phân từ, do ảnh hưởng từ các mẫu như “nên làm”, “có thể làm” trong tiếng Việt.

title: Both, Either, Neither
summary: Two-item reference, and the verb agreement each one forces.

commonMistakes.right: Both of the books are on the table.
commonMistakes.why: Both refers to two things, so the verb is plural. We usually say both of + plural noun or both + plural noun.
commonMistakes.wrong: Both of the books is on the table.

commonMistakes.right: Either of the answers is correct.
commonMistakes.why: Either means one of two, so we use a singular verb in this structure.
commonMistakes.wrong: Either of the answers are correct.

commonMistakes.right: Neither of my parents is at home.
commonMistakes.why: Neither means not one of two, so it takes a singular verb here.
commonMistakes.wrong: Neither of my parents are at home.

commonMistakes.right: Both Anna and Tom were late.
commonMistakes.why: When both and and join two subjects, the verb is plural.
commonMistakes.wrong: Both Anna and Tom was late.

acceptedAnswers: Both
drills.explanation: Both is used for two things or two people together.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: _____ of my sisters live in Hanoi.
drills.target: Both

acceptedAnswers: Either
drills.explanation: Either means one of two choices.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: You can sit on _____ side of the table.
drills.target: Either

acceptedAnswers: Neither
drills.explanation: Neither means not one and not the other of two.
drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: _____ of the two jackets is mine.
drills.target: Neither

acceptedAnswers: Both of the windows are open.
drills.explanation: Both refers to two windows, so the verb is plural: are.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: both / the windows / open
drills.target: Both of the windows are open.

acceptedAnswers: Either of these pens is fine.
drills.explanation: Either means one of two or one of a small set considered as two choices here, and the verb is singular: is.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: either / these pens / fine
drills.target: Either of these pens is fine.

acceptedAnswers: Neither of my brothers is married.
drills.explanation: Neither refers to not one of two, so the verb is singular: is.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: neither / my brothers / married
drills.target: Neither of my brothers is married.

acceptedAnswers: Both of them are tired.
drills.explanation: Both refers to two people, so the verb is plural: are.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using both: The two of them are tired.
drills.target: Both of them are tired.

acceptedAnswers: Either of the answers is acceptable.
choices: Either of the answers are acceptable.
Either of the answers is acceptable.
Both of the answers is acceptable.
drills.explanation: Choose either when one of two options is enough. The verb is singular: is.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Either of the answers is acceptable.

acceptedAnswers: Neither of the rooms is available.
choices: Neither of the rooms are available.
Neither of the rooms is available.
Both of the rooms is available.
drills.explanation: Neither means not one of the two rooms, so the verb is singular: is.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Neither of the rooms is available.

acceptedAnswers: Both of my children are asleep.
choices: Both of my children is asleep.
Both of my children are asleep.
Either of my children are asleep.
drills.explanation: Both refers to two children, so the verb is plural: are.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Both of my children are asleep.

acceptedAnswers: Both Maria and Linh speak English.
drills.explanation: When both joins two subjects with and, the verb is plural: speak.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using both: Maria speaks English and Linh speaks English.
drills.target: Both Maria and Linh speak English.

acceptedAnswers: Neither parent called me.
drills.explanation: Neither can be used before a singular noun, and the noun stays singular: parent.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: neither / parent / called me
drills.target: Neither parent called me.

acceptedAnswers: Both of the teachers were late.
choices: Both of the teachers was late.
Both of the teachers were late.
Either of the teachers were late.
drills.explanation: Both refers to two teachers, so the verb must be plural: were.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: Both of the teachers were late.

acceptedAnswers: Either answer is correct.
drills.explanation: Either can come before a singular noun when you mean one of two options; the noun stays singular.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence with: either / answer / correct
drills.target: Either answer is correct.

explanation: Both, either, and neither all refer to two things, but they are not used the same way. Both means the two together, so it usually matches a plural verb: Both of my friends are here. Either means one of two, so it usually takes a singular verb: Either of the answers is correct. Neither means not one and not the other, and it also usually takes a singular verb: Neither of the options is good. A very common mistake is to make the verb plural after either and neither because the noun after of is plural. In standard English, the verb agrees with the idea of one, not with the plural noun inside the phrase. When both joins two subjects with and, the verb is plural: Both Anna and Tom are late. The noun after neither can be singular: Neither child was hungry. With both, either, and neither, always ask whether the meaning is two together, one of two, or not one of two, then choose the verb form from that meaning, not from the noun that follows.
explanationVi: Both, either và neither đều liên quan đến hai đối tượng, nhưng cách dùng không giống nhau. Both nghĩa là “cả hai”, nên động từ thường chia số nhiều: Both of my friends are here. Either nghĩa là “một trong hai”, nên thường đi với động từ số ít: Either of the answers is correct. Neither nghĩa là “không cái nào trong hai”, và cũng thường đi với động từ số ít: Neither of the options is good. Lỗi rất hay gặp của người Việt là nhìn thấy danh từ phía sau là số nhiều rồi chia động từ số nhiều, ví dụ: Either of the answers are..., Neither of the rooms are.... Trong tiếng Anh chuẩn, động từ phải theo ý nghĩa “một” hoặc “không cái nào”, không theo danh từ số nhiều ở phía sau. Khi both nối hai chủ ngữ bằng and, động từ dùng số nhiều: Both Anna and Tom are late. Neither cũng có thể đi với danh từ số ít: Neither child was hungry. Khi làm bài, hãy xác định ý nghĩa trước: “cả hai”, “một trong hai”, hay “không cái nào trong hai”, rồi chọn động từ theo ý nghĩa đó.
formPatterns: both + plural noun / both of + plural noun + plural verb
either of + plural noun + singular verb
neither of + plural noun + singular verb
both + noun and noun + plural verb
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không bắt buộc chia động từ theo số ít/số nhiều như tiếng Anh, nên người học dễ nhìn danh từ số nhiều sau of và chia động từ số nhiều theo thói quen. Cũng dễ nhầm either/neither với nghĩa “hai cái đều...” thay vì “một trong hai” và “không cái nào trong hai”.

title: All and Whole
summary: All the day against the whole day, and where the article sits.

commonMistakes.right: I stayed there all day.
commonMistakes.why: Use all + day/time word without the article when you mean the full length of the day. In this structure, the article is usually omitted.
commonMistakes.wrong: I stayed there the whole day.

commonMistakes.right: I spent the whole day cleaning the house.
commonMistakes.why: Use the whole + singular noun when you mean the complete unit. Here the article comes before whole, not before day.
commonMistakes.wrong: I spent all day cleaning the house.

commonMistakes.right: All of the students passed the test.
commonMistakes.why: All can be followed by of + determiner + noun, especially with pronouns or specific groups.
commonMistakes.wrong: All the students passed the test.

commonMistakes.right: The whole of the class was late.
commonMistakes.why: Whole can be followed by of + determiner + noun in more formal English.
commonMistakes.wrong: The whole class was late.

acceptedAnswers: all day
drills.explanation: Use all + day to mean the full length of the day. In this structure, you usually do not add the article the.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: I worked from morning to night; I worked ______.
drills.target: all day

acceptedAnswers: the whole day
drills.explanation: Use the whole + singular noun when you mean the complete day. The article the comes before whole.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: I spent ______ waiting for the result.
drills.target: the whole day

acceptedAnswers: I stayed at home all day.
drills.explanation: All day is the natural form when you mean during the entire day. The phrase the whole day is possible in some contexts, but this sentence is best with all day.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using all day: I stayed at home during the entire day.
drills.target: I stayed at home all day.

acceptedAnswers: She studied the whole night.
drills.explanation: The whole + singular noun is used for a complete unit of time. Put the article before whole, not before night.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the whole night: She studied all night.
drills.target: She studied the whole night.

acceptedAnswers: All of the answers are correct.
choices: All of the answers are correct.
All the of answers are correct.
The all answers are correct.
drills.explanation: All of the + noun phrase is correct when you want to emphasize the whole set. The other options place all in the wrong position.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: All of the answers are correct.

acceptedAnswers: the whole class
drills.explanation: Use the whole + singular noun to mean the complete class as one group. The article the goes before whole.
drills.prompt: Complete the phrase: ______ was listening carefully.
drills.target: the whole class

acceptedAnswers: All of my friends live in Hanoi.
drills.explanation: With a possessive determiner like my, all often takes of: all of my friends. This is especially common in written and careful English.
drills.prompt: Write a full sentence about your friends living in Hanoi. Use all of my friends.
drills.target: All of my friends live in Hanoi.

acceptedAnswers: He worked the whole afternoon.
drills.explanation: The whole + singular time noun is correct here. It refers to the complete afternoon, with the article before whole.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: He worked all the afternoon.
drills.target: He worked the whole afternoon.

acceptedAnswers: We waited all year for this moment.
drills.explanation: All year is the usual form for an entire period of time. The article the is not needed here.
drills.prompt: Write a full sentence using all year to say you waited for a long time.
drills.target: We waited all year for this moment.

acceptedAnswers: The whole of the village came to the festival.
choices: The whole of the village came to the festival.
The all of the village came to the festival.
All of the village whole came to the festival.
drills.explanation: Whole can be followed by of + the + noun in this structure. The other options place whole or all incorrectly.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: The whole of the village came to the festival.

explanation: All and whole both mean “complete,” but they are used in different patterns. All is common with time expressions like all day, all night, all year, and it usually comes directly before the time word without the article. Whole is common with singular nouns like the whole day, the whole book, the whole class, and the article the normally goes before whole. All can also be followed by of, especially before pronouns and specific determiner phrases: all of them, all of my friends, all of the students. Whole can also take of in more formal styles: the whole of the country.
formPatterns: all + time word: all day, all night, all week
the whole + singular noun: the whole day, the whole book
all of + pronoun/determiner phrase: all of them, all of my friends
the whole of + determiner + noun: the whole of the class
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt dễ bỏ quên hoặc đặt sai mạo từ the vì tiếng Việt không có mạo từ. Cũng dễ dùng all và whole như từ đồng nghĩa hoàn toàn mà không chú ý mẫu câu đi kèm.

title: Another, Other, The Other
summary: Countability and definiteness across another, other, others, and the other.

commonMistakes.right: I need another pen.
commonMistakes.why: Use another with a singular countable noun when you mean one more of the same kind.
commonMistakes.wrong: I need other pen.

commonMistakes.right: I have two phones, and one is old while the other is new.
commonMistakes.why: Use the other for the second of two specific items.
commonMistakes.wrong: I have two phones, and one is old while another is new.

commonMistakes.right: I bought some apples, but I did not buy any others.
commonMistakes.why: Others is a pronoun that means other ones; it can stand alone.
commonMistakes.wrong: I bought some apples, but I did not buy any other.

commonMistakes.right: Some people stayed outside, while the others went inside.
commonMistakes.why: The others refers to the rest of a known group.
commonMistakes.wrong: Some people stayed outside, while others went inside.

acceptedAnswers: another
drills.explanation: Another is used before a singular countable noun or by itself to mean one more.
drills.prompt: I have one ticket, but I need ______ ticket for my friend.
drills.target: another

acceptedAnswers: the other
drills.explanation: The other is used for the second of two specific things or people.
drills.prompt: There are two doors. One is open, and ______ is closed.
drills.target: the other

acceptedAnswers: others
drills.explanation: Others is a pronoun meaning other people or things, and it can stand alone.
drills.prompt: Some students finished early. ______ stayed to do the extra exercise.
drills.target: others

acceptedAnswers: another apple
drills.explanation: Another means one more of the same kind, so it is followed by a singular countable noun.
drills.prompt: Please give me ______ . I am still hungry.
drills.target: another apple

acceptedAnswers: the other car
drills.explanation: The other shows that there are two cars and you mean the second one.
drills.prompt: My brother owns two cars. He drives one car every day, but he rarely uses ______ .
drills.target: the other car

acceptedAnswers: the others
drills.explanation: The others means the rest of a known group, so the article the is needed.
drills.prompt: Five people joined the meeting. Two left early, and ______ stayed until the end.
drills.target: the others

acceptedAnswers: I need another minute.
choices: I need other minute.
I need another minute.
I need the other minute.
drills.explanation: Another is correct before a singular countable noun. Other cannot be used like this, and the other is not for an unspecified extra item.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I need another minute.

acceptedAnswers: We met some tourists, but the others spoke only Spanish.
choices: We met some tourists, but others spoke only Spanish.
We met some tourists, but the others spoke only Spanish.
We met some tourists, but another spoke only Spanish.
drills.explanation: The others is correct because the speaker means the rest of a known group. Others alone would be incomplete here, and another is singular.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: We met some tourists, but the others spoke only Spanish.

acceptedAnswers: I want another cup of tea.
choices: I want other cup of tea.
I want another cup of tea.
I want the other cup of tea.
drills.explanation: Another is used for one more cup. Other cannot directly modify a singular countable noun here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I want another cup of tea.

acceptedAnswers: one is yours and the other is mine
drills.explanation: The other is the correct way to refer to the second item when there are only two.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so it sounds natural and correct: One is yours and second is mine.
drills.target: one is yours and the other is mine

acceptedAnswers: There are two answers, and the other is correct.
drills.explanation: The other is needed because there are two answers and you mean the second one.
drills.prompt: Correct the sentence: There are two answers, and another is correct.
drills.target: There are two answers, and the other is correct.

acceptedAnswers: Could you bring another chair?
drills.explanation: This is a natural sentence using another before a singular countable noun.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: could you / bring / another / chair
drills.target: Could you bring another chair?

acceptedAnswers: The others were waiting outside.
drills.explanation: The others refers to the rest of a known group, so the sentence needs the definite article.
drills.prompt: Write a correct sentence using: the others / were / waiting / outside
drills.target: The others were waiting outside.

explanation: Another, other, others, and the other all depend on countability and whether the noun or group is definite. Another means one more or an extra one, and it is used with singular countable nouns or as a pronoun: another book, another one, another cup of tea. Other is usually used with plural nouns or uncountable nouns: other people, other ideas, other water in the sense of different water, though this is less common; in practice, plural or uncountable nouns often need other or some other before them. Others is a pronoun meaning other people or things, so it stands alone: Some left, others stayed. The other refers to the second of two, or to the rest of a specific group when it is used with a plural noun: the other car, the other students, the others. Do not use another to mean the second item in a pair, and do not use other directly before a singular countable noun unless it is part of a phrase like the other or some other.
explanationVi:
Another, other, others và the other khác nhau chủ yếu ở hai điểm: danh từ đi kèm có đếm được hay không, và ý nghĩa có xác định hay không. Đây là lỗi rất phổ biến với người Việt vì tiếng Việt không có mạo từ như a, the và cũng không chia số ít/số nhiều bằng hình thức bắt buộc như tiếng Anh.

Another nghĩa là “thêm một”, “một cái nữa”, “một người nữa”, và chỉ đi với danh từ đếm được số ít. Ví dụ: another pen, another day, another chance. Another cũng có thể đứng một mình nếu ngữ cảnh rõ: I need another.

Other thường đi với danh từ số nhiều hoặc danh từ không đếm được, mang nghĩa “những cái/người khác”, “loại khác”. Ví dụ: other people, other ideas, other information. Nhưng other không đi trực tiếp trước danh từ đếm được số ít theo kiểu *other pen. Muốn nói “một cây bút khác”, phải dùng another pen hoặc the other pen nếu đang nói về cái còn lại trong hai cái.

Others là đại từ, không đứng trước danh từ. Nó có nghĩa là “những người khác”, “những cái khác” và có thể đứng một mình. Ví dụ: Some students left, others stayed. Nếu thêm the, ta có the others để nói về “những người/cái còn lại” trong một nhóm đã xác định.

The other dùng khi có đúng hai thứ, hoặc khi nói về phần còn lại của một nhóm cụ thể. Ví dụ: One is mine and the other is yours. Nếu có nhiều hơn hai và bạn muốn nói “những cái còn lại”, dùng the others. Nếu không có the, others chỉ có nghĩa chung chung là “những cái/người khác”, không phải “những cái còn lại đã biết”.

Tóm tắt nhanh: another = một cái nữa; other = khác, thường với số nhiều hoặc không đếm được; others = những cái khác, đứng một mình; the other = cái còn lại trong hai; the others = những cái/người còn lại trong một nhóm đã xác định.
formPatterns: other + plural noun or uncountable noun
the others + remaining members of a known group
l1Notes: Người học tiếng Việt thường bỏ quên a/the và không cảm nhận rõ số ít số nhiều, nên dễ nói sai như other pen thay vì another pen. Cũng dễ nhầm the other với another vì tiếng Việt thường chỉ nói “cái còn lại” mà không phân biệt trong hai hay trong một nhóm lớn. Hãy nhớ: another = thêm một; the other = cái còn lại trong hai; the others = những cái còn lại trong nhóm đã biết; others = những cái khác, đứng một mình.

title: Double-Object Passive
summary: He was given a book against A book was given to him, from a two-object verb.

commonMistakes.right: He was given a book by the teacher.
commonMistakes.why: In the passive of a two-object verb, the recipient can become the subject. The original object can be kept as the object, and the giver is often added with by.
commonMistakes.wrong: A book was given him by the teacher.

commonMistakes.right: A book was given to him by the teacher.
commonMistakes.why: If the book becomes the subject, the recipient is usually introduced with to. The sentence needs to show clearly who received the book.
commonMistakes.wrong: A book was given him by the teacher.

commonMistakes.right: He was sent a message yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: A double-object passive uses the recipient as the subject: he was sent a message. This is correct passive English.
commonMistakes.wrong: He was gave a message yesterday.

commonMistakes.right: She was offered a job last week.
commonMistakes.why: With verbs like offer, give, send, teach, and show, the person receiving the thing can become the passive subject.
commonMistakes.wrong: A job was offered her last week.

acceptedAnswers: He was given a book.
choices: He was given a book.
A book was given to he.
He given a book.
drills.explanation: In the double-object passive, the recipient can become the subject. He was given a book is correct; the other options are ungrammatical.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He was given a book.

acceptedAnswers: A book was given to him.
drills.explanation: When the thing given becomes the subject, the recipient is usually introduced by to. This sentence is the passive form of Someone gave him a book.
drills.prompt: Write the passive sentence from: Someone gave him a book.
drills.target: A book was given to him.

acceptedAnswers: She was sent an email.
drills.explanation: This is the passive form of a two-object verb. The recipient she becomes the subject, and the thing sent stays as an object.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the passive: They sent her an email.
drills.target: She was sent an email.

acceptedAnswers: He was given a book by the teacher.
choices: He was given a book by the teacher.
A book was given to him by the teacher.
A book gave him by the teacher.
drills.explanation: The correct passive can focus on the recipient, he. The first option is correct; the others are not grammatical English.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: He was given a book by the teacher.

acceptedAnswers: A book was given to her.
drills.explanation: This sentence uses the passive with the thing given as subject and the recipient introduced by to. It is a natural and correct alternative to She was given a book.
drills.prompt: Write a passive sentence meaning: someone gave her a book.
drills.target: A book was given to her.

acceptedAnswers: He was offered a job.
drills.explanation: Offer is another two-object verb. In the passive, the recipient becomes the subject and the thing offered stays as an object.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the passive: The company offered him a job.
drills.target: He was offered a job.

acceptedAnswers: She was shown the results.
choices: She was shown the results.
The results were shown her.
She showed the results.
drills.explanation: With show, the person who receives the information can become the subject in the passive. The other options are wrong because they either use the wrong structure or the wrong voice.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: She was shown the results.

acceptedAnswers: They were taught English by Mrs. Lan.
English was taught to them by Mrs. Lan.
drills.explanation: Both passives are correct. You can make the people the subject or make the thing taught the subject, depending on what you want to emphasize.
drills.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the passive: Mrs. Lan taught them English.
drills.target: They were taught English by Mrs. Lan.

acceptedAnswers: She was given a chance.
drills.explanation: A two-object verb can be passivized with the recipient as subject. Here, she is the person receiving the chance.
drills.prompt: Write a passive sentence meaning: someone gave her a chance.
drills.target: She was given a chance.

explanation:
With many two-object verbs such as give, send, offer, show, teach, and tell, English has two passive patterns. You can make the recipient the subject: He was given a book. Or you can make the thing given the subject and keep the recipient with to: A book was given to him.

In the first pattern, the person who receives the thing becomes the grammatical subject. This is very common in English and often sounds natural when the recipient is the focus. In the second pattern, the thing received becomes the subject, and to is usually needed before the recipient.

Not every verb allows both patterns equally well, and style can affect which one sounds better. But with common two-object verbs, both forms are often correct. Avoid dropping to in the second pattern: A book was given him is not standard English.
explanationVi:
Trong tiếng Anh, nhiều động từ có hai tân ngữ như give, send, offer, show, teach, tell có thể chuyển sang thể bị động theo hai cách. Cách 1 là đưa người nhận lên làm chủ ngữ: He was given a book. Cách 2 là đưa vật được cho lên làm chủ ngữ và giữ người nhận sau giới từ to: A book was given to him.

Điểm quan trọng là: khi bạn chọn cách 2, thường phải có to trước người nhận. Vì vậy A book was given him là sai trong tiếng Anh chuẩn. Nhiều người Việt hay bỏ quên to vì trong tiếng Việt cấu trúc tương đương không cần từ tương đương rõ ràng như vậy.

Cũng cần nhớ rằng không phải động từ nào cũng dùng hai kiểu bị động giống nhau, nhưng với các động từ thông dụng như give, send, offer, show, teach, tell thì hai kiểu này đều rất thường gặp. Khi muốn nhấn mạnh người nhận, dùng dạng He was given a book. Khi muốn nhấn mạnh món đồ, dùng dạng A book was given to him.
formPatterns: be + past participle + direct object + to + recipient
recipient + be + past participle + direct object
l1Notes: Tiếng Việt thường không có sự bắt buộc rõ như tiếng Anh giữa 'He was given a book' và 'A book was given to him'. Người học dễ quên thêm 'to' khi đưa vật lên làm chủ ngữ, hoặc dùng nhầm cấu trúc chủ động/câu sai dạng như 'A book was given him'. Cần chú ý rằng với bị động của động từ hai tân ngữ, tiếng Anh thường giữ giới từ 'to' trước người nhận ở kiểu thứ hai.

title: Verb + Object + Infinitive
summary: Want, expect, and persuade someone to do something. A pattern distinct from plain verb + infinitive.

commonMistakes.right: I want you to help me with this report.
commonMistakes.why: After want, expect, persuade, and similar verbs, English uses an object + to-infinitive. Vietnamese often leaves out the object-to pattern or uses a direct infinitive idea.
commonMistakes.wrong: I want you help me with this report.

commonMistakes.right: The manager asked us to arrive early.
commonMistakes.why: Ask also follows object + to-infinitive. The wrong sentence leaves out to, which makes the structure ungrammatical.
commonMistakes.wrong: The manager asked us arrive early.

commonMistakes.right: She persuaded her friend to join the club.
commonMistakes.why: Persuade requires an object and then to + verb. Vietnamese learners often produce a bare infinitive after the object, but English does not allow that here.
commonMistakes.wrong: She persuaded her friend join the club.

commonMistakes.right: We expected them to finish the task today.
commonMistakes.why: Expect takes object + to-infinitive. The wrong sentence is not standard English because the to is missing before the verb.
commonMistakes.wrong: We expected them finish the task today.

acceptedAnswers: I want you to call me tonight.
choices: I want you call me tonight.
I want you to call me tonight.
I want that you call me tonight.
drills.explanation: After want, English uses an object plus to-infinitive: want you to call. The bare verb form is wrong here.
drills.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
drills.target: I want you to call me tonight.

acceptedAnswers: The teacher asked the students to sit down.
